Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of the words of God Most High: ﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ (1) ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ (2)

God Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾ by obeying Him, performing His obligations, fulfilling the rights due to Him from you, refraining from what He has forbidden, and not violating His limits. ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾ who say to you: "Drive away from yourself your followers among the weak believers, so that we may sit with you." ﴿And the hypocrites﴾ who show you faith in God and sincere counsel, while they do not spare you, your companions, or your religion from corruption (khabal). So do not accept their opinion, and do not consult them seeking their advice, for they are your enemies. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ means: Indeed, God has knowledge of what their souls conceal and what they intend by showing you sincere counsel while harboring what they hide within themselves; He is Wise in managing your affair, the affair of your companions and your religion, and in the management of all His creation. ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means: act upon what God sends down to you of His revelation and the verses of His Book. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ means: indeed God is Acquainted (khabir) with what you and your companions do of this Qur'an and of your other affairs and the affairs of His servants, meaning He is one of full knowledge (dhu khibra), nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it with the reward He has promised you.

In accordance with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words, ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾: that is, this Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾.

* *

The interpretation of the words of God Most High: ﴿And rely upon God; and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs﴾ (3)

God Most High says: Entrust your affair to God, O Muhammad, and trust in Him. ﴿And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs﴾ means: God is sufficient for you in what He commands you, as a Guardian and Protector over you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 3–4:

On the interpretation of God's words, ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, the exegetes differed about what is meant by God's words ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the denial, by Him, of a claim made by a group of the hypocrites (munafiqun) who described the Prophet of God (ﷺ) as having two hearts, so God negated that of His Prophet and denied them.

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Nufayl related to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya related to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, that his father told him, saying: We said to Ibn Abbas: Tell us about God's words, ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾: what did He mean by that? He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood one day and prayed, and he made a slip [[khatara khatra: sahā sahwa, he forgot]], and the hypocrites who prayed with him said: He has two hearts, one with you and one with them. So God revealed: ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾.

Others said: rather, it refers to a man from Quraysh who was called "the one with two hearts" because of his intelligence [[al-dahw, al-dahā, al-du'a': intellect]].

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, he said: A man of Quraysh, known for his intelligence, was called "the one with two hearts," so God revealed this concerning him.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, he said: A man from the clan of Fihr said: "Within my body are two hearts; with each of them I understand better than Muhammad's understanding," and he lied.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding God's words: ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾. Qatada said: A man in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was called "the one with two hearts," so God revealed concerning him what you hear.

Qatada said: al-Hasan used to say: A man would say to me: "A soul commands me and a soul forbids me," so God revealed concerning him what you hear.

Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Ikrima, who said: A man was called "the one with two hearts," so ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾ was revealed.

Others said: rather, it refers to Zayd ibn Haritha, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had adopted him, so God struck this as an example.

Those who said this:

al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, regarding God's words: ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, he said: We have been told that this was about Zayd ibn Haritha; He struck for him an example, saying: "The son of another man is not your son."

The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who say: this is God's refutation of the statement of one who says that a man has two hearts within him by which he understands, in the manner transmitted from Ibn Abbas. It is also possible that this is God's refutation of those who described the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with this, and that it is a refutation of those who named the Qurashi who was said to be called "the one with two hearts" for his intelligence. Whichever of the two it was, it is God's negation, concerning His creation of men, that they should possess that attribute.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers﴾

God, mentioned be His remembrance, says: God has not made, O men, your wives, whom you say to: "You are to us like the backs of our mothers," your mothers. Rather, He has made that from you a lie, and has obligated you to a penalty, an expiation (kaffara).

The exegetes said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers﴾: that is, He did not make her your mother; so when a man makes zihar against his wife, God has not made her his mother, but He has placed in it an expiation.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾

He says: God has not made the one whom you claim to be your son, who is the son of another, your son by your claim.

It is mentioned that this was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning his adoption of Zayd ibn Haritha.

Narration reporting this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿your adopted sons﴾, he said: This verse was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Haritha.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾: Zayd ibn Haritha, when God and His Messenger bestowed favor upon him, was called Zayd ibn Muhammad, because he had adopted him. So God said: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. He said: And He mentions the wives and the sister, and informs that the wives are not your mothers, nor your adopted sons your sons.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾: that is, He has not made your adopted one your son. He says: when a man claims another man as a son while he is not his son ﴿That is your saying with your mouths...﴾, the verse. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever claims descent from other than his father, knowingly, God has forbidden him Paradise."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Ash'ath, from Amir, who said: "There is no adoption in the case of Zayd." As for His words: ﴿That is your saying with your mouths﴾, God, mentioned be His remembrance, says: this statement, which is the saying of a man to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," and his claim of one who is not his son to be his son, is only your saying with your mouths, having no reality. The lineage of the one whose sonship is claimed is not established by this claim, nor does the wife become a mother by a man's saying to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother." ﴿And God speaks the truth﴾: that is, God is the truthful One who speaks the truth, and by His word lineage is established for whoever He establishes it for, and by it a woman becomes the mother of a child, when He so rules. ﴿And He guides to the way﴾: God, mentioned be His remembrance, says: God makes clear to His servants the way of truth, and guides them to the path of right direction.

The explanation of the words of God, may He be exalted: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, but [blame lies in] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (5)

God, may He be remembered, says: Attribute your adopted sons, whose lineages you have joined to yours, to their fathers. He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Attribute the lineage of Zayd to his father Haritha, and do not call him Zayd ibn Muhammad.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is more just in the sight of God﴾

He says: Your calling them by [the names of] their fathers is more just, more truthful and more correct in the sight of God than your calling them by other than their fathers and attributing them to the one who adopted and claimed them, when they are not his sons.

As [reported]:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God﴾: that is, more equitable in the sight of God. And His saying: ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾: He, may He be remembered, says: If you, O people, do not know the fathers of your adopted sons, who they are, so that you may attribute them to them, and you do not recognize them so that you may join them to them, ﴿then they are your brothers in religion﴾, that is: they are your brothers in religion if they are of your community, ﴿and your clients﴾ if they are your freed slaves and not your sons.

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] have said in agreement with what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God﴾: that is, more equitable in the sight of God. ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾: if you do not know whose father he is, then he is simply your brother and your client.

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Uyayna ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Abu Bakra said: God said: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾. I am among those whose father is not known, and I am among your brothers in religion. He said: My father said: By God, I think that if he had known that his father was a donkey driver, he would still have claimed him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred﴾

He says: There is no sin or blame upon you for an error you commit in attributing some person to a father, when you think he is the son of the one to whom they attribute him, while he is in fact the son of someone else. ﴿But [blame lies in] what your hearts intended﴾: that is, the sin and blame upon you lie in attributing him to other than his father when you know that he is the son of other than the one to whom you attribute him.

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] have said in agreement with what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred﴾: that is, if you call a man by other than his father while you think that he is so. ﴿But [blame lies in] what your hearts intended﴾: God says: Do not call him by other than his father deliberately. As for error, God does not hold you accountable for it. ﴿But He holds you accountable for what your hearts intended﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿what your hearts intended﴾, who said: Intention is what occurs after clarification and prohibition, in this matter and others. The "ma" in His saying ﴿but [blame lies in] what your hearts intended﴾ is in the genitive case, in agreement with the "ma" in His saying ﴿for that in which you have erred﴾. This is because the meaning of the statement is: There is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, but [there is blame] for that which your hearts have intended.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: God is ever one who conceals the sin of the one who likens his wife to his mother, speaks falsehood and lying words, and who censures the one who claims another's child as his own son, once they repent, return to the command of God, and desist from speaking falsehood after their Lord has forbidden it to them. He is merciful to them, so that He does not punish them for that after their repentance from their sin.

The Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you show kindness to your close friends. That is written in the Book.﴾ (6)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿The Prophet﴾, Muhammad, ﴿is closer to the believers﴾, meaning: more entitled over the believers, ﴿than their own selves﴾, so that he may judge among them with whatever judgment he wills, and that is permitted for him over them.

As related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ — just as you are closer to your slave: whatever judgment you pass concerning them is valid, just as whatever you decree over your slave is valid.

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ — he said: "He is a father to them."

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar related to us, saying: Fulayh related to us, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amra, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no believer except that I am the closest of people to him in this world and the Hereafter. Recite, if you wish: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾. Whichever believer leaves wealth, it belongs to his heirs and his male relatives (asabah), whoever they may be; and if he leaves debt or dependents, let him come to me, for I am his guardian (mawla)."

* Ibn Waki told us, saying: Hasan ibn Ali related to us, from Abu Musa Israil ibn Musa, saying: al-Hasan recited this verse: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers﴾, and said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am closer to every believer than his own self." Al-Hasan said: In the first recitation it is: ﴿closer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them﴾.

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said, regarding some recitation: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them﴾. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whichever man leaves dependents, I am responsible for them; and if he leaves wealth, it belongs to his heirs."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and his wives are their mothers﴾

It means: the sanctity of his wives is, for them, like the sanctity of their mothers, in that it is forbidden for them to marry them after his death, just as it is forbidden for them to marry their own mothers.

The people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers﴾ — thereby magnifying their rights. And in some recitation: ﴿and he is a father to them﴾.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿and his wives are their mothers﴾: they are forbidden to them.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those of blood-relationship, whose inheritance is conferred upon one another, are more entitled to the inheritance of one another than the believers and emigrants are to inherit from one another, by virtue of emigration and faith, rather than by kinship.

The people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants﴾ — the Muslims remained for a time inheriting through emigration, while a Muslim Bedouin inherited nothing from the emigrants. Then Allah revealed this verse, and so He mixed the believers together, and inheritance became based on religious community (milal).

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾: The Prophet (ﷺ) had established brotherhood between the emigrants and the Helpers at the very beginning of the emigration, and they used to inherit from one another on that basis. Allah said: ﴿And for each We have appointed heirs to what is left by parents and close relatives, and those with whom your oaths have bound you — give them their share﴾. He said: If there was no blood-relative to stand in the way of these, then this was the earlier rule. Then Allah said: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾, meaning: except that you bequeath to them. ﴿That is written in the Book﴾ — that those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah. He said: The believers and emigrants did not inherit from one another if they were of blood-relationship until they emigrated to Medina. He recited: Allah said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate — you have no guardianship over them until they emigrate...﴾ to His saying: ﴿and great corruption﴾. So they did not inherit from one another, until the year of the Conquest, when emigration ceased and Islam spread. Whoever wished to remain upon what the Prophet and those with him were upon was not accepted unless he emigrated. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to those he sent out: "Set out in the name of Allah; do not commit excess, nor betray. Call them to Islam; if they respond, accept it, and call them to emigration. If they emigrate with you, they have what you have and bear what you bear. If they refuse, do not emigrate, and choose their own abode, then leave them there; they are like the Bedouins, the rulings of Islam apply to them, and they have no share in this booty." He said: When the Conquest came and emigration ended, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no emigration after the Conquest." Islam spread, and people inherited through kinship wherever they were. That earlier arrangement between the believers and the emigrants was abrogated, and they had a share in the booty even if they remained and refused. Their right in Islam became one: the emigrant, the non-emigrant, the Bedouin, and everyone alike, once the Conquest came.

So the meaning of the statement according to this interpretation is: those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another among the believers and emigrants, in that they inherit from one another by virtue of emigration. It may also be that the apparent meaning of this statement is that the kinship of believers and emigrants gives them priority in inheritance over one who has neither believed nor emigrated.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: the meaning is: except that you bequeath to your kinsmen who are not of the faith and emigration.

Those who said so:

* Ibn Waki told us, saying: Abu Muawiya related to us, from Hajjaj, from Salim, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾ — they said: he bequeaths to his relatives among the polytheists.

* He said: Ubayd related to us, saying: I read to Ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾ — he said: for relatives among the polytheists there is a bequest, but they have no inheritance.

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾ — he said: to your close friends among the polytheists, a bequest; but they have no inheritance.

* Ibn Waki told us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri and Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Mu'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ikrimah: ﴿to your close friends, kindness﴾ — he said: a bequest.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, saying: I asked Ata: what is His saying: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾? He said: the gift. I said to him: a believer and a disbeliever, is there kinship between them? He said: Yes; his giving to him is a gift and a bequest to him.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: except that you hold fast to kindness among yourselves by the right of faith, emigration and alliance, giving them their due of support and blood-money on their behalf.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾: "Your allies whom the Prophet (ﷺ) bound together from among the emigrants and the Helpers; holding fast to kindness, blood-money and support among them."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: that you bequeath to your close friends among the emigrants.

Those who said so:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿except that you show kindness to your close friends﴾ — meaning: except that you bequeath to them.

The most correct of these views in my judgment, is to say: the meaning is: except that you do kindness to your close friends whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made brothers between you and them, from among the emigrants and the Helpers, by way of bequest to them, support, blood-money on their behalf, and the like, because all of that is kindness which Allah has urged upon His servants.

I have chosen this view and said it is more correct than the view of those who said that it refers to bequests to kinsmen among the polytheists, because a relative of a polytheist, though related by lineage, is not a protector (mawla); for polytheism severs the bond of guardianship between the believer and the polytheist, and Allah has forbidden the believers to take them as allies by His saying: ﴿Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. It is not permissible that He forbid them from taking them as allies and then describe them, may His praise be exalted, as being their allies. The position of "an" in His saying ﴿except that you show kindness﴾ is in the accusative as an exception. The meaning of the statement is: those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and emigrants, except that you show kindness to your close friends who are not blood-relatives of yours.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿That is written in the Book﴾

He says: those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah, that is, in the Preserved Tablet, written (masṭūr), meaning inscribed, as the rajaz poet said:

In the earlier scrolls that were inscribed [[A line in rajaz meter, by al-Ajjaj the rajaz poet, from his lengthy poem in praise of Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Mu'ammar, whom Abd al-Malik sent against the Kharijite Abu Fudayk, and who was victorious over him. (Diwan al-Ajjaj, Leipzig 1903, p. 19). The line is evidence that the meaning of saṭara is "to write," and al-saṭr is "line" and "writing."]]

The people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿That is written in the Book﴾: meaning, that those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "That is written in the Book": the polytheist does not inherit from the believer.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 7–8:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [Qur'an 33:7].

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: That was in the Book inscribed, when We wrote down everything that is to occur in the Book. ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾ — that too was in the Book inscribed. By "covenant" (mithaq) is meant the pledge, and we have already explained this with its evidences earlier. ﴿And from you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ — He says: And We took from all of them a firm pledge that some of them would confirm the others.

As follows:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾. He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "I was the first of the prophets in creation, and the last of them in being sent forth." ﴿And Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ — a covenant that Allah took from the prophets, especially that some of them would confirm the others, and that some of them would follow the others.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, saying: When Qatadah recited this verse, ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾, he would say: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was first among the prophets in creation.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾. He said: In the loins of Adam.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾. He said: The solemn covenant is the pledge.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾ [Qur'an 33:8].

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: We took from these prophets their covenant so that I might question the messengers about what their nations responded to them with, and what their peoples did regarding what they conveyed to them from their Lord of the message.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾. He said: The messengers who conveyed and discharged (the message).

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾. He said: The messengers who conveyed and discharged (the message).

* Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾. He said: The messengers who discharged and conveyed (the message).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾.

He says: And He has prepared for the disbelievers in Allah among the nations a painful, afflicting punishment.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 33, Verse 9:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when there came to you soldiers, so We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.﴾

His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾ which He bestowed upon your community, and that was when the Muslims were besieged with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the days of the Trench (al-Khandaq). ﴿When there came to you soldiers﴾: the soldiers of the confederates (al-Ahzab): Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu al-Nadir. ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾ and it was, as has been mentioned, the east wind (rih al-saba).

As follows:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: The south wind said to the north wind on the night of the confederates: "Let us go and help the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The north wind said: "The free woman does not travel by night." He said: So the wind that was sent upon them was the east wind (al-Saba).

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, he said: al-Zubayr (meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allah) told me, he said: Rubayh ibn Abi Saʿid told me, from his father, from Abu Saʿid, he said: We said on the day of the Trench: "O Messenger of Allah, the hearts have reached the throats, is there anything you can say?" He said: "Yes, say: O Allah, conceal our faults and secure our frightened hearts." So Allah struck the faces of His enemies with the wind, and Allah defeated them with the wind.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr told me, from Nafiʿ, from ʿAbd Allah, he said: My maternal uncle ʿUthman ibn Mazʿun sent me on the night of the Trench, in severe cold and wind, to Medina, and said: "Bring us food and a blanket." He said: So I asked permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he permitted me and said: "Whoever you meet of my companions, instruct them to return." He said: So I went, and the wind was blowing away everything, so I did not meet anyone without ordering him to return to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: None of them turned his neck. He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind kept striking it against me, and it had iron in it. He said: The wind struck it until some of that iron fell upon my palm, and it pierced it through to the ground.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, he said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, did you see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and accompany him?" He said: "Yes, my nephew." He said: "How did you used to act?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive greatly." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had met him we would not have let him walk on the earth; we would have carried him on our necks." Hudhayfah said: "O my nephew, by Allah, you would have seen us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Trench, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a portion of the night [[hawiyyan, with an open or closed ha' and a shadda on the ya', meaning an extended period of the night (al-Lisan: hawa).]] then turned to us and said: "Is there a man who will stand and look for us what the people have done? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stipulates for him that if he returns, Allah will admit him to Paradise." No one stood. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a portion of the night, then turned to us and said the same, and no man among us stood. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a portion of the night, then turned to us and said: "Is there a man who will stand and look for us what the people have done, then return? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stipulates for him the return. I ask Allah that he be my companion in Paradise." No man stood out of intense fear, intense hunger, and intense cold. When no one stood, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, and I had no choice but to stand when he called me. He said: "O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people and look, and do not do anything new until you come to us." He said: So I went and entered among the people, and the wind and the soldiers of Allah were doing to them what they were doing, not leaving for them a cooking pot, nor a fire, nor a structure. Then Abu Sufyan stood and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each man look at his neighbor." Hudhayfah said: So I took hold of the hand of the man beside me and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not woken up in a place of stay. The horses and the camels have perished, the Banu Qurayzah have broken their word, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have encountered from this wind what you see. By Allah, no cooking pot settles for us, no fire is kindled for us, and no structure holds firm for us. So depart, for I am departing." Then he rose to his camel, which was tied, sat upon it, and struck it, and it leapt with it on three legs. He did not untie its rope until it was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to me that I should not do anything until I came to him, I would have killed him with an arrow. Hudhayfah said: So I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was standing praying in a cloak belonging to one of his wives. When he saw me, he brought me in between his legs and cast the edge of the cloak over me, then he bowed and prostrated while I was in it. When he finished the prayer, I told him the news. The Ghatafan had heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back in retreat to their lands.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿when there came to you soldiers﴾ he said: The confederates: ʿUyaynah ibn Badr, Abu Sufyan, and Qurayzah.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿so We sent upon them a wind﴾

He said: It was the east wind that was sent upon the confederates on the day of the Trench, until it overturned their cooking pots onto their mouths and uprooted their tents until it drove them away.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and armies you did not see﴾

He said: The angels, and they did not fight that day.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when there came to you soldiers, so We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ he said: It means the angels. He said: This verse was revealed on the day of the confederates, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been besieged for a month, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dug the trench. Abu Sufyan came with Quraysh and those who followed him from the people, until they encamped in the courtyard [[al-ʿaqwah: the open space and what is around the house (from al-Lisan: ʿaqa).]] of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUyaynah ibn Hisn, one of Banu Badr, and those who followed him from the people came until they encamped in the courtyard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Jews corresponded with Abu Sufyan and supported him, and he said, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿when they came to you from above you and from below you﴾. Then Allah sent upon them terror and wind. It was mentioned to us that whenever they lit a fire, Allah extinguished it, until it was mentioned to us that the chief of every tribe would call out: "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" When they gathered around him, he would say: "Escape! Escape! You have come because of the terror that Allah has sent upon them."

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you...﴾ the verse, he said: It was the day of Abu Sufyan, the day of the confederates.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid ibn Rumán told me, regarding Allah's words: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when there came to you soldiers, so We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ The soldiers were Quraysh, Ghatafan, and Banu Qurayzah, and the soldiers that Allah sent upon them along with the wind were the angels.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And Allah is, regarding your deeds that day, which included your steadfastness in the hardship and severity you were in, your firmness against your enemy, and other of your deeds, All-Seeing; nothing of that is hidden from Him. He counts it against them, in order to reward them for it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 10–12 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ (10) ﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ (11) ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾ (12)

He, the Exalted, says: "And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do, when the armies of the confederates came upon you from above you and from below you." It has been said: those who came upon them from below them were Abu Sufyan and the Quraysh and those with him.

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when they came upon you from above you﴾: He said: Uyayna ibn Badr [[He is attributed to his father, al-A'la.]] with the people of Najd. ﴿and from below you﴾: He said: Abu Sufyan. He said: and Qurayza faced them.

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ubayda narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, that she mentioned the Day of the Trench and recited ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, and she said: "It is the Day of the Trench."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and from one whom I do not suspect, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, that the account of the Trench was that a group of Jews, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, and Kinana ibn al-Rabi' [[In some copies of the Sira of Ibn Ishaq it reads Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, without "ibn al-Rabi'".]] ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Hawdha ibn Qays al-Wa'ili, and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, along with a group from the Banu al-Nadir and a group from the Banu Wa'il, — and they are the ones who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — went out until they came to Mecca to the Quraysh, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." The Quraysh said to them: "O assembly of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and the knowledge of what we and Muhammad differ over. Is our religion better or his?" They said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than he is" [[Thus in the Sira (3: 225), Halabi edition. In the original: "minhum" (from them).]]. He said: They are the ones about whom Allah revealed ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in idols and false deities, and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believed, in the way"...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sufficient is Hell as a blaze﴾. When they said that to the Quraysh, it pleased them what they said, and they became eager for what they had invited them to, of war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they gathered for that and arranged a time for it. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays Aylan, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and informed them that they would be with them against him, and that the Quraysh had followed them in that; so they gathered for it, and they answered them [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 26): "fa-ijtama'u ma'ahum fihi" (so they gathered with them in it), and the words "fa-ajabuhum" (and they answered them) have fallen out of it.]]. So the Quraysh went out, and their leader was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb; and Ghatafan went out, and their leader was Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr among the Banu Fazara, and al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri among the Banu Murra, and Mis'ar ibn Rukhayla ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif ibn Sahma ibn Abd Allah ibn Hilal ibn Khalawa ibn Ashja' ibn Rayth ibn Ghatafan, with whoever followed him of his people from Ashja'. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them and of what they had gathered for, he dug the trench around Medina. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished with the trench, the Quraysh came and camped at the confluence of the sands of Rawma between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 230) it is "Zaghaba", with a fatha on the za and ghayn (and see al-Suhayli 2: 189).]], with ten thousand of their allies (ahabish), and whoever followed them from the Banu Kinana and the people of Tihama; and Ghatafan came and whoever followed them from the people of Najd, until they camped at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims went out until they placed their backs to Sal', three thousand of the Muslims; there he pitched his camp, with the trench between him and the people, and he ordered the children and women to be lifted into the fortresses (atam). The enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri went out until he came to Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, holder of the pact and covenant of the Banu Qurayza, who had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on behalf of his people and made a covenant and alliance with him on that. When Ka'b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he shut his fortress against him, and he asked permission to enter, but he refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Ka'b, open for me." He said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what is between me and him, and I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness." He said: "Woe to you, open for me, that I may speak with you." He said: "I will not do so." He said: "By Allah, if you shut me out, I will fear for your porridge that I might eat from it with you." The man became angry, and so he opened to him. He said: "O Ka'b, I have brought you the might of the age and a sea that has overflowed. I have brought you the Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the confluence of the sands of Rawma, and Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. They have pledged to me and made a covenant with me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him." Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age, and with a cloud that has poured out its water, thundering and lightning, with nothing in it. Leave me with Muhammad and what I am upon, for I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity." Huyayy did not cease to coax Ka'b, twisting him at the forelock and the back, until he consented on condition that he gave him a covenant and pledge from Allah that if Quraysh and Ghatafan returned without striking Muhammad, he would enter with him into his fortress so that what afflicted him would afflict Huyayy. Ka'b ibn Asad broke his covenant and renounced what was between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh ibn al-Nu'man ibn Imru' al-Qays, of the Banu al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn Ubada ibn Dulaym, brother of the Banu Sa'ida ibn Ka'b ibn al-Khazraj, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, and with them Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf. He said: "Go, and see whether what has reached us about these people is true or not. If it is true, then speak to me in a code I will understand, and do not weaken the resolve of the people; and if they are upon fidelity between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." They went out until they came to them, and found them at the worst of what had reached them about them, and they insulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "There is no covenant between us and Muhammad, nor any pact." Sa'd ibn Ubada and they insulted one another, and Sa'd ibn Ubada was a man with a hot temper. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insult." Then Sa'd and Sa'd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and then said: "Adal and al-Qara:" that is, [[Thus in the Sira (Halabi 3: 233). In the original it is without "ay".]] like the treachery of Adal and al-Qara against the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the people of al-Raji', Khubayb ibn Adi and his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is greatest! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!" At that the trial became great, and fear intensified, and their enemy came upon them from above them and from below them, until the Muslims thought every kind of thought, and hypocrisy erupted from some of the hypocrites, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, while one of us cannot go to relieve himself," and until Aws ibn Qayzi, one of the Banu Haritha ibn al-Harith, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and that was before a group of the men of his people, "so permit us to return to our homes, for they are outside Medina." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained some twenty-odd nights, nearly a month, and there was no fighting between the people except shooting with arrows and the siege [[In some references: "wa-l-hasa", written with an alif.]].

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding His saying ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾: those who came upon them from above them were Qurayza, and those who came upon them from below them were Quraysh and Ghatafan.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾

He says: and when the eyes turned away from their place and stared in alarm.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾: it means they stared fixedly.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾

He says: the hearts were uprooted from their places out of terror and fear, so they reached the throats.

As:

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿and the hearts reached the throats﴾: He said: from fright.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾

He says: and you assumed about Allah false assumptions, such as the assumption of those among them who thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be defeated, and that what Allah had promised of victory would not come to pass, and similar of their false assumptions which were assumed by those among those with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his army.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Hawdha ibn Khalifa narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: He said: various assumptions: the hypocrites assumed that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah had promised them was true, that He would make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists disliked it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿And you assumed about Allah the assumptions﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans recited ﴿al-zununa﴾ with the alif affirmed, and likewise ﴿wa-atana al-Rasula﴾ and ﴿fa-adallana al-sabila﴾ in pause and in continuity. The argument of those who maintained this was that it is affirmed with the alif in all the codices of the Muslims in these letters. Some of the Kufan reciters affirmed the alif in them at pause and omitted it in continuity, arguing that the Arabs do so at the rhyme-endings of poetry and its verse-ends, adding the alif at the place of the fatha for pause, and do not do so in the middle of verses; and that these letters were fitting for affirming the alifs, since they are the ends of verses, likening them to rhymes. Some reciters of Basra and Kufa recited it by omitting the alif from all of it, both in pause and continuity, arguing that this is not found in Arabic speech except in the rhymes of poetry and not otherwise, and that they only do so in rhymes to complete the meter of poetry, for if they did not do so the poetry would not be correct; and that this is not so in the Qur'an, since nothing compels them to that in the Qur'an. They said: moreover, they are without alif in the codex of Abd Allah.

The most correct of these recitations in my view is the recitation of him who recited it with the alif omitted in continuity and in pause, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, together with the fame of this recitation among the reciters of the two garrison cities, Kufa and Basra. Then the recitation with the alif affirmed in them in both pause and continuity; for the reason of him who affirmed it in the state of pause is that it is so in the script of the codices of the Muslims. And if the reason for affirming the alif in some states is that it is affirmed in the codices of the Muslims, then the obligation is that the recitation be established in all states, since it is affirmed in their codices. It is not permissible for the reason that requires reciting it in one manner in some states to exist in another state while the recitation differs; and this is not comparable to the rhymes of poetry, for in poetry the alifs are added at places of fatha, the yas at places of kasra, and the waws at places of damma, to complete the meter, and if that were not done the poem would cease to be poetry, having deviated from its meter; and nothing compels the reciter of the Qur'an to do that in the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾

He says: at that time the faith of the believers was tested, and the people were sifted, and the believer was distinguished from the hypocrite.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: He said: they were sifted.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾

He says: they were moved by the trial with a severe movement, and were tried and tested.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾

Doubt regarding faith and weakness in their belief in it: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." This, it is mentioned, was the saying of Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: he means Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, when he said what he said on the Day of the Trench.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾: He said: they spoke with hypocrisy that day, and the believers spoke with the truth and faith, ﴿They said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised"﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: He said: some people among the hypocrites said it. Muhammad used to promise us the conquest of Persia and Rome, while we are besieged here, so that none of us can go out for his need. "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: A man said on the Day of the Confederates to a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "O so-and-so, have you seen when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: 'When Caesar perishes, there is no Caesar after him, and when Kisra perishes, there is no Kisra after him, and by Him in whose hand is my soul, their treasures will surely be spent in the way of Allah'? So where is this from that, while one of us cannot go out to urinate for fear?" — "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." He said to him: "You have lied; I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of your words." He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he summoned him and said: "What did you say?" He said: "He lied against me, O Messenger of Allah; I said nothing, this never came out of my mouth." Allah said: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, and indeed they said the word of disbelief...﴾ until ﴿and they have no protector or helper in the earth.﴾ He said: and this is the saying of Allah: ﴿If We pardon a group of you, We will punish another group﴾.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah narrated to us, saying: Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug the trench (al-khandaq) in the year the Confederates (al-Ahzab) were mentioned, from Ahmar al-Shaykhayn [[In al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya with the commentary of al-Zurqani (2:102), al-Tabarani narrated with a chain that is not objectionable, from Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, that he (ﷺ) dug the trench from Akhmar al-Shaykhayn ... and they are two mounds at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh ...]] at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh. Then he assigned forty cubits to every ten (men). The Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) disagreed about Salman al-Farisi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: "Salman is one of us." The Muhajirun said: "Salman is one of us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Salman is of us, the People of the House." Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, and six men from the Ansar were assigned forty cubits. We dug beneath Dubar until we reached al-Sirra [[This phrase is thus given in the text, and it is perhaps corrupted. "Dubar" is a Persian word meaning "twice." His saying "until we reached" may be "until, when we reached."]]. God brought forth from the belly of the trench a white, round rock [[In some sources: "rounded." Al-Sirra means "the water."]]. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us. We said: "O Salman, go up to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him of the news of this rock. Either we shall deviate from it, for deviation is near, or he will command us concerning it with his command, for we do not wish to exceed his line."

Salman went up until he came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was pitching a Turkish tent, and said: "O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you, a white, round rock has emerged from the belly of the trench. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us, until no little or much of it comes away. So command us concerning it with your command, for we do not wish to exceed your line."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended with Salman into the trench, while we, the nine of us, stood on the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck the rock a blow that split it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains (labatayh), meaning the two lava plains of Madinah, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a second time, and it split, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a third time and broke it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest. Then he took Salman's hand and came up.

Salman said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of God, I have seen something I have never seen before." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you. We saw you strike, and a flash came out like a wave, and we saw you say 'Allahu akbar,' so we said it, and we saw nothing other than that." He said: "You have spoken truly. I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of the red ones (al-Humr) in the land of the Romans, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw came out from it, and the palaces of Sana'a illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. So rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory.

The Muslims rejoiced and said: "Praise be to God, a true promise, that He promised us victory after siege." The Confederates gathered (against them), and the Muslims said: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth ...﴾ [the verse]. The hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel? He tells you, and he makes you hope and promises you falsehood. He informs you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be opened to you, while you are digging the trench out of fear, and you cannot even come out." And God revealed the Qur'an: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 10–12 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ (10) ﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ (11) ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾ (12)

He, the Exalted, says: "And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do, when the armies of the confederates came upon you from above you and from below you." It has been said: those who came upon them from below them were Abu Sufyan and the Quraysh and those with him.

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when they came upon you from above you﴾: He said: Uyayna ibn Badr [[He is attributed to his father, al-A'la.]] with the people of Najd. ﴿and from below you﴾: He said: Abu Sufyan. He said: and Qurayza faced them.

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ubayda narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, that she mentioned the Day of the Trench and recited ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, and she said: "It is the Day of the Trench."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and from one whom I do not suspect, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, that the account of the Trench was that a group of Jews, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, and Kinana ibn al-Rabi' [[In some copies of the Sira of Ibn Ishaq it reads Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, without "ibn al-Rabi'".]] ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Hawdha ibn Qays al-Wa'ili, and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, along with a group from the Banu al-Nadir and a group from the Banu Wa'il, — and they are the ones who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — went out until they came to Mecca to the Quraysh, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." The Quraysh said to them: "O assembly of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and the knowledge of what we and Muhammad differ over. Is our religion better or his?" They said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than he is" [[Thus in the Sira (3: 225), Halabi edition. In the original: "minhum" (from them).]]. He said: They are the ones about whom Allah revealed ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in idols and false deities, and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believed, in the way"...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sufficient is Hell as a blaze﴾. When they said that to the Quraysh, it pleased them what they said, and they became eager for what they had invited them to, of war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they gathered for that and arranged a time for it. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays Aylan, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and informed them that they would be with them against him, and that the Quraysh had followed them in that; so they gathered for it, and they answered them [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 26): "fa-ijtama'u ma'ahum fihi" (so they gathered with them in it), and the words "fa-ajabuhum" (and they answered them) have fallen out of it.]]. So the Quraysh went out, and their leader was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb; and Ghatafan went out, and their leader was Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr among the Banu Fazara, and al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri among the Banu Murra, and Mis'ar ibn Rukhayla ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif ibn Sahma ibn Abd Allah ibn Hilal ibn Khalawa ibn Ashja' ibn Rayth ibn Ghatafan, with whoever followed him of his people from Ashja'. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them and of what they had gathered for, he dug the trench around Medina. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished with the trench, the Quraysh came and camped at the confluence of the sands of Rawma between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 230) it is "Zaghaba", with a fatha on the za and ghayn (and see al-Suhayli 2: 189).]], with ten thousand of their allies (ahabish), and whoever followed them from the Banu Kinana and the people of Tihama; and Ghatafan came and whoever followed them from the people of Najd, until they camped at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims went out until they placed their backs to Sal', three thousand of the Muslims; there he pitched his camp, with the trench between him and the people, and he ordered the children and women to be lifted into the fortresses (atam). The enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri went out until he came to Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, holder of the pact and covenant of the Banu Qurayza, who had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on behalf of his people and made a covenant and alliance with him on that. When Ka'b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he shut his fortress against him, and he asked permission to enter, but he refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Ka'b, open for me." He said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what is between me and him, and I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness." He said: "Woe to you, open for me, that I may speak with you." He said: "I will not do so." He said: "By Allah, if you shut me out, I will fear for your porridge that I might eat from it with you." The man became angry, and so he opened to him. He said: "O Ka'b, I have brought you the might of the age and a sea that has overflowed. I have brought you the Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the confluence of the sands of Rawma, and Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. They have pledged to me and made a covenant with me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him." Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age, and with a cloud that has poured out its water, thundering and lightning, with nothing in it. Leave me with Muhammad and what I am upon, for I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity." Huyayy did not cease to coax Ka'b, twisting him at the forelock and the back, until he consented on condition that he gave him a covenant and pledge from Allah that if Quraysh and Ghatafan returned without striking Muhammad, he would enter with him into his fortress so that what afflicted him would afflict Huyayy. Ka'b ibn Asad broke his covenant and renounced what was between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh ibn al-Nu'man ibn Imru' al-Qays, of the Banu al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn Ubada ibn Dulaym, brother of the Banu Sa'ida ibn Ka'b ibn al-Khazraj, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, and with them Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf. He said: "Go, and see whether what has reached us about these people is true or not. If it is true, then speak to me in a code I will understand, and do not weaken the resolve of the people; and if they are upon fidelity between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." They went out until they came to them, and found them at the worst of what had reached them about them, and they insulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "There is no covenant between us and Muhammad, nor any pact." Sa'd ibn Ubada and they insulted one another, and Sa'd ibn Ubada was a man with a hot temper. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insult." Then Sa'd and Sa'd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and then said: "Adal and al-Qara:" that is, [[Thus in the Sira (Halabi 3: 233). In the original it is without "ay".]] like the treachery of Adal and al-Qara against the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the people of al-Raji', Khubayb ibn Adi and his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is greatest! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!" At that the trial became great, and fear intensified, and their enemy came upon them from above them and from below them, until the Muslims thought every kind of thought, and hypocrisy erupted from some of the hypocrites, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, while one of us cannot go to relieve himself," and until Aws ibn Qayzi, one of the Banu Haritha ibn al-Harith, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and that was before a group of the men of his people, "so permit us to return to our homes, for they are outside Medina." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained some twenty-odd nights, nearly a month, and there was no fighting between the people except shooting with arrows and the siege [[In some references: "wa-l-hasa", written with an alif.]].

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding His saying ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾: those who came upon them from above them were Qurayza, and those who came upon them from below them were Quraysh and Ghatafan.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾

He says: and when the eyes turned away from their place and stared in alarm.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾: it means they stared fixedly.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾

He says: the hearts were uprooted from their places out of terror and fear, so they reached the throats.

As:

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿and the hearts reached the throats﴾: He said: from fright.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾

He says: and you assumed about Allah false assumptions, such as the assumption of those among them who thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be defeated, and that what Allah had promised of victory would not come to pass, and similar of their false assumptions which were assumed by those among those with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his army.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Hawdha ibn Khalifa narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: He said: various assumptions: the hypocrites assumed that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah had promised them was true, that He would make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists disliked it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿And you assumed about Allah the assumptions﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans recited ﴿al-zununa﴾ with the alif affirmed, and likewise ﴿wa-atana al-Rasula﴾ and ﴿fa-adallana al-sabila﴾ in pause and in continuity. The argument of those who maintained this was that it is affirmed with the alif in all the codices of the Muslims in these letters. Some of the Kufan reciters affirmed the alif in them at pause and omitted it in continuity, arguing that the Arabs do so at the rhyme-endings of poetry and its verse-ends, adding the alif at the place of the fatha for pause, and do not do so in the middle of verses; and that these letters were fitting for affirming the alifs, since they are the ends of verses, likening them to rhymes. Some reciters of Basra and Kufa recited it by omitting the alif from all of it, both in pause and continuity, arguing that this is not found in Arabic speech except in the rhymes of poetry and not otherwise, and that they only do so in rhymes to complete the meter of poetry, for if they did not do so the poetry would not be correct; and that this is not so in the Qur'an, since nothing compels them to that in the Qur'an. They said: moreover, they are without alif in the codex of Abd Allah.

The most correct of these recitations in my view is the recitation of him who recited it with the alif omitted in continuity and in pause, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, together with the fame of this recitation among the reciters of the two garrison cities, Kufa and Basra. Then the recitation with the alif affirmed in them in both pause and continuity; for the reason of him who affirmed it in the state of pause is that it is so in the script of the codices of the Muslims. And if the reason for affirming the alif in some states is that it is affirmed in the codices of the Muslims, then the obligation is that the recitation be established in all states, since it is affirmed in their codices. It is not permissible for the reason that requires reciting it in one manner in some states to exist in another state while the recitation differs; and this is not comparable to the rhymes of poetry, for in poetry the alifs are added at places of fatha, the yas at places of kasra, and the waws at places of damma, to complete the meter, and if that were not done the poem would cease to be poetry, having deviated from its meter; and nothing compels the reciter of the Qur'an to do that in the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾

He says: at that time the faith of the believers was tested, and the people were sifted, and the believer was distinguished from the hypocrite.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: He said: they were sifted.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾

He says: they were moved by the trial with a severe movement, and were tried and tested.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾

Doubt regarding faith and weakness in their belief in it: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." This, it is mentioned, was the saying of Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:
