Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: he means Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, when he said what he said on the Day of the Trench.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾: He said: they spoke with hypocrisy that day, and the believers spoke with the truth and faith, ﴿They said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised"﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: He said: some people among the hypocrites said it. Muhammad used to promise us the conquest of Persia and Rome, while we are besieged here, so that none of us can go out for his need. "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: A man said on the Day of the Confederates to a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "O so-and-so, have you seen when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: 'When Caesar perishes, there is no Caesar after him, and when Kisra perishes, there is no Kisra after him, and by Him in whose hand is my soul, their treasures will surely be spent in the way of Allah'? So where is this from that, while one of us cannot go out to urinate for fear?" — "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." He said to him: "You have lied; I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of your words." He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he summoned him and said: "What did you say?" He said: "He lied against me, O Messenger of Allah; I said nothing, this never came out of my mouth." Allah said: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, and indeed they said the word of disbelief...﴾ until ﴿and they have no protector or helper in the earth.﴾ He said: and this is the saying of Allah: ﴿If We pardon a group of you, We will punish another group﴾.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah narrated to us, saying: Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug the trench (al-khandaq) in the year the Confederates (al-Ahzab) were mentioned, from Ahmar al-Shaykhayn [[In al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya with the commentary of al-Zurqani (2:102), al-Tabarani narrated with a chain that is not objectionable, from Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, that he (ﷺ) dug the trench from Akhmar al-Shaykhayn ... and they are two mounds at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh ...]] at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh. Then he assigned forty cubits to every ten (men). The Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) disagreed about Salman al-Farisi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: "Salman is one of us." The Muhajirun said: "Salman is one of us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Salman is of us, the People of the House." Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, and six men from the Ansar were assigned forty cubits. We dug beneath Dubar until we reached al-Sirra [[This phrase is thus given in the text, and it is perhaps corrupted. "Dubar" is a Persian word meaning "twice." His saying "until we reached" may be "until, when we reached."]]. God brought forth from the belly of the trench a white, round rock [[In some sources: "rounded." Al-Sirra means "the water."]]. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us. We said: "O Salman, go up to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him of the news of this rock. Either we shall deviate from it, for deviation is near, or he will command us concerning it with his command, for we do not wish to exceed his line."

Salman went up until he came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was pitching a Turkish tent, and said: "O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you, a white, round rock has emerged from the belly of the trench. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us, until no little or much of it comes away. So command us concerning it with your command, for we do not wish to exceed your line."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended with Salman into the trench, while we, the nine of us, stood on the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck the rock a blow that split it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains (labatayh), meaning the two lava plains of Madinah, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a second time, and it split, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a third time and broke it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest. Then he took Salman's hand and came up.

Salman said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of God, I have seen something I have never seen before." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you. We saw you strike, and a flash came out like a wave, and we saw you say 'Allahu akbar,' so we said it, and we saw nothing other than that." He said: "You have spoken truly. I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of the red ones (al-Humr) in the land of the Romans, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw came out from it, and the palaces of Sana'a illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. So rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory.

The Muslims rejoiced and said: "Praise be to God, a true promise, that He promised us victory after siege." The Confederates gathered (against them), and the Muslims said: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth ...﴾ [the verse]. The hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel? He tells you, and he makes you hope and promises you falsehood. He informs you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be opened to you, while you are digging the trench out of fear, and you cannot even come out." And God revealed the Qur'an: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 10–12 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ (10) ﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ (11) ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾ (12)

He, the Exalted, says: "And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do, when the armies of the confederates came upon you from above you and from below you." It has been said: those who came upon them from below them were Abu Sufyan and the Quraysh and those with him.

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when they came upon you from above you﴾: He said: Uyayna ibn Badr [[He is attributed to his father, al-A'la.]] with the people of Najd. ﴿and from below you﴾: He said: Abu Sufyan. He said: and Qurayza faced them.

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ubayda narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, that she mentioned the Day of the Trench and recited ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, and she said: "It is the Day of the Trench."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and from one whom I do not suspect, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, that the account of the Trench was that a group of Jews, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, and Kinana ibn al-Rabi' [[In some copies of the Sira of Ibn Ishaq it reads Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, without "ibn al-Rabi'".]] ibn Abi al-Huqayq al-Nadri, and Hawdha ibn Qays al-Wa'ili, and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, along with a group from the Banu al-Nadir and a group from the Banu Wa'il, — and they are the ones who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — went out until they came to Mecca to the Quraysh, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." The Quraysh said to them: "O assembly of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and the knowledge of what we and Muhammad differ over. Is our religion better or his?" They said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than he is" [[Thus in the Sira (3: 225), Halabi edition. In the original: "minhum" (from them).]]. He said: They are the ones about whom Allah revealed ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in idols and false deities, and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believed, in the way"...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sufficient is Hell as a blaze﴾. When they said that to the Quraysh, it pleased them what they said, and they became eager for what they had invited them to, of war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they gathered for that and arranged a time for it. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays Aylan, and invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and informed them that they would be with them against him, and that the Quraysh had followed them in that; so they gathered for it, and they answered them [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 26): "fa-ijtama'u ma'ahum fihi" (so they gathered with them in it), and the words "fa-ajabuhum" (and they answered them) have fallen out of it.]]. So the Quraysh went out, and their leader was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb; and Ghatafan went out, and their leader was Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr among the Banu Fazara, and al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri among the Banu Murra, and Mis'ar ibn Rukhayla ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif ibn Sahma ibn Abd Allah ibn Hilal ibn Khalawa ibn Ashja' ibn Rayth ibn Ghatafan, with whoever followed him of his people from Ashja'. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them and of what they had gathered for, he dug the trench around Medina. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished with the trench, the Quraysh came and camped at the confluence of the sands of Rawma between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba [[In the Sira (Halabi 3: 230) it is "Zaghaba", with a fatha on the za and ghayn (and see al-Suhayli 2: 189).]], with ten thousand of their allies (ahabish), and whoever followed them from the Banu Kinana and the people of Tihama; and Ghatafan came and whoever followed them from the people of Najd, until they camped at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims went out until they placed their backs to Sal', three thousand of the Muslims; there he pitched his camp, with the trench between him and the people, and he ordered the children and women to be lifted into the fortresses (atam). The enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri went out until he came to Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, holder of the pact and covenant of the Banu Qurayza, who had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on behalf of his people and made a covenant and alliance with him on that. When Ka'b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he shut his fortress against him, and he asked permission to enter, but he refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Ka'b, open for me." He said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what is between me and him, and I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness." He said: "Woe to you, open for me, that I may speak with you." He said: "I will not do so." He said: "By Allah, if you shut me out, I will fear for your porridge that I might eat from it with you." The man became angry, and so he opened to him. He said: "O Ka'b, I have brought you the might of the age and a sea that has overflowed. I have brought you the Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the confluence of the sands of Rawma, and Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the slope of Nuqmi beside Uhud. They have pledged to me and made a covenant with me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him." Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age, and with a cloud that has poured out its water, thundering and lightning, with nothing in it. Leave me with Muhammad and what I am upon, for I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity." Huyayy did not cease to coax Ka'b, twisting him at the forelock and the back, until he consented on condition that he gave him a covenant and pledge from Allah that if Quraysh and Ghatafan returned without striking Muhammad, he would enter with him into his fortress so that what afflicted him would afflict Huyayy. Ka'b ibn Asad broke his covenant and renounced what was between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh ibn al-Nu'man ibn Imru' al-Qays, of the Banu al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn Ubada ibn Dulaym, brother of the Banu Sa'ida ibn Ka'b ibn al-Khazraj, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, and with them Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf. He said: "Go, and see whether what has reached us about these people is true or not. If it is true, then speak to me in a code I will understand, and do not weaken the resolve of the people; and if they are upon fidelity between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." They went out until they came to them, and found them at the worst of what had reached them about them, and they insulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "There is no covenant between us and Muhammad, nor any pact." Sa'd ibn Ubada and they insulted one another, and Sa'd ibn Ubada was a man with a hot temper. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insult." Then Sa'd and Sa'd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and then said: "Adal and al-Qara:" that is, [[Thus in the Sira (Halabi 3: 233). In the original it is without "ay".]] like the treachery of Adal and al-Qara against the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the people of al-Raji', Khubayb ibn Adi and his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is greatest! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!" At that the trial became great, and fear intensified, and their enemy came upon them from above them and from below them, until the Muslims thought every kind of thought, and hypocrisy erupted from some of the hypocrites, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, while one of us cannot go to relieve himself," and until Aws ibn Qayzi, one of the Banu Haritha ibn al-Harith, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and that was before a group of the men of his people, "so permit us to return to our homes, for they are outside Medina." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained some twenty-odd nights, nearly a month, and there was no fighting between the people except shooting with arrows and the siege [[In some references: "wa-l-hasa", written with an alif.]].

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding His saying ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾: those who came upon them from above them were Qurayza, and those who came upon them from below them were Quraysh and Ghatafan.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾

He says: and when the eyes turned away from their place and stared in alarm.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾: it means they stared fixedly.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾

He says: the hearts were uprooted from their places out of terror and fear, so they reached the throats.

As:

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿and the hearts reached the throats﴾: He said: from fright.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾

He says: and you assumed about Allah false assumptions, such as the assumption of those among them who thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be defeated, and that what Allah had promised of victory would not come to pass, and similar of their false assumptions which were assumed by those among those with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his army.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Hawdha ibn Khalifa narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: He said: various assumptions: the hypocrites assumed that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah had promised them was true, that He would make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists disliked it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿And you assumed about Allah the assumptions﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans recited ﴿al-zununa﴾ with the alif affirmed, and likewise ﴿wa-atana al-Rasula﴾ and ﴿fa-adallana al-sabila﴾ in pause and in continuity. The argument of those who maintained this was that it is affirmed with the alif in all the codices of the Muslims in these letters. Some of the Kufan reciters affirmed the alif in them at pause and omitted it in continuity, arguing that the Arabs do so at the rhyme-endings of poetry and its verse-ends, adding the alif at the place of the fatha for pause, and do not do so in the middle of verses; and that these letters were fitting for affirming the alifs, since they are the ends of verses, likening them to rhymes. Some reciters of Basra and Kufa recited it by omitting the alif from all of it, both in pause and continuity, arguing that this is not found in Arabic speech except in the rhymes of poetry and not otherwise, and that they only do so in rhymes to complete the meter of poetry, for if they did not do so the poetry would not be correct; and that this is not so in the Qur'an, since nothing compels them to that in the Qur'an. They said: moreover, they are without alif in the codex of Abd Allah.

The most correct of these recitations in my view is the recitation of him who recited it with the alif omitted in continuity and in pause, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, together with the fame of this recitation among the reciters of the two garrison cities, Kufa and Basra. Then the recitation with the alif affirmed in them in both pause and continuity; for the reason of him who affirmed it in the state of pause is that it is so in the script of the codices of the Muslims. And if the reason for affirming the alif in some states is that it is affirmed in the codices of the Muslims, then the obligation is that the recitation be established in all states, since it is affirmed in their codices. It is not permissible for the reason that requires reciting it in one manner in some states to exist in another state while the recitation differs; and this is not comparable to the rhymes of poetry, for in poetry the alifs are added at places of fatha, the yas at places of kasra, and the waws at places of damma, to complete the meter, and if that were not done the poem would cease to be poetry, having deviated from its meter; and nothing compels the reciter of the Qur'an to do that in the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾

He says: at that time the faith of the believers was tested, and the people were sifted, and the believer was distinguished from the hypocrite.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: He said: they were sifted.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾

He says: they were moved by the trial with a severe movement, and were tried and tested.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾

Doubt regarding faith and weakness in their belief in it: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." This, it is mentioned, was the saying of Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.

The commentators have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: he means Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, when he said what he said on the Day of the Trench.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾: He said: they spoke with hypocrisy that day, and the believers spoke with the truth and faith, ﴿They said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised"﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾: He said: some people among the hypocrites said it. Muhammad used to promise us the conquest of Persia and Rome, while we are besieged here, so that none of us can go out for his need. "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: A man said on the Day of the Confederates to a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "O so-and-so, have you seen when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: 'When Caesar perishes, there is no Caesar after him, and when Kisra perishes, there is no Kisra after him, and by Him in whose hand is my soul, their treasures will surely be spent in the way of Allah'? So where is this from that, while one of us cannot go out to urinate for fear?" — "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." He said to him: "You have lied; I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of your words." He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he summoned him and said: "What did you say?" He said: "He lied against me, O Messenger of Allah; I said nothing, this never came out of my mouth." Allah said: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, and indeed they said the word of disbelief...﴾ until ﴿and they have no protector or helper in the earth.﴾ He said: and this is the saying of Allah: ﴿If We pardon a group of you, We will punish another group﴾.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah narrated to us, saying: Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug the trench (al-khandaq) in the year the Confederates (al-Ahzab) were mentioned, from Ahmar al-Shaykhayn [[In al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya with the commentary of al-Zurqani (2:102), al-Tabarani narrated with a chain that is not objectionable, from Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, that he (ﷺ) dug the trench from Akhmar al-Shaykhayn ... and they are two mounds at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh ...]] at the edge of Banu Harithah, until it reached al-Mudhadh. Then he assigned forty cubits to every ten (men). The Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) disagreed about Salman al-Farisi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: "Salman is one of us." The Muhajirun said: "Salman is one of us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Salman is of us, the People of the House." Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, and six men from the Ansar were assigned forty cubits. We dug beneath Dubar until we reached al-Sirra [[This phrase is thus given in the text, and it is perhaps corrupted. "Dubar" is a Persian word meaning "twice." His saying "until we reached" may be "until, when we reached."]]. God brought forth from the belly of the trench a white, round rock [[In some sources: "rounded." Al-Sirra means "the water."]]. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us. We said: "O Salman, go up to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him of the news of this rock. Either we shall deviate from it, for deviation is near, or he will command us concerning it with his command, for we do not wish to exceed his line."

Salman went up until he came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was pitching a Turkish tent, and said: "O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you, a white, round rock has emerged from the belly of the trench. It broke our iron tools and was hard on us, until no little or much of it comes away. So command us concerning it with your command, for we do not wish to exceed your line."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended with Salman into the trench, while we, the nine of us, stood on the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck the rock a blow that split it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains (labatayh), meaning the two lava plains of Madinah, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a second time, and it split, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said it too. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck it a third time and broke it, and from it there flashed a flash that lit up what was between its two lava plains, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest. Then he took Salman's hand and came up.

Salman said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of God, I have seen something I have never seen before." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, may our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you. We saw you strike, and a flash came out like a wave, and we saw you say 'Allahu akbar,' so we said it, and we saw nothing other than that." He said: "You have spoken truly. I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw illuminated for me from it the palaces of the red ones (al-Humr) in the land of the Romans, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw came out from it, and the palaces of Sana'a illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. So rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory. "And rejoice!" He gives them the news of victory.

The Muslims rejoiced and said: "Praise be to God, a true promise, that He promised us victory after siege." The Confederates gathered (against them), and the Muslims said: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth ...﴾ [the verse]. The hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel? He tells you, and he makes you hope and promises you falsehood. He informs you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be opened to you, while you are digging the trench out of fear, and you cannot even come out." And God revealed the Qur'an: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return," and a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed; they only intended to flee.﴾ (13) ﴿And if they had been entered from its all sides, then they had been asked to commit fitnah (apostasy), they would have done it, and they would not have delayed in it except briefly.﴾ (14)

His exalted saying means: And when some of them said, "O people of Yathrib" — i.e., some of them said, "O people of Yathrib." Yathrib is the name of a land, and it is said that the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is in a part of Yathrib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿lā muqāma lakum fa-irjiʿū﴾ ("there is no place for you, so return")

It is read with a fatha on the mim in muqām. He means: there is no place for you in which you may stand, as the poet said:

"So whichever of me and you was evil... then go to the station (al-maqāma), you will not see it." [[The line is by ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās, and its use as evidence was mentioned earlier (20:66). Abu ʿUbayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 193b), on the interpretation of His saying "lā muqāma lakum": the first (mim) is fatha. Its meaning: there is no place for you in which you stand. And from it is his saying: "fa-innī mā wa-ayyuka kān sharran..." the verse.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿fa-irjiʿū﴾ ("so return")

He means: return to your dwellings. He commanded them to flee from the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to escape from it, and to leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was also said that this was the speech of Aws ibn Qayẓī and those who agreed with his opinion.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Rumān told me: ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib..."﴾ up to ﴿except fleeing﴾: He means Aws ibn Qayẓī and whoever held his opinion from his people. The reading with fatha on the mim in ﴿lā maqāma lakum﴾ means: there is no place of standing for you, and this is the reading I do not consider permissible to depart from, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. It is reported from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it ﴿lā muqāma lakum﴾ with a damma on the mim, meaning: there is no residence for you.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed; they only intended to flee.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, means: some of them asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to depart from him to their homes, but they intended only to flee and escape from the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And a party of them asked the Prophet...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿except fleeing﴾: He said: They were the Banu Haritha, who said: "Our houses are unguarded; we fear theft for them."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾: He said: We fear theft for them.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed﴾: And it is on the side facing the enemy, and we fear thieves for it; so the Prophet (ﷺ) sent someone, and he found no enemy there. Allah said: ﴿They only intend to flee﴾: meaning, their saying "Indeed, our houses are exposed" was only intended to flee.

Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, he said: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Hamran narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Shaddad Abu Talut narrated to us, from his father, regarding this verse, ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed, and they are not exposed﴾: He said: "Unprotected."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they had been entered from its all sides﴾

He means: if the city had been entered upon these who said ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾ from its sides, i.e., from its flanks and regions. Its singular is qaṭr, and there is another dialect: quṭr, and aqtār. From it is the saying of the rajiz:

"If you wish to anoint or to dye, then give them your quṭrak al-ashar..." [[The two verses are from the mashṭūr rajaz meter. I have not identified their speaker. The evidence in them is in his saying "quṭrak," with damma then sukun, meaning qaṭr, which is the side and region. Abu ʿUbayda said: "min aqtārihā" means from its sides and regions; its singular is qaṭr. In Lisan al-ʿArab (qatar): al-qatr, with damma then sukun, and al-futr, with two dammas: the region and side, a dialect for qaṭr, and its plural is al-aqtār. And in Lisan (qaṭar): in the revealed Book, "from the aqtār of the heavens and the earth": its aqtār means its regions; its singular is qaṭr, and likewise aqtārahā, its singular qatr.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Then they had been asked the fitnah﴾

He means: then they had been asked to return from faith to polytheism. ﴿they would have done it﴾: meaning, they would have acted and turned away from Islam and associated partners with Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿and they would not have delayed in it except briefly﴾

He means: they would not have hesitated in answering the call to polytheism except briefly, a little; they would have hastened to it.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And if they had been entered from its sides﴾, i.e., if it had been entered from the regions of the city; ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah﴾, i.e., polytheism; ﴿they would have done it﴾, meaning, they would have given it; ﴿and they would not have delayed in it except briefly﴾, meaning: except that they would have given it willingly, without holding back.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And if they had been entered from its sides﴾, meaning: if the city had been entered upon them from its regions, ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah, they would have done it﴾: if they had been asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: These hypocrites, if armies had entered upon them, and those who wish to fight them, then they had been asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: The fitnah is disbelief, and it is what Allah says: ﴿The fitnah is worse than killing﴾, meaning disbelief. He means: fear of them and the corruption of the fitnah they are upon, which is hypocrisy, drives them to disbelieve in it.

The readers differed in the reading of His saying: ﴿lā-ātawhā﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and some readers of Mecca read ﴿la-atawhā﴾ with a short alif, meaning "they came to it." Some Meccans and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read ﴿la-ātawhā﴾ with a long alif, meaning "they gave it," due to His saying: ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah﴾. They said: when there is a request, it is giving. The long alif is the more preferable of the two readings to me for what I have mentioned, although the other is also permissible.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And if they had been entered from its sides﴾, i.e., if it had been entered from the regions of the city; ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah﴾, i.e., polytheism; ﴿they would have done it﴾, meaning, they would have given it; ﴿and they would not have delayed in it except briefly﴾, meaning: except that they would have given it willingly, without holding back.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And if they had been entered from its sides﴾, meaning: if the city had been entered upon them from its regions, ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah, they would have done it﴾: if they had been asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: These hypocrites, if armies had entered upon them, and those who wish to fight them, then they had been asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: The fitnah is disbelief, and it is what Allah says: ﴿The fitnah is worse than killing﴾, meaning disbelief. He means: fear of them and the corruption of the fitnah they are upon, which is hypocrisy, drives them to disbelieve in it.

The readers differed in the reading of His saying: ﴿lā-ātawhā﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and some readers of Mecca read ﴿la-atawhā﴾ with a short alif, meaning "they came to it." Some Meccans and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read ﴿la-ātawhā﴾ with a long alif, meaning "they gave it," due to His saying: ﴿then they had been asked the fitnah﴾. They said: when there is a request, it is giving. The long alif is the more preferable of the two readings to me for what I have mentioned, although the other is also permissible.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 15:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs. And the covenant of Allah is ever questioned.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who were asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to withdraw from him, saying, ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed⦆ [and vulnerable], had made a covenant with Allah before that, that they would not turn their backs to their enemy. Indeed, their saying (that) in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among them was (a lie), so they did not fulfill their covenant. ﴿And the covenant of Allah is ever questioned﴾ means: Allah will question those to whom He gave it, about what they pledged of themselves.

It has been mentioned that this was revealed concerning the Banu Harithah, because of what they did at the Trench after what had occurred from them at Uhud.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me regarding ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs. And the covenant of Allah is ever questioned.﴾ They were the Banu Harithah, and they were the ones who intended to lose heart on the Day of Uhud along with the Banu Salamah when the two groups were inclined to falter on the Day of Uhud. Then they made a covenant with Allah that they would not return to the like of it, so Allah reminded them of what they had pledged of themselves.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs. And the covenant of Allah is ever questioned.﴾ He said: Some people were absent from the Battle of Badr, and they saw what Allah had given the companions of Badr of honor and virtue, so they said: "If Allah makes us witness fighting, we will surely fight." Then Allah brought that test upon them until it was in the vicinity of Madinah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 16–17:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Flight will never benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little.﴾ (16) ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy? And they will not find for themselves, other than Allah, any ally or any helper.﴾ (17)

His exalted Mention says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say⁠﴾, O Muhammad, to these who ask your permission to withdraw from you and say: "Indeed, our houses are exposed" (to danger), ﴿flight will never benefit you if you flee from death or killing﴾, meaning: because that, or whatever of the two Allah has decreed, will reach you in every case, whether you dislike it or like it. ﴿And then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾, meaning: and if you flee from death or killing, your flight will not add to your lifespans and your terms; rather, you will only be given enjoyment in this world until the time that has been decreed for you, and then what has been decreed for you and against you will come to you.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Say: Flight will never benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾: "Indeed, the whole of this world is little."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾: He said: "Until their terms (ajal)."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾: He said: "What is between them and their term."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, the like of it, except that he said: "What is between them and their terms."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾ (Q 9:82). He said: "Let them laugh in this world a little and let them weep in the Fire much." And he said regarding this verse: ﴿and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾: He said: "Until their terms." One of these two reports he traced back to Rabi' ibn Khuthaym.

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾: He said: "The term (ajal)." And he raised the word ﴿you will be given enjoyment﴾ and did not put it in the accusative governed by "idhan" because of the waw that precedes it. That is because when a waw comes before it, the meaning of "idhan" is delay after the verb, as if it were said: "Even if they fled, they would not be given enjoyment except for a little, then." Sometimes it is put in the accusative even when a waw accompanies it, since the verb is omitted, so it is as if it were at the beginning of the speech.

* *

His words: ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?⁠﴾

His exalted Mention says: Say, O Muhammad, to these who ask your permission and say: ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾, fleeing from killing: Who is it that will prevent you from Allah if He intends for you harm in yourselves, whether killing, affliction, or otherwise, or well-being and safety? Is what befalls you in yourselves of harm or mercy anything other than from Him?

As:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?⁠﴾: That is, the matter is only what You have decreed.

* *

And His words: ﴿And they will not find for themselves, other than Allah, any ally or any helper⁠﴾

His exalted Mention says: And these hypocrites will not find, if Allah intends for them harm in their selves and their wealth, ﴿other than Allah, any ally﴾ who will take charge of them with sufficiency, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who will help them against Allah and repel from them what Allah intends for them of such harm.

Those have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah.﴾

His, may He be remembered, saying: Allah knows those among you who hinder the people from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, turning them away from him and from attending the battle with him, out of hypocrisy and discouraging [them] from Islam and its people. ﴿And those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾: that is, come to us, and leave Muhammad, and do not attend his battle with him, for we fear destruction for you by his destruction. ﴿And they do not come to battle except a little﴾ means: they do not attend the war and fighting, if they attend, except [making] excuses and warding off [suspicion] from themselves [and] from the believers.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others], and those who say to their brothers﴾: He said: These are people from the hypocrites who used to say to their brothers: Muhammad and his companions are but a morsel of bread; if they were flesh, Abu Sufyan and his companions would have devoured them. Leave this man, for he is doomed.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And they do not come to battle except a little﴾

That is: they do not attend the fighting; they absent themselves from it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to us: ﴿Allah knows those among you who hinder [others]﴾: that is, the people of hypocrisy; ﴿and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not come to battle except a little﴾: that is, except [making] a defense and excuses.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: (Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others], and those who say to their brothers ...) to the end of the verse: He said: This was the day of the Confederates. A man departed from the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found his brother before him with roasted meat, bread, and nabidh (date wine). He said to him: You are here with the roast meat, the bread, and the nabidh, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among the spears and swords? He said: Come to this, for it has reached you and your companion. By Him by whom he swears, Muhammad will never face them again. He said: You lie, by Him by whom he swears. He said—and he was his brother from his father and mother—: By Allah, I will surely inform the Prophet ﷺ of your matter. He said: So he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to inform him; he said: He found that Jibril, peace be upon him, had already descended with news of it: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others], and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not come to battle except a little﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿being stingy toward you﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning in which Allah described these hypocrites with stinginess in this place. Some of them said: He described them as being stingy toward you regarding the booty.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿being stingy toward you﴾ regarding the booty.

Others said: Rather, He described them as being stingy toward you with good.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to me, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿being stingy toward you﴾ — he said: "with good," [referring to] the hypocrites. Another said: its meaning is: stingy toward you with spending on the weak among the believers from among you.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that it should be said: Allah described these hypocrites with cowardice and stinginess, and did not restrict their description to one meaning of stinginess over another. So they are, as Allah described them: stingy toward the believers regarding the booty, the good, and spending in the way of Allah, upon the needy among the Muslims. The accusative of His words ﴿being stingy toward you﴾ is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) referring to the noun in His words ﴿and they do not come to battle﴾, as if it were said: They are cowardly at the time of battle, stingy at the time of distributing the booty. It may also be a detached element (qaṭʿ) from His words ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others]﴾, so its interpretation would be: Allah knows those who hinder people from fighting, and who are stingy at the conquest with the booty. It is also permissible that it be detached from His words: "Come to us, [being] stingy," and they are thus stingy. Exalted is His praise, He described them with what He described them of stinginess toward the believers because of the enmity and rancor they hold in their hearts toward them.

As:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿being stingy toward you﴾: that is, out of the rancor that is in their hearts.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when fear comes…﴾

up to His words: ﴿from death﴾. He, may He be remembered, says: When the peril arrives and fighting comes, they fear destruction and killing. You see them, O Muhammad, looking at you, seeking refuge in you; their eyes revolve out of fear of being killed and in flight from it. ﴿Like one who is overcome with unconsciousness from death﴾ means: like the revolving of the eye of one who faints from the death descending upon him. ﴿But when the fear departs﴾ means: when the fighting ceases and they are at ease, ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving﴾ — out of fear.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one fainting from death﴾: that is, out of awe and fright of it. As for His words ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾, He means: they bite you with sharp tongues. It is said of an eloquent man with a sharp tongue: a khatib musalliq and musallaq (a fluent orator), and khatib sallaq and sallaq.

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning in which Allah described these hypocrites as lashing the believers. Some said: that lashing is their assailing them at the time of booty, by demanding a share from them.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿But when the fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ — as for at the time of booty, they are the stingiest people and the worst in dividing; "Give us, give us, for we have witnessed with you." As for at the time of peril, they are the most cowardly people and the most forsaking of the truth.

Others said: Rather, that lashing of them is by harm.

Mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾: he said: "they confront you."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾: he said: "they speak to you."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they lash them with speech of what you dislike, out of hypocrisy.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿But when the fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ — in speech of what you dislike, because they do not hope for an afterlife, nor does reckoning move them; they dread death with the dread of one who does not hope for what comes after it.

The most fitting of these statements to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the view of one who said: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues, being stingy toward good﴾. He informs that their lashing of the Muslims is out of stinginess regarding the booty and good. Thus, since that is so, it is known that it is for seeking the booty. And when this is their aim in seeking booty, the saying of one who said: its meaning is: they lash you with harm, is included, for their doing so is undoubtedly harmful to the believers.

* *

And His saying: ﴿being stingy toward good﴾

He says: stingy regarding the booty when the believers are victorious.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: Those whose description I have conveyed to you in these verses did not truly affirm Allah and His Messenger. Rather, they are people of disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿So Allah has nullified their deeds﴾ means: Allah has removed and voided the rewards of their deeds. It has been mentioned that the one described with this attribute was one of the people of Badr, so Allah nullified his deed.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿So Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾: He said: My father told me that he was of the people of Badr, and that His words ﴿so Allah has nullified their deeds﴾ mean that Allah nullified his deed on the day of Badr.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and that is ever easy for Allah﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: And the nullifying of their deeds, which they had done before their apostasy and hypocrisy, was easy for Allah.

The accusative of His words ﴿being stingy toward you﴾ is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) referring to the noun in His words ﴿and they do not come to battle﴾, as if it were said: They are cowardly at the time of battle, stingy at the time of distributing the booty. It may also be a detached element (qaṭʿ) from His words ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others]﴾, so its interpretation would be: Allah knows those who hinder people from fighting, and who are stingy at the conquest with the booty. It is also permissible that it be detached from His words: "Come to us, [being] stingy," and they are thus stingy. Exalted is His praise, He described them with what He described them of stinginess toward the believers because of the enmity and rancor they hold in their hearts toward them.

As:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿being stingy toward you﴾: that is, out of the rancor that is in their hearts.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when fear comes…﴾

up to His words: ﴿from death﴾. He, may He be remembered, says: When the peril arrives and fighting comes, they fear destruction and killing. You see them, O Muhammad, looking at you, seeking refuge in you; their eyes revolve out of fear of being killed and in flight from it. ﴿Like one who is overcome with unconsciousness from death﴾ means: like the revolving of the eye of one who faints from the death descending upon him. ﴿But when the fear departs﴾ means: when the fighting ceases and they are at ease, ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving﴾ — out of fear.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one fainting from death﴾: that is, out of awe and fright of it. As for His words ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾, He means: they bite you with sharp tongues. It is said of an eloquent man with a sharp tongue: a khatib musalliq and musallaq (a fluent orator), and khatib sallaq and sallaq.

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning in which Allah described these hypocrites as lashing the believers. Some said: that lashing is their assailing them at the time of booty, by demanding a share from them.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿But when the fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ — as for at the time of booty, they are the stingiest people and the worst in dividing; "Give us, give us, for we have witnessed with you." As for at the time of peril, they are the most cowardly people and the most forsaking of the truth.

Others said: Rather, that lashing of them is by harm.

Mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾: he said: "they confront you."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues﴾: he said: "they speak to you."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they lash them with speech of what you dislike, out of hypocrisy.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me: ﴿But when the fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ — in speech of what you dislike, because they do not hope for an afterlife, nor does reckoning move them; they dread death with the dread of one who does not hope for what comes after it.

The most fitting of these statements to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the view of one who said: ﴿they lash you with sharp tongues, being stingy toward good﴾. He informs that their lashing of the Muslims is out of stinginess regarding the booty and good. Thus, since that is so, it is known that it is for seeking the booty. And when this is their aim in seeking booty, the saying of one who said: its meaning is: they lash you with harm, is included, for their doing so is undoubtedly harmful to the believers.

* *

And His saying: ﴿being stingy toward good﴾

He says: stingy regarding the booty when the believers are victorious.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: Those whose description I have conveyed to you in these verses did not truly affirm Allah and His Messenger. Rather, they are people of disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿So Allah has nullified their deeds﴾ means: Allah has removed and voided the rewards of their deeds. It has been mentioned that the one described with this attribute was one of the people of Badr, so Allah nullified his deed.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿So Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾: He said: My father told me that he was of the people of Badr, and that His words ﴿so Allah has nullified their deeds﴾ mean that Allah nullified his deed on the day of Badr.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and that is ever easy for Allah﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: And the nullifying of their deeds, which they had done before their apostasy and hypocrisy, was easy for Allah.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn; and if the confederates should come, they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins, asking about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.﴾ (33:20)

Almighty God says: These hypocrites think the confederates, who are Quraysh and Ghatafan, have not gone away.

As related to us:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me, concerning ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾: they are Quraysh and Ghatafan.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿have not withdrawn﴾:

It means: they have not departed, even though they had already departed, out of cowardice and terror of them.

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying, ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾, he said: They think them to be near.

It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: ﴿They think the confederates have already gone; but when they find them not gone, they wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿and if the confederates should come, they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾:

Almighty God says: And if the confederates come upon the believers, the confederates being the groups, singular hizb, ﴿they would wish﴾: they would long, out of fear and cowardice, to be absent from you in the desert among the Bedouins, out of fear of being killed. This is because His saying, ﴿that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾: one says, "So-and-so has become a badw (desert dweller)" when he goes into the desert, so he is yabdu, and he is badin. As for al-A'rab (the Bedouins), they are the plural of a'rabi, and the singular of al-Arab is 'arabi. It was only said a'rabi for the people of the desert, to distinguish between the people of the deserts and the people of the cities; so al-A'rab are assigned to the people of the desert, and al-Arab to the people of the settled towns.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿asking about your news﴾:

It means: these hypocrites inquire of you, O believers, of the people about your news, meaning: about your circumstances in the desert, whether Muhammad and his companions have been destroyed. We say: they wish to hear of your news of your destruction, and not to witness your battles with you. ﴿And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little﴾. Almighty God says to the believers: Even if they were also among you, they would not benefit you, and they would not fight the polytheists except a little, meaning: except for a show, because they do not fight them for the sake of God or in hope of reward.

Scholars of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying, ﴿asking about your news﴾, he said: your news. The reciters of all the major cities, except Asim al-Jahdari, read ﴿yas'alūna ʿan anbā'ikum﴾ (they ask about your news), meaning: they ask those people who come to them about the news of your army and your affairs. It is reported from Asim al-Jahdari that he used to read it as ﴿yassā'alūna﴾ with a doubled sin, meaning: they ask one another about it.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is what the reciters of the major cities have, since the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 21–22:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.﴾ (21) ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ (22)

The readers differed over the reading of His words ﴿uswah﴾ (pattern). The majority of the readers of the regional centres read it as ﴿iswah﴾ with a kasra on the alif, except ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, who read it with a damma, ﴿uswah﴾. Yahya ibn Wththab used to read this with a kasra, and he read His words ﴿Indeed, there was for you in them an excellent pattern﴾ with a damma. Both are dialectal forms.

It is mentioned that the kasra is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the damma is the dialect of Qays, who say ﴿uswah﴾ and ﴿ukhwah﴾ (brotherhood).

This is a rebuke from Allah to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his army in Medina, from among the believers in him. He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent pattern﴾, meaning: that you should follow him and be with him wherever he is, and not stay behind from him. ﴿For whoever hopes for Allah﴾ means: indeed, whoever hopes for Allah's reward and mercy in the Hereafter does not prefer his own self, but for him there is a pattern in him, in being with him wherever he is.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, he said: Then he turned to the believers and said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, that they should not prefer their own selves over his self, nor over a place where he is. ﴿And remembers Allah often﴾ means: and they remember Allah much in fear, hardship and ease.

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates﴾

meaning: when the believers in Allah and His Messenger witnessed the gatherings of the disbelievers, they said, in submission to the command of Allah and in certainty that this was the fulfilment of His promise to them, which He promised them with His words: ﴿Do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿near﴾, ﴿"This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly."﴾ So Allah praised them for their certainty and their submission to His command, and He said: The gathering of the confederates against them increased them only in faith in Allah and submission to His decree and command, and He granted them, through it, victory and triumph over the enemies.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates...﴾ the verse. He said: That is because Allah had said to them in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Do you think that you will enter Paradise...﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed, the help of Allah is near.﴾ He said: So when hardship touched them, when they bound themselves against the confederates in the trench, the believers interpreted that, and it did not increase them except in faith and submission.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, he said: Then he mentioned the believers, their truthfulness, and their affirmation of what Allah had promised them of trial with which He would test them, ﴿They said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission﴾: that is, patience upon trial, submission to the decree, and affirmation of the fulfilment of what Allah and His Messenger had promised them.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly."﴾ Allah had promised them in Surat al-Baqarah, saying: (Do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? They were touched by misfortune and adversity and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.) He chose them, made them most patient, and most knowing of Allah. ﴿"When is the help of Allah? Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near."﴾ This, by Allah, was the trial and the severe hardship. When the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what afflicted them of hardship and trial, ﴿they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission﴾, in affirmation of what Allah had promised them, and in submission to the decree of Allah.
