Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 23–24:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who awaits, and they have not changed in the least.﴾ (33:23) ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (33:24)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Among the believers﴾ in God and His Messenger, ﴿are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾. That is, they fulfilled what they pledged to God regarding patience in hardship and adversity and at the time of battle. ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾: that is, among them is one who has finished the work that he vowed to God and obligated upon himself, so some were martyred on the day of Badr, some on the day of Uhud, and some in other battlefields. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ its fulfilment and completion, just as those who passed away before them fulfilled their pledge to God, awaiting God's help and victory over His enemy. And al-nahb (the vow) means "the vow" in the speech of the Arabs. Al-nahb also has other meanings in their speech, among them death, as the poet said:

"He fulfilled his nahb in the meeting of the people, Hawbar..." [[This is the second half of a verse by Dhu al-Rummah, whose first half is: "A life after which the Harithiyyun fled..."

Hawbar is the name of a man; he meant Ibn Hawbar (Lisan: h-b-r). Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an, regarding His saying "Among them is he who has fulfilled his nahb": that is, his vow which he had. Al-nahb also means the soul, i.e., death. Dhu al-Rummah said: "He fulfilled his nahb..." meaning his soul; and it is in fact Yazid ibn Hawbar, end quote. In the Diwan (Cambridge edition, 1919, p. 235) he meant Yazid ibn Hawbar, a man of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b.]]

That is: his appointed time and his soul. Another meaning is a great peril, as Jarir said:

"At Takhfah we fought the kings, and our horses, on the evening of Bistam, ran in nahb..." [[The verse is by Jarir ibn Atiyah ibn al-Khatafi (Abu 'Ubaydah, Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 174b), and in Lisan (n-h-b), he said: Jarir ibn al-Khatafi made it mean a great peril, saying "Takhfah..." the verse, meaning a great peril. Takhfah, with a fatha or kasra on the ta', is a long red mountain in the dwellings of the Banu Tamim. There was a battle there between the Banu Yarbu' and Qabus ibn al-Nu'man, for al-Nu'man had sent an army against them under his son Qabus and his brother Hassan. The Banu Yarbu' defeated them at Takhfah and captured both of them until they were granted freedom, and that is what Jarir meant (see Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri, Takhfah).]]

That is, in a great peril. Another meaning is al-nahib (lamentation); it is said: "He nahaba in his journey the whole day," when he pressed on and did not dismount throughout the day and night. Another meaning is al-tanhib, which is al-khatar (risking), as the poet said:

"When Kalb lamented over the people, which of them is more worthy of the crown of the glorious, the heaped-up?" [[The verse is by al-Farazdaq (his Diwan, Sawi edition, Cairo, p. 759). Al-tanhib here is a verbal noun of nahaba, with the ha' doubled, meaning he shouted or called out intensely. The root sense of al-tanhib is persistence in something and devotion to it, not leaving it. The author took it to mean al-khatar, and perhaps he means risking oneself.]]

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Rumán told me: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾: that is, they fulfilled to God what they pledged to Him. ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾, that is, he finished his work, and returned to his Lord, like those who were martyred on the day of Badr and the day of Uhud. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ what God promised of His help and martyrdom, in keeping with what his companions had passed on.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: his pledge, so he was killed or lived. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ a day in which there is jihad, and then he fulfils his vow, so he is killed or is truthful in his meeting.

* Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: his pledge. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ — he said: a day in which there is fighting, and he is truthful in the encounter.

* He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mujahid: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: he died upon the covenant.

* He said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn so-and-so — he named him, but his name has escaped me — from his father: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: his vow.

* Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from his paternal uncle 'Isa ibn Talhah: that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him: "Who are those who have fulfilled their vows?" He turned away from him; then he asked again, and he turned away from him. Then Talhah entered from the door of the mosque, wearing two green garments, and he said: "This is one of those who have fulfilled their vows."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: his death upon truthfulness and fidelity. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ — death upon the like of that. And among them is he who has not changed in the least [[In al-Durr al-Manthur it is replaced by: "and others have not changed in the least."]].

* Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Mujahid: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow and among them is he who awaits﴾ — he said: al-nahb is the covenant.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — upon truthfulness and fidelity. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ from himself, truthfulness and fidelity.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾: he died upon what he was upon of confirmation and faith. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ that.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Sharik ibn 'Abdullah informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he said: death upon what he covenanted with God. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ — death upon what he covenanted with God.

It has also been said: this verse was revealed concerning a people who did not witness Badr, and they covenanted with God to fight the polytheists alongside the Messenger of God ﷺ. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 23–24:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who awaits, and they have not changed in the least.﴾ (33:23) ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (33:24)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Among the believers﴾ in God and His Messenger, ﴿are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾. That is, they fulfilled what they pledged to God regarding patience in hardship and adversity and at the time of battle. ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾: that is, among them is one who has finished the work that he vowed to God and obligated upon himself, so some were martyred on the day of Badr, some on the day of Uhud, and some in other battlefields. ﴿And among them is he who awaits﴾ its fulfilment and completion, just as those who passed away before them fulfilled their pledge to God, awaiting God's help and victory over His enemy. And al-nahb (the vow) means "the vow" in the speech of the Arabs. Al-nahb also has other meanings in their speech, among them death, as the poet said:

"He fulfilled his nahb in the meeting of the people, Hawbar..." [[This is the second half of a verse by Dhu al-Rummah, whose first half is: "A life after which the Harithiyyun fled..."

Hawbar is the name of a man; he meant Ibn Hawbar (Lisan: h-b-r). Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an, regarding His saying "Among them is he who has fulfilled his nahb": that is, his vow which he had. Al-nahb also means the soul, i.e., death. Dhu al-Rummah said: "He fulfilled his nahb..." meaning his soul; and it is in fact Yazid ibn Hawbar, end quote. In the Diwan (Cambridge edition, 1919, p. 235) he meant Yazid ibn Hawbar, a man of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b.]]

That is: his appointed time and his soul. Another meaning is a great peril, as Jarir said:

"At Takhfah we fought the kings, and our horses, on the evening of Bistam, ran in nahb..." [[The verse is by Jarir ibn Atiyah ibn al-Khatafi (Abu 'Ubaydah, Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 174b), and in Lisan (n-h-b), he said: Jarir ibn al-Khatafi made it mean a great peril, saying "Takhfah..." the verse, meaning a great peril. Takhfah, with a fatha or kasra on the ta', is a long red mountain in the dwellings of the Banu Tamim. There was a battle there between the Banu Yarbu' and Qabus ibn al-Nu'man, for al-Nu'man had sent an army against them under his son Qabus and his brother Hassan. The Banu Yarbu' defeated them at Takhfah and captured both of them until they were granted freedom, and that is what Jarir meant (see Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri, Takhfah).]]

That is, in a great peril. Another meaning is al-nahib (lamentation); it is said: "He nahaba in his journey the whole day," when he pressed on and did not dismount throughout the day and night. Another meaning is al-tanhib, which is al-khatar (risking), as the poet said:

"When Kalb lamented over the people, which of them is more worthy of the crown of the glorious, the heaped-up?" [[The verse is by al-Farazdaq (his Diwan, Sawi edition, Cairo, p. 759). Al-tanhib here is a verbal noun of nahaba, with the ha' doubled, meaning he shouted or called out intensely. The root sense of al-tanhib is persistence in something and devotion to it, not leaving it. The author took it to mean al-khatar, and perhaps he means risking oneself.]]

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and Allah is ever Strong and Mighty﴾: Strong in His command, Mighty in His vengeance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 26–27 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A party you killed, and a party you took captive.﴾ [26] ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.﴾ [27]

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And Allah brought down those who aided the confederates from Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. That is their supporting them. By this is meant the Banu Qurayzah, who were the ones who supported the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
* *
As for His words: ﴿of the People of the Scripture﴾
it means: of the People of the Torah, and they were Jews. As for His words: ﴿from their fortresses﴾ it means: from their strongholds.
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said about this.

Huyay ibn Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayzah in their fortress when Quraysh and Ghatafan had withdrawn from them, in fulfilment of his pledge to Ka'b ibn Asad. When they became certain that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not turn away from them until he engaged them, Ka'b ibn Asad said to them: O assembly of Jews, what has befallen you is what you see, and I offer you three options; choose one of them. They said: What are they? He said: We pledge allegiance to this man and affirm him, for by Allah it has become clear to you that he is indeed a prophet sent, and that he is the one you find in your Book, and you will be secure for your lives, your wealth, your sons and your women. They said: We will never leave the judgement of the Torah nor exchange it for anything else. He said: If you refuse this for me, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad and his Companions as men with drawn swords, leaving behind us no burden that concerns us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we perish, having left nothing behind that we fear for; and if we prevail, by my life, we will surely take other women and sons. They said: We would kill these poor ones? What good is life after them? He said: If you refuse this for me, then tonight is the night of Saturday, and it may be that Muhammad and his Companions feel secure, so come down, perhaps we may catch Muhammad and his Companions unawares. They said: Shall we desecrate our Sabbath and do in it what those before us did not do? Do you not know what befell them of transformation, which is not hidden from you? He said: Not a man of you has spent a single night since his mother bore him with resolve. Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Send us Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, — and they were allies of the Aws — that we may consult him about our affair. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him. When they saw him, the men rose to him, and the women and children came crying out in his face, and he was moved with pity for them. They said to him: O Abu Lubabah, do you think we should come down to the judgement of Muhammad? He said: Yes, and he gestured with his hand to his throat: it is slaughter. When the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had been slow to come, he said: "As for him, had he come to me I would have asked forgiveness for him. In that same night Amr ibn Sa'dah al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), over which Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari was that night. When he saw him, he said: Who is this? He said: Amr ibn Sa'dah. Amr had refused to join Banu Qurayzah in their treachery against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: I will never betray Muhammad. Muhammad ibn Maslamah, when he recognised him, said: O Allah, do not deprive me of the pardoning of the stumbles of the noble. Then he released him, and he went off straight ahead until he spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah. Then he left, and it is not known where he went in the land of Allah to this day. The matter of him was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "That is a man whom Allah saved through his fidelity." He said: Some people claimed that he had been bound with a rope among those of Banu Qurayzah who were bound when they came down to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and in the morning his rope was found lying loose, and it is not known where he went. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made that statement, and Allah knows best.
When they awoke, they came down to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Aws sprang up and said: O Messenger of Allah, they are our clients apart from the Khazraj, and you have done with the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge concerning them?" They said: Yes. He said: "Then it is up to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the tent of a woman of Aslam called Rufaydah, in his mosque, who tended the wounded, and counted her own self in the service of whoever among the Muslims was afflicted with loss. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to his people when an arrow struck him at the Trench: "Place him in the tent of Rufaydah until I visit him soon." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him as judge over Banu Qurayzah, his people came to him, lifted him onto a donkey, having spread for him a cushion of leather, for he was a large man, and they came with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with this so that you would be good to them. When they pressed him, he said: The time has come for Sa'd that he should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. Some of those who were with him from his people returned to the house of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, and the men of Banu Qurayzah reported to them the words they had heard from him before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them. When Sa'd reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, he said: "Rise for your chief." So they rose to him and said: O Abu Amr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with your clients so that you judge concerning them. Sa'd said: Upon you is the covenant and pledge of Allah, that the judgement concerning them is as I judge? They said: Yes. He said: And upon whoever is here? — in the direction where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, while he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of reverence for him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes." Sa'd said: I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the offspring and women be taken captive.

As for His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾
He means: and He cast into their hearts fear of you, ﴿a party you slew﴾, meaning you killed a group of them, namely those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed when he gained the upper hand over them, ﴿and a party you made captive﴾, meaning you took captive a group of them, namely their women and children who were taken as captives.
As has been related:
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿a party you slew﴾ those whose necks were struck, ﴿and a party you made captive﴾ those who were taken captive.

As for His saying: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾
The exegetes differed concerning it: what land is it? Some said: it is Rome, Persia and the like of the lands which Allah afterward opened for the Muslims.
Mention of those who said that:
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾ He said: al-Hasan said: it is Rome and Persia, and what Allah opened for them.
Others said: it is Makkah.
And others said: rather, it is Khaybar.
Mention of those who said that:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾ He said: Khaybar.
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land and their homes﴾: Qurayzah and al-Nadir, the People of the Book. ﴿And a land you had not trodden﴾: Khaybar.
The correct view on this matter is that it is said: Allah, mighty is His mention, informed that He caused the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to inherit the land of Banu Qurayzah, their homes and their wealth, and a land they had not trodden on that day, and it was neither Makkah nor Khaybar, nor the land of Persia and Rome, nor Yemen, of what they had trodden on that day; then they trod upon that afterward, and Allah caused them to inherit it. All of that falls under His saying ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾, because He, mighty is His mention, did not single out some of it over others. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ He, mighty is His mention, says: Allah was competent to cause the believers to inherit that, and to grant them victory, and other matters, with power; nothing He willed is beyond Him, and nothing He attempted to do is out of His reach.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 26–27 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A party you killed, and a party you took captive.﴾ [26] ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.﴾ [27]

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And Allah brought down those who aided the confederates from Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. That is their supporting them. By this is meant the Banu Qurayzah, who were the ones who supported the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

When they became certain that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not turn away from them until he engaged them, Ka'b ibn Asad said to them: O assembly of Jews, what has befallen you is what you see, and I offer you three options; choose one of them. They said: What are they? He said: We pledge allegiance to this man and affirm him, for by Allah it has become clear to you that he is indeed a prophet sent, and that he is the one you find in your Book, and you will be secure for your lives, your wealth, your sons and your women. They said: We will never leave the judgement of the Torah nor exchange it for anything else. He said: If you refuse this for me, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad and his Companions as men with drawn swords, leaving behind us no burden that concerns us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we perish, having left nothing behind that we fear for; and if we prevail, by my life, we will surely take other women and sons. They said: We would kill these poor ones? What good is life after them? He said: If you refuse this for me, then tonight is the night of Saturday, and it may be that Muhammad and his Companions feel secure, so come down, perhaps we may catch Muhammad and his Companions unawares. They said: Shall we desecrate our Sabbath and do in it what those before us did not do? Do you not know what befell them of transformation, which is not hidden from you? He said: Not a man of you has spent a single night since his mother bore him with resolve. Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Send us Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, — and they were allies of the Aws — that we may consult him about our affair. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him. When they saw him, the men rose to him, and the women and children came crying out in his face, and he was moved with pity for them. They said to him: O Abu Lubabah, do you think we should come down to the judgement of Muhammad? He said: Yes, and he gestured with his hand to his throat: it is slaughter. Abu Lubabah said: By Allah, my feet had not moved before I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger. Then Abu Lubabah set off straight ahead. He did not come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he had tied himself to a pillar of the pillars in the mosque, and said: I will not leave my place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I did, and I pledge to Allah that I will never tread the land of Banu Qurayzah, nor let Allah see me in a land where I betrayed Allah and His Messenger. When the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had been slow to come, he said: "As for him, had he come to me I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done what he has done, I am not the one who will release him from his place until Allah accepts his repentance." Then Tha'labah ibn Sa'yah, Usayd ibn Sa'yah, and Asad ibn Ubayd, who were a group from the Banu Hudhayl, not of Banu Qurayzah nor of al-Nadir, but of a higher lineage, being cousins of the people, became Muslims on the night when Qurayzah came down to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In that same night Amr ibn Sa'dah al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), over which Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari was that night. When he saw him, he said: Who is this? He said: Amr ibn Sa'dah. Amr had refused to join Banu Qurayzah in their treachery against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: I will never betray Muhammad. Muhammad ibn Maslamah, when he recognised him, said: O Allah, do not deprive me of the pardoning of the stumbles of the noble. Then he released him, and he went off straight ahead until he spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah. Then he left, and it is not known where he went in the land of Allah to this day. The matter of him was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "That is a man whom Allah saved through his fidelity." He said: Some people claimed that he had been bound with a rope among those of Banu Qurayzah who were bound when they came down to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and in the morning his rope was found lying loose, and it is not known where he went. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made that statement, and Allah knows best.
When they awoke, they came down to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Aws sprang up and said: O Messenger of Allah, they are our clients apart from the Khazraj, and you have done with the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had, before Banu Qurayzah, besieged Banu Qaynuqa', who were allies of the Khazraj, and they came down to his judgement, and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him for them, and he gave them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge concerning them?" They said: Yes. He said: "Then it is up to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the tent of a woman of Aslam called Rufaydah, in his mosque, who tended the wounded, and counted her own self in the service of whoever among the Muslims was afflicted with loss. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to his people when an arrow struck him at the Trench: "Place him in the tent of Rufaydah until I visit him soon." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him as judge over Banu Qurayzah, his people came to him, lifted him onto a donkey, having spread for him a cushion of leather, for he was a large man, and they came with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with this so that you would be good to them. When they pressed him, he said: The time has come for Sa'd that he should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. Some of those who were with him from his people returned to the house of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, and the men of Banu Qurayzah reported to them the words they had heard from him before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them. When Sa'd reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, he said: "Rise for your chief." So they rose to him and said: O Abu Amr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with your clients so that you judge concerning them. Sa'd said: Upon you is the covenant and pledge of Allah, that the judgement concerning them is as I judge? They said: Yes. He said: And upon whoever is here? — in the direction where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, while he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of reverence for him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes." Sa'd said: I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the offspring and women be taken captive.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have judged among them by the judgement of Allah from above seven heavens." Then they were brought down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confined them in the house of the daughter of al-Harith, a woman of the Banu al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market of Madinah, which is its market today, and dug trenches in it, then sent for them, and struck their necks in those trenches. They were brought out to him in groups, and among them was the enemy of Allah, Huyay ibn Akhtab, and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six or seven hundred; the one who gave the highest count said they were between eight and nine hundred. When they were being led to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in groups, they said to Ka'b ibn Asad: O Ka'b, what do you think will be done with us? Ka'b said: Will you not understand in every situation? Do you not see that the summoner does not turn back, and whoever among you is led away does not return? By Allah, it is death. So that continued until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished with them. Huyay ibn Akhtab, the enemy of Allah, was brought, wearing a garment of his, of a light yellow colour, which had been slit by him from every side, like the joint of a finger, finger by finger, so that it would not be stripped from him; his hands were bound to his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: As for me, by Allah, I did not blame myself for enmity to you, but whoever is forsaken by Allah is forsaken. Then he turned to the people and said: O people, there is no harm in the command of Allah; the Book of Allah and His decree, and a slaughter that was written for the Children of Israel. Then he sat down and his neck was struck. Jabal ibn Jawwal al-Tha'labi said:
By your life, Ibn Akhtab did not blame himself,
but whoever is forsaken by Allah is forsaken.
He struggled until he gave the soul its excuse,
and shook off every shaker who sought glory.[[The two verses are by Jabal ibn Jawwal al-Tha'labi, of the Banu Tha'labah ibn Sa'd ibn Dhubyan ibn Baghid ibn Rith ibn Ghatafan; he was a Jew who became Muslim, and he had companionship with the Prophet (see al-Rawd al-Anf of al-Suhayli and al-Isti'ab of Ibn Abd al-Barr; and see Ibn Hisham's Sirah, Halabi edition: 3: 252). The meaning of qalqala: moved. He recited the two verses at the death of Huyay ibn Akhtab, chief of Banu Qurayzah.]]
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from A'ishah, who said: Only one woman of their women was killed. She said: By Allah, she was with me, conversing with me and laughing at midday, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was killing their men in the market. Then a caller called out her name: Where is so-and-so? She said: I am, by Allah. I said: Woe to you, what is wrong with you? She said: Am I to be killed? I said: Why? She said: For a deed I committed. He said: So she was taken away and her neck was struck. A'ishah used to say: I never forget my wonder at her, her cheerful spirit and her much laughter, though she knew she was to be killed.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Zayd ibn Ruman narrated to me, regarding ﴿And He brought down those who supported them of the People of the Scripture from their fortresses﴾: the sayasi are the fortresses and towers in which they dwelt. ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾.
⁕ Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri narrated to us, saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿from their fortresses﴾: He said: from their strongholds.
⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from their fortresses﴾: He said: He brought them down from their fortresses; he said: their palaces.
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿from their fortresses﴾: that is, from their strongholds and their towers.
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And He brought down those who supported them of the People of the Scripture from their fortresses﴾: The sayasi are their fortresses which they thought would protect them from Allah, blessed and exalted is He. The root of sayasi is the plural of sayṣah, it is said: and by it here is meant their fortresses. The Arabs say of the edge of a mountain: sayṣah, and of the root of a thing: sayṣah; it is said: "May Allah cut off the sayṣah of so-and-so," meaning his root. And the thorn of weavers is called sayasi, as the poet said:
"Like the striking of the sayasi in the stretched weave"[[This is the second half of a verse by Durayd ibn al-Simmah, whose first half is: "So I came to him while the spears were tearing at him."
(Lisan al-Arab: s-y-s). Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 194a, at His words (from their sayasi): that is, from their fortresses and their roots. It is also the thorn of weavers, he said: "Like the striking of the sayasi in the stretched weave."]]

Or the two spurs of the cock; it is also a horn of the cow. End of quote. In (Lisan al-Arab, entry ṣ-y-ṣ): al-ṣayṣa is the weaver's shuttle-spike with which the warp and weft are smoothed; Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma said: "I came to him..." (the verse). From the same root: ṣaysat al-dik, which is in its leg, and ṣayāṣī al-baqar, their horns. Sometimes they were fitted onto spears in place of the spearheads. And al-ṣayāṣī means fortresses, and everything one holds on to and fortifies oneself with is a ṣayṣiya; from this, fortresses are called ṣayāṣī.]]
Or the two spurs of the cock.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾
He means: and He cast into their hearts fear of you, ﴿a party you slew﴾, meaning you killed a group of them, namely those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed when he gained the upper hand over them, ﴿and a party you made captive﴾, meaning you took captive a group of them, namely their women and children who were taken as captives.
As has been related:
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿a party you slew﴾ those whose necks were struck, ﴿and a party you made captive﴾ those who were taken captive.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me: ﴿a party you slew and a party you made captive﴾, i.e., the men were killed and the offspring and women were taken captive. ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth﴾, meaning: and He made you possessors after their destruction of their land, meaning their farms and plantations and their homes, meaning their dwellings and their wealth, meaning all wealth other than land and houses.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾
The exegetes differed concerning it: what land is it? Some said: it is Rome, Persia and the like of the lands which Allah afterward opened for the Muslims.
Mention of those who said that:
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾ He said: al-Hasan said: it is Rome and Persia, and what Allah opened for them.
Others said: it is Makkah.
And others said: rather, it is Khaybar.
Mention of those who said that:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me: ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾ He said: Khaybar.
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land and their homes﴾: Qurayzah and al-Nadir, the People of the Book. ﴿And a land you had not trodden﴾: Khaybar.
The correct view on this matter is that it is said: Allah, mighty is His mention, informed that He caused the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to inherit the land of Banu Qurayzah, their homes and their wealth, and a land they had not trodden on that day, and it was neither Makkah nor Khaybar, nor the land of Persia and Rome, nor Yemen, of what they had trodden on that day; then they trod upon that afterward, and Allah caused them to inherit it. All of that falls under His saying ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾, because He, mighty is His mention, did not single out some of it over others. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ He, mighty is His mention, says: Allah was competent to cause the believers to inherit that, and to grant them victory, and other matters, with power; nothing He willed is beyond Him, and nothing He attempted to do is out of His reach.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 33, verses 28–29:

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release. (28) But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾ (29)

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you﴾ means: I will give you the provision (mut'ah) which Allah has made obligatory upon men for women when they separate from them by divorce, by His saying: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision in kindness, a duty upon the doers of good.﴾ And His saying ﴿and release you in a graceful release﴾ means: and I will set you free in accordance with what Allah has permitted and taught His servants by His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time.﴾ ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: if you desire the pleasure of Allah, the pleasure of His Messenger and their obedience, then obey them. ﴿Indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾ — and they are those among them who act in accordance with the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger — ﴿a great reward.﴾

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because 'Aisha asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for something of the goods of this world, either an increase in maintenance or something else, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives for a month, as is related. Then Allah commanded him to give them the choice between patience with him and contentment with what was apportioned to them, and acting in obedience to Allah, or to provide for them and part from them if they would not be content with what was apportioned to them. It was also said: the cause of this was jealousy which 'Aisha felt.

Mention of the narration by those who said: it was on account of some matter of maintenance and other things.

• Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out [for prayer], and they said: What is the matter with him? 'Umar said: If you wish, I will find out for you what his matter is. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began to say to myself: what word can I speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that perhaps he will laugh, or something similar? I said: O Messenger of Allah, if you saw so-and-so, and she asked me for maintenance, and I slapped her with a slap. He said: "That is what kept me from you." He said: Then he went to Hafsah and said: Do not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything; whatever need you have, come to me. Then he followed the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, speaking to them, and he said to 'Aisha: Does it delude you that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you? You shall desist, or the Qur'an will be revealed concerning you. He said: Umm Salamah said: O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you but to interpose between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wives? A woman asks only of her husband. He said: And the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ He said: So he began with 'Aisha and gave her the choice, and recited the Qur'an to her. She said: Have you begun with any of your wives before me? He said: "No." She said: Then I choose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, and do not inform them of that. He said: Then he followed them. He began giving them the choice and reciting the Qur'an to them, informing them of what 'Aisha had done, and they followed suit.

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ He said: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: He gave them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and Paradise and Hellfire, concerning something which they had desired from this world. And 'Ikrimah said: it was out of jealousy which 'Aisha felt. Under him at that time were nine wives: five from Quraysh: 'Aisha, Hafsah, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, and Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah. And under him were Safiyyah bint Huyayy of Khaybar, Maymunah bint al-Harith of the Hilal, Zaynab bint Jahsh of the Asad, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq. He began with 'Aisha, and when she chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they all followed suit, choosing Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode.

• Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, and this is the saying of Qatadah, concerning the saying of Allah ﷺ ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ Both said: Allah commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and Paradise and Hellfire. Qatadah said: and it was jealousy from 'Aisha concerning something she desired from this world. Under him were nine wives: 'Aisha, Hafsah, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq, and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. He began with 'Aisha, and she was the most beloved of them to him. When they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they followed suit.

• Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, and this is the saying of Qatadah, who said: When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that, saying ﴿Women are not lawful for you hereafter, nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty pleases you﴾ — He restricted it to them, and they were the nine who chose Allah and His Messenger.

Mention of those who said that it was on account of jealousy:

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will…﴾ the verse. He said: His wives had been jealous of the Prophet ﷺ, so he abandoned them for a month. The giving of choice from Allah to him concerning them was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ and he recited until he reached ﴿and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. So he gave them the choice between choosing to be released and divorced, or to remain, if they desired Allah and His Messenger, on condition that they be Mothers of the Believers, never to marry again, and on condition that he may take to himself whom he will of them, for whoever gives herself to him, until he himself raises his head toward her, and puts off whom he will until he himself raises his head toward her; and whoever he seeks from among those with him, and whoever he sets aside, there is no blame upon him. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they not grieve, and that they may be content﴾ when they know that it is from My decree concerning them, the preference of some of them over others. ﴿More suitable that they may be content.﴾ He said: ﴿And whoever you seek from among those you have set aside﴾ — whoever he seeks, he attains; and whoever he sets aside, he does not attain. So he gave them the choice, between being content with this or being parted from them, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, except one woman, a Bedouin, who went away. He was upon this, and this condition had been stipulated for him, and he continued to act equitably among them until he met Allah.

• Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi related to us, he said: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aisha said: When the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "I wish to mention to you a matter, and do not decide on it until you consult your two parents." She said: I said: And what is it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: and he recited it to her. She said: What is it, O Messenger of Allah? He recited to them ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ to the end of the verse. She said: I said: Rather, we choose Allah and His Messenger. She said: The Prophet ﷺ was delighted by that.

• Ibn Wakī' related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aisha, who said: When the verse of the option was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ began with 'Aisha and said: "O 'Aisha, I am presenting to you a matter, so do not act upon it in anything until you consult your two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Rumman." She said: O Messenger of Allah, what is it? He said: "Allah said ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ up to ﴿a great reward.﴾" She said: I said: I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, and I will not consult my two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Rumman, in that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then he asked the chambers to recite, and said: "'Aisha said such-and-such." They said: We too say the same as what 'Aisha said.

• Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amrah, from 'Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he came down to his wives, was commanded to give them the choice. He entered upon me and said: "I will mention to you a matter, and do not hasten until you consult your father." I said: And what is it, O Prophet of Allah? He said: "I have been commanded to give you the choice." And he recited to her the verse of the option, to the end of the two verses. She said: I said: And what is it you say? "Do not hasten until you consult your father?" Indeed I choose Allah and His Messenger. He was pleased by that, and presented it to his wives, and they all followed suit, and chose Allah and His Messenger.

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Musa ibn 'Ali and Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, he said: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that 'Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: "I am mentioning to you a matter, and there is no harm to you in not hastening until you consult your two parents." She said: He knew that my two parents would never have commanded me to part from him. She said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release.﴾ She said: I said: Then concerning which of these should I consult my two parents? Indeed I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode. 'Aisha said: Then the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did as I did, and that was not on the occasion when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said it to them; and they chose it as a divorce, because they had chosen it.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 33, verses 28–29:

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release. (28) But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾ (29)

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you﴾ means: I will give you the provision (mut'ah) which Allah has made obligatory upon men for women when they separate from them by divorce, by His saying: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision in kindness, a duty upon the doers of good.﴾ And His saying ﴿and release you in a graceful release﴾ means: and I will set you free in accordance with what Allah has permitted and taught His servants by His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time.﴾ ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: if you desire the pleasure of Allah, the pleasure of His Messenger and their obedience, then obey them. ﴿Indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾ — and they are those among them who act in accordance with the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger — ﴿a great reward.﴾

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because 'Aisha asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for something of the goods of this world, either an increase in maintenance or something else, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives for a month, as is related. Then Allah commanded him to give them the choice between patience with him and contentment with what was apportioned to them, and acting in obedience to Allah, or to provide for them and part from them if they would not be content with what was apportioned to them. It was also said: the cause of this was jealousy which 'Aisha felt.

Mention of the narration by those who said: it was on account of some matter of maintenance and other things.

• Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out [for prayer], and they said: What is the matter with him? 'Umar said: If you wish, I will find out for you what his matter is. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began to say to myself: what word can I speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that perhaps he will laugh, or something similar? I said: O Messenger of Allah, if you saw so-and-so, and she asked me for maintenance, and I slapped her with a slap. He said: "That is what kept me from you." He said: Then he went to Hafsah and said: Do not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything; whatever need you have, come to me. Then he followed the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, speaking to them, and he said to 'Aisha: Does it delude you that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you? You shall desist, or the Qur'an will be revealed concerning you. He said: Umm Salamah said: O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you but to interpose between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wives? A woman asks only of her husband. He said: And the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ He said: So he began with 'Aisha and gave her the choice, and recited the Qur'an to her. She said: Have you begun with any of your wives before me? He said: "No." She said: Then I choose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, and do not inform them of that. He said: Then he followed them. He began giving them the choice and reciting the Qur'an to them, informing them of what 'Aisha had done, and they followed suit.

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ He said: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: He gave them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and Paradise and Hellfire, concerning something which they had desired from this world. And 'Ikrimah said: it was out of jealousy which 'Aisha felt. Under him at that time were nine wives: five from Quraysh: 'Aisha, Hafsah, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, and Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah. And under him were Safiyyah bint Huyayy of Khaybar, Maymunah bint al-Harith of the Hilal, Zaynab bint Jahsh of the Asad, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq. He began with 'Aisha, and when she chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they all followed suit, choosing Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode.

• Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, and this is the saying of Qatadah, concerning the saying of Allah ﷺ ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾ up to His saying ﴿a great reward.﴾ Both said: Allah commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and Paradise and Hellfire. Qatadah said: and it was jealousy from 'Aisha concerning something she desired from this world. Under him were nine wives: 'Aisha, Hafsah, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq, and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. He began with 'Aisha, and she was the most beloved of them to him. When they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they followed suit.

• Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, and this is the saying of Qatadah, who said: When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that, saying ﴿Women are not lawful for you hereafter, nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty pleases you﴾ — He restricted it to them, and they were the nine who chose Allah and His Messenger.

Mention of those who said that it was on account of jealousy:

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will…﴾ the verse. He said: His wives had been jealous of the Prophet ﷺ, so he abandoned them for a month. The giving of choice from Allah to him concerning them was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ and he recited until he reached ﴿and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. So he gave them the choice between choosing to be released and divorced, or to remain, if they desired Allah and His Messenger, on condition that they be Mothers of the Believers, never to marry again, and on condition that he may take to himself whom he will of them, for whoever gives herself to him, until he himself raises his head toward her, and puts off whom he will until he himself raises his head toward her; and whoever he seeks from among those with him, and whoever he sets aside, there is no blame upon him. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they not grieve, and that they may be content﴾ when they know that it is from My decree concerning them, the preference of some of them over others. ﴿More suitable that they may be content.﴾ He said: ﴿And whoever you seek from among those you have set aside﴾ — whoever he seeks, he attains; and whoever he sets aside, he does not attain. So he gave them the choice, between being content with this or being parted from them, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, except one woman, a Bedouin, who went away. He was upon this, and this condition had been stipulated for him, and he continued to act equitably among them until he met Allah.

• Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi related to us, he said: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aisha said: When the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "I wish to mention to you a matter, and do not decide on it until you consult your two parents." She said: I said: And what is it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: and he recited it to her. She said: What is it, O Messenger of Allah? He recited to them ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ to the end of the verse. She said: I said: Rather, we choose Allah and His Messenger. She said: The Prophet ﷺ was delighted by that.

• Ibn Wakī' related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aisha, who said: When the verse of the option was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ began with 'Aisha and said: "O 'Aisha, I am presenting to you a matter, so do not act upon it in anything until you consult your two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Rumman." She said: O Messenger of Allah, what is it? He said: "Allah said ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ up to ﴿a great reward.﴾" She said: I said: I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, and I will not consult my two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Rumman, in that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then he asked the chambers to recite, and said: "'Aisha said such-and-such." They said: We too say the same as what 'Aisha said.

• Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amrah, from 'Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he came down to his wives, was commanded to give them the choice. He entered upon me and said: "I will mention to you a matter, and do not hasten until you consult your father." I said: And what is it, O Prophet of Allah? He said: "I have been commanded to give you the choice." And he recited to her the verse of the option, to the end of the two verses. She said: I said: And what is it you say? "Do not hasten until you consult your father?" Indeed I choose Allah and His Messenger. He was pleased by that, and presented it to his wives, and they all followed suit, and chose Allah and His Messenger.

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Musa ibn 'Ali and Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, he said: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that 'Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: "I am mentioning to you a matter, and there is no harm to you in not hastening until you consult your two parents." She said: He knew that my two parents would never have commanded me to part from him. She said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release.﴾ She said: I said: Then concerning which of these should I consult my two parents? Indeed I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode. 'Aisha said: Then the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did as I did, and that was not on the occasion when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said it to them; and they chose it as a divorce, because they had chosen it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an clearly indecent act, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ (33:30)

Exalted is He, says to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an clearly indecent act﴾, meaning: whoever of you commits well-known fornication (zina) for which Allah has prescribed the hadd (the prescribed legal penalty), ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her﴾ for her immorality in the Hereafter, ﴿twofold﴾ compared to the immorality of other people's wives.

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾, he said: it means the punishment of the Hereafter.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the major cities recited ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ (يُضَاعَفْ) with an alif, except Abu Amr, who recited it as ﴿yuḍaʿʿaf﴾ (يُضَعَّفْ) with a doubled ʿayn, interpreting it as the doubling of a thing once, meaning that a thing becomes two things. So, according to him, the meaning of the statement is: the punishment of whoever of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ commits a clearly indecent act, in this world and the Hereafter, is made double the punishment of all other women besides them. He says that ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ means that the thing is made to have its double added to it, until it becomes three times as much. So the meaning of whoever recites ﴿yudaʿaf﴾, in his view, is that her punishment is three times the punishment of other women who are not wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Therefore he chose ﴿yuḍaʿʿaf﴾ over ﴿yudaʿaf﴾. Others who recited ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ rejected this, saying: we do not know any difference between ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ and ﴿yuḍaʿʿaf﴾.

The correct recitation in this matter is what the reciters of the major cities follow, namely ﴿yudaʿaf﴾. As for the interpretation that Abu Amr adopted, it is an interpretation that we know no scholar to have claimed other than him, and other than Abu Ubayda Mamar ibn al-Muthanna. It is not permissible to oppose what the proof has come with, on which there is consensus, with an interpretation that has no evidence from a direction to which submission is required.

And His saying: ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾

Exalted is He says: the doubling of the punishment upon those of them who do that is ever ﴿easy for Allah﴾, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her an honorable provision.﴾

Exalted is He says: Whoever of you obeys Allah and His Messenger, and acts by what Allah has commanded; ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾ means: Allah will give her the reward for her deed, twice the reward of the deeds of other women among the rest of mankind's women. ﴿And We have prepared for her an honorable provision﴾ means: We have prepared for her in the Hereafter a pleasant life in Paradise. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger...﴾ the verse, meaning: from "whoever of you obeys Allah and His Messenger" to the end of the report is missing from the original, and it is in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (5: 196), ﴿and does righteousness﴾: fasts and prays.

Salm ibn Janadah narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, he said: I asked Amir about qunut, and he said: "And what is it?" I said: [He recited] ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾. He said: "Obedient." I said: [He recited] ﴿Whoever of you is obedient (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger﴾. He said: "She obeys."

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: whoever of you obeys Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and We have prepared for her an honorable provision﴾, which is Paradise.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿and does [taʿmal] righteousness﴾. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra recited ﴿wa-taʿmal﴾ with the letter "ta" (taʿmal), in agreement with the interpretation of the one (feminine) referred to after His saying ﴿minkunna﴾ (of you, feminine plural). Some transmitted from the Arabs that they say: "How many slave-girls were sold to you?" and that if they put the slave-girl first, they say: "How many slave-girls were sold to you?" – making the verb feminine after "slave-girl," while the verb in both constructions refers to "you" and not to the slave-girl. Al-Farra' mentioned that some Arabs recited to him:

O Umm Amr, whoever has in the center of his dwelling
A open space of 'Adi, eating the insects,
And his forehead turns black from the scorching of the hot winds,
And he is wounded if he has... [dhawi bakarat]

Then he said: "in kana dhawi" was not stated as "in kana" [but] "wa in kanu," which is how one who returns it to the meaning speaks. As for the people of Kufa, the majority of their reciters recited ﴿wa-ya'mal﴾ with the letter "ya" (ya'mal), in coordination with "yaqnut," since all of them in the reading with "ya" are in that form. The correct position on this is that both are well-known recitations and established dialects in Arabic speech, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct. This is because the Arabs sometimes return the predicate of "man" to its wording, making it singular and masculine, and sometimes to its meaning, as the Most High said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. Can you make the deaf hear, although they do not reason? And among them are those who look at you﴾ — He made it plural once for the meaning and singular another time for the wording.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 32–33 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an honorable manner. And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women﴾, meaning, of the women of this community, ﴿if you fear Allah﴾, meaning, if you obey Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you.

As [reported]:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women﴾: meaning, of the women of this community.

* *

And His words: ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾
meaning: do not be yielding in speech to men in what the people of immorality among you desire.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:
* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech﴾: he said, do not be lenient in speech, and do not be yielding in words.
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾: "Khada' al-qawl (yielding speech) is what is disliked of women's speech to men, which enters into men's hearts."

* *

And His words: ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾
meaning: lest one in whose heart is weakness should covet. Because of the weakness of his faith in his heart, he is either doubtful about Islam, a hypocrite, and therefore, because of that, he treats the limits of Allah lightly, or he is negligent in committing immoralities.

The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: He only described him as having a disease in his heart because he is a hypocrite.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾: he said, hypocrisy.

Others said: Rather, He described him with that because they desire to commit immoralities.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾: he said, "Ikrimah said: the desire for fornication."

* *

And His words: ﴿but speak in an honorable manner﴾
meaning: and speak a speech which Allah has permitted you and made lawful for you.

As [reported]:
* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿but speak in an honorable manner﴾: "A beautiful, good speech, honorable in goodness."

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words, ﴿And remain (waqarna) in your houses﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and some of the Kufans recited it ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ with a fatha on the qaf, meaning: "wa-qarna" (and remain), as if the one who recited it this way dropped the first ra' of iqrarna, which is fatha, then transferred its vowel to the qaf, as it is said ﴿فظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ (so you remained [and began] to marvel), meaning fazallatum: he dropped the first lam, which is kasra, then transferred its kasra to the zha'. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it ﴿وَقِرْنَ﴾ with a kasra on the qaf, meaning: be people of dignity (waqar) and tranquillity in your houses.

This recitation, with the kasra on the qaf, is more correct in our view, because if it is from waqar (dignity), as we have chosen, then there is no doubt that the recitation is with a kasra on the qaf, because it is said: waqara fulan fi manzilihi, fa-huwa yaqiru waqaran (so-and-so was dignified in his home, and he is dignified), so the qaf is kasra in the form yafil. When the imperative is formed from it, it is said: qir, as one says from wazana yazinu: zin, and from wa'ada ya'idu: 'id. If it is from qarar (settling), then the correct form would be iqrarna. Because those Arabs who say zalltu af'alu kadha and ahsastu bikadha, dropping the middle radical and transferring its vowel to the first radical in fa'ala, fa'alna and fa'altum, do not do that in the imperative and prohibition; one does not say zal qa'iman, nor tazal qa'iman. Therefore, the reasoning of the one who argues for the validity of the fatha on the qaf in this is not supported by the Arabs' saying in zalalta and ahsastu: zalat and ahsat, with a reason that necessitates its validity according to the reason you have described. Some have related from one of the Bedouins, heard from him: yanhatin min al-jabal (they descend from the mountain), meaning yanhatituna; if that is sound, it is closer to being a proof for the people of this recitation than the other argument.

* *

And His words: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾

It has been said: tabarruj in this context means swaggering and coquetry.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾: meaning, when you leave your houses. He said: they had a gait, coquetry and flirtatiousness. By this He meant the first ignorance, so Allah forbade them from that.
* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His words, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾: he said, swaggering.

It has also been said that tabarruj is the display of adornment and a woman's showing her beauties to men.

As for His words, ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance (al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾, the exegetes differed regarding "the first ignorance." Some of them said: it is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Zakariya, from 'Amir, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said, the first ignorance is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

Others said: it is what was between Adam and Nuh.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hakam, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said, there were eight hundred years between Adam and Nuh, and their women were among the ugliest of women, while their men were handsome. So a woman would seek a man for herself, and so this verse was revealed: ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾.

Others said: rather, it is between Nuh and Idris.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Zuhayr narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Dawud, meaning Ibn Abi al-Furat, narrated to us, saying: 'Alba' ibn Ahmar narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: he recited this verse, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾, and said: it was between Nuh and Idris, and it was a thousand years. Two tribes of the offspring of Adam, one of them dwelt in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, while the women were unattractive; the women of the plain were beautiful, while the men were unattractive. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth, hired himself out to him, and served him. Iblis made something similar to the instrument with which shepherds play, and he produced a sound the like of which had never been heard. This reached those around them, so they came to them to listen to it, and they made it a festival they gathered for once a year. The men displayed themselves to the women, and the women adorned themselves for the men. A man from the people of the mountain came upon them during their festival, saw the women, and went to his companions and informed them. So they moved toward the women, descended upon them, and immorality appeared among them. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾.

The most correct of the sayings in my view, regarding this, is that it should be said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, forbade the wives of the Prophet from displaying themselves as was the display of the first ignorance. It is permissible that this refers to what was between Adam and 'Isa, so the meaning would be: do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance that preceded Islam.

If someone says: Is there ignorance in Islam, so that it is said that by His words ﴿the first ignorance﴾ He meant that which preceded Islam? It is said: there are traits of ignorance within it.

As [reported]:
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said: He says, that which was before Islam. He said: Is there ignorance in Islam? He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Darda', and he said to a man who was contending with him: "O son of so-and-so's mother," by which he was reproaching him in the time of ignorance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Darda', there is ignorance in you." He said: Is it ignorance of disbelief or of Islam? He said: "Rather, ignorance of disbelief." He said: I wished that I had begun my Islam that day. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Three of the deeds of the people of ignorance, people will not abandon them: slandering lineages, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing."
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Thawr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him: What do you think of the saying of Allah to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾? Was there not only one [ignorance]? Ibn Abbas said: And was there any first [ignorance] except that it has a last? 'Umar said: May God grant you understanding, O Ibn Abbas, how did you say that? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, was there any first [ignorance] except that it has a last? He said: Then bring evidence confirming what you say from the Book of Allah. He said: Yes: ﴿and strive in Allah with the striving due to Him; He has chosen you...﴾ [with the reading: "as you fought the first time"]. [The manuscript has this reading, and it may be a reading of Ibn Abbas.] 'Umar said: Who was commanded to fight? He said: Two tribes of Quraysh: Makhzum and Banu 'Abd Shams. 'Umar said: You have spoken the truth.

It is permissible that this refers to what was between Adam and Nuh. It is also permissible that it refers to what was between Idris and Nuh, so that the last ignorance is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad. When this is something that the apparent sense of the revelation allows, the correct position is to say regarding it as Allah said: that He forbade the display of the first ignorance.

* *

And His words: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾
