meaning: and establish the obligatory prayer, and give the zakah obligatory upon you in your wealth. ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in what they command you and forbid you. ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾: meaning, Allah only intends to remove from you evil and indecency, O people of the household of Muhammad, and to purify you from the defilement that exists among the people of disobedience to Allah, [with] purification.

Ahl al-ta'wil said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾: they are the people of the household whom Allah purified from evil and singled out with His mercy.
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾: he said, the impurity here is Satan, and other than that of impurity is shirk.

The exegetes differed regarding those meant by His words, ﴿O people of the household﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them.

Mention of those who said that:
* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Zaban al-'Anazi narrated to us, saying: Mandal narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: concerning me, 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), and Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her): ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾."
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariya, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: 'A'ishah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out one morning, wearing a black woolen cloak with designs. Then al-Hasan came, so he brought him in with him, then said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾.
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pass by Fatimah's house for six months, every time he went out to prayer, saying: "The prayer, O people of the household: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾."
* Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Hilal, meaning Ibn Miqlas, from Zubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was with me, along with 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. I made a broth of khazirah for them, so they ate and slept. He covered them with a cloak or a blanket, then said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification."
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud informed me, from Abu al-Hamra', who said: I guarded Madinah for seven months during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ), when dawn broke, come to the door of 'Ali and Fatimah and say: "The prayer, the prayer," [and recited]: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾.
* 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, with his chain, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.
* 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Kulthum al-Muharibi, from Abu 'Ammar, who said: I was sitting with Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' when they mentioned 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and they reviled him. When they stood up, he said: Sit until I tell you about this one whom they reviled. I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn came to him, so he threw his cloak over them, then said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; O Allah, remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification." I said: O Messenger of Allah, and me? He said: "And you." He said: By Allah, it is indeed the most reliable of my deeds with me.
* 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to me, saying: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to me, who said: I heard Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' relate: I asked about 'Ali ibn Abi Talib at his house, and Fatimah said: He has gone to bring the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and I entered. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat on the bedding, seated Fatimah on his right, 'Ali on his left, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn in front of him. He wrapped them with his garment and said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾. "O Allah, these are my family; O Allah, my family have more right." Wathilah said: I said from the side of the house: And I, O Messenger of Allah, am I of your family? He said: "And you are of my family." Wathilah said: Indeed, it is among the most hopeful of what I hope for.
* Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from Umm Salamah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and covered them with a Khaybari cloak, and said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; O Allah, remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification." Umm Salamah said: Am I not among them? He said: "You are on the path to good."

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zurbi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umm Salamah, who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a cooking pot in which she had prepared 'asida (a porridge), and she placed it on a tray before him. He said: "Where is your cousin and your two sons?" She said: "In the house." He said: "Call them." So she went to Ali and said: "Answer the Prophet (ﷺ), you and your two sons." Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached out to a cloak that was on the sleeping place (al-minamah), spread it out, and seated them on it. Then he took the four corners of the cloak in his left hand and gathered it over their heads, and with his right hand he pointed toward his Lord, and said: "These are the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt). So remove from them the impurity (al-rijs) and purify them with a thorough purification."

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that this verse was revealed in her house: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. She said: I was sitting at the door of the house, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I not from the People of the House?" He said: "You are on the path of good; you are one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: In the house were the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them.

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Khalid ibn Mikhlad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn Hashim ibn 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas narrated to me, from 'Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, who said: Umm Salamah informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Ali and the two grandsons (al-Hasan and al-Husayn), then drew them under his garment, then cried out to Allah, and then said: "These are the People of my House (Ahl Bayti)." Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me enter with them." He said: "You are indeed of my family (Ahli)."

Narrated to me by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Isfahani narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Ubayd al-Makki, from 'Ata', from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the house of Umm Salamah: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. So he called al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah and seated them before him, and he called Ali and seated him behind him. Then he and they were covered with the cloak, and he said: "These are the People of my House. So remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification." Umm Salamah said: "I am with them in your place, and you are upon good." [[The phrase "I am with them in your place and you are upon good" is entirely the words of Umm Salamah, and it is parallel to the Prophet's (ﷺ) words to her in the narrations before this one: "You are on the path of good; you are one of the wives of the Prophet ..." etc. (See the nineteenth part of the manuscript no. 100 Tafsir at Dar al-Kutub, folio 60.)]]

Narrated to me by Muhammad ibn 'Umarah, who said: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muri narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a man from the people of Syria: "Did you not read in al-Ahzab: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾?" He said: "And are you they?" He said: "Yes."

Narrated to us by Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us, who said: I heard 'Amir ibn Sa'd, who said: Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when the revelation came down to him, and he took Ali, his two sons and Fatimah, and drew them under his garment, then said: "My Lord, these are my family and the People of my House."

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, in the presence of Umm Salamah, and she said: "It was concerning him that this was revealed: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾." Umm Salamah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to my house and said: "Do not permit anyone to enter." Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering upon her father. Then al-Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering upon his grandfather and his mother. Then al-Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered around the Prophet (ﷺ) on a rug, and the Prophet of Allah covered them with a cloak that he had on, then said: "These are the People of my House. So remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification." This verse was revealed when they had gathered on the rug. She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what about me?" She said: By Allah, he did not respond further, and he said: "You are upon good."

Others said: Rather, by this is meant the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh narrated to us, from 'Alqamah, who said: 'Ikrimah used to proclaim in the marketplace: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾, and he said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verses 32–33 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an honorable manner. And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women﴾, meaning, of the women of this community, ﴿if you fear Allah﴾, meaning, if you obey Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you.

As [reported]:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women﴾: meaning, of the women of this community.

* *

And His words: ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾
meaning: do not be yielding in speech to men in what the people of immorality among you desire.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:
* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech﴾: he said, do not be lenient in speech, and do not be yielding in words.
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾: "Khada' al-qawl (yielding speech) is what is disliked of women's speech to men, which enters into men's hearts."

* *

And His words: ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾
meaning: lest one in whose heart is weakness should covet. Because of the weakness of his faith in his heart, he is either doubtful about Islam, a hypocrite, and therefore, because of that, he treats the limits of Allah lightly, or he is negligent in committing immoralities.

The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: He only described him as having a disease in his heart because he is a hypocrite.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾: he said, hypocrisy.

Others said: Rather, He described him with that because they desire to commit immoralities.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾: he said, "Ikrimah said: the desire for fornication."

* *

And His words: ﴿but speak in an honorable manner﴾
meaning: and speak a speech which Allah has permitted you and made lawful for you.

As [reported]:
* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿but speak in an honorable manner﴾: "A beautiful, good speech, honorable in goodness."

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words, ﴿And remain (waqarna) in your houses﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and some of the Kufans recited it ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ with a fatha on the qaf, meaning: "wa-qarna" (and remain), as if the one who recited it this way dropped the first ra' of iqrarna, which is fatha, then transferred its vowel to the qaf, as it is said ﴿فظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ (so you remained [and began] to marvel), meaning fazallatum: he dropped the first lam, which is kasra, then transferred its kasra to the zha'. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it ﴿وَقِرْنَ﴾ with a kasra on the qaf, meaning: be people of dignity (waqar) and tranquillity in your houses.

This recitation, with the kasra on the qaf, is more correct in our view, because if it is from waqar (dignity), as we have chosen, then there is no doubt that the recitation is with a kasra on the qaf, because it is said: waqara fulan fi manzilihi, fa-huwa yaqiru waqaran (so-and-so was dignified in his home, and he is dignified), so the qaf is kasra in the form yafil. When the imperative is formed from it, it is said: qir, as one says from wazana yazinu: zin, and from wa'ada ya'idu: 'id. If it is from qarar (settling), then the correct form would be iqrarna. Because those Arabs who say zalltu af'alu kadha and ahsastu bikadha, dropping the middle radical and transferring its vowel to the first radical in fa'ala, fa'alna and fa'altum, do not do that in the imperative and prohibition; one does not say zal qa'iman, nor tazal qa'iman. Therefore, the reasoning of the one who argues for the validity of the fatha on the qaf in this is not supported by the Arabs' saying in zalalta and ahsastu: zalat and ahsat, with a reason that necessitates its validity according to the reason you have described. Some have related from one of the Bedouins, heard from him: yanhatin min al-jabal (they descend from the mountain), meaning yanhatituna; if that is sound, it is closer to being a proof for the people of this recitation than the other argument.

* *

And His words: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾

It has been said: tabarruj in this context means swaggering and coquetry.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾: meaning, when you leave your houses. He said: they had a gait, coquetry and flirtatiousness. By this He meant the first ignorance, so Allah forbade them from that.
* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His words, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾: he said, swaggering.

It has also been said that tabarruj is the display of adornment and a woman's showing her beauties to men.

As for His words, ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance (al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾, the exegetes differed regarding "the first ignorance." Some of them said: it is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Zakariya, from 'Amir, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said, the first ignorance is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

Others said: it is what was between Adam and Nuh.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hakam, regarding ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said, there were eight hundred years between Adam and Nuh, and their women were among the ugliest of women, while their men were handsome. So a woman would seek a man for herself, and so this verse was revealed: ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾.

Others said: rather, it is between Nuh and Idris.

Mention of those who said that:
* Ibn Zuhayr narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Dawud, meaning Ibn Abi al-Furat, narrated to us, saying: 'Alba' ibn Ahmar narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: he recited this verse, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾, and said: it was between Nuh and Idris, and it was a thousand years. Two tribes of the offspring of Adam, one of them dwelt in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, while the women were unattractive; the women of the plain were beautiful, while the men were unattractive. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth, hired himself out to him, and served him. Iblis made something similar to the instrument with which shepherds play, and he produced a sound the like of which had never been heard. This reached those around them, so they came to them to listen to it, and they made it a festival they gathered for once a year. The men displayed themselves to the women, and the women adorned themselves for the men. A man from the people of the mountain came upon them during their festival, saw the women, and went to his companions and informed them. So they moved toward the women, descended upon them, and immorality appeared among them. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾.

The most correct of the sayings in my view, regarding this, is that it should be said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, forbade the wives of the Prophet from displaying themselves as was the display of the first ignorance. It is permissible that this refers to what was between Adam and 'Isa, so the meaning would be: do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance that preceded Islam.

If someone says: Is there ignorance in Islam, so that it is said that by His words ﴿the first ignorance﴾ He meant that which preceded Islam? It is said: there are traits of ignorance within it.

As [reported]:
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾: he said: He says, that which was before Islam. He said: Is there ignorance in Islam? He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Darda', and he said to a man who was contending with him: "O son of so-and-so's mother," by which he was reproaching him in the time of ignorance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Darda', there is ignorance in you." He said: Is it ignorance of disbelief or of Islam? He said: "Rather, ignorance of disbelief." He said: I wished that I had begun my Islam that day. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Three of the deeds of the people of ignorance, people will not abandon them: slandering lineages, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing."
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Thawr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him: What do you think of the saying of Allah to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the first ignorance﴾? Was there not only one [ignorance]? Ibn Abbas said: And was there any first [ignorance] except that it has a last? 'Umar said: May God grant you understanding, O Ibn Abbas, how did you say that? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, was there any first [ignorance] except that it has a last? He said: Then bring evidence confirming what you say from the Book of Allah. He said: Yes: ﴿and strive in Allah with the striving due to Him; He has chosen you...﴾ [with the reading: "as you fought the first time"]. [The manuscript has this reading, and it may be a reading of Ibn Abbas.] 'Umar said: Who was commanded to fight? He said: Two tribes of Quraysh: Makhzum and Banu 'Abd Shams. 'Umar said: You have spoken the truth.

It is permissible that this refers to what was between Adam and Nuh. It is also permissible that it refers to what was between Idris and Nuh, so that the last ignorance is what was between 'Isa and Muhammad. When this is something that the apparent sense of the revelation allows, the correct position is to say regarding it as Allah said: that He forbade the display of the first ignorance.

* *

And His words: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾
meaning: and establish the obligatory prayer, and give the zakah obligatory upon you in your wealth. ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in what they command you and forbid you. ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾: meaning, Allah only intends to remove from you evil and indecency, O people of the household of Muhammad, and to purify you from the defilement that exists among the people of disobedience to Allah, [with] purification.

Ahl al-ta'wil said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾: they are the people of the household whom Allah purified from evil and singled out with His mercy.
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾: he said, the impurity here is Satan, and other than that of impurity is shirk.

The exegetes differed regarding those meant by His words, ﴿O people of the household﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them.

Mention of those who said that:
* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Zaban al-'Anazi narrated to us, saying: Mandal narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: concerning me, 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), and Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her): ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾."
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariya, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: 'A'ishah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out one morning, wearing a black woolen cloak with designs. Then al-Hasan came, so he brought him in with him, then said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾.
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pass by Fatimah's house for six months, every time he went out to prayer, saying: "The prayer, O people of the household: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾."
* Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Hilal, meaning Ibn Miqlas, from Zubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was with me, along with 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. I made a broth of khazirah for them, so they ate and slept. He covered them with a cloak or a blanket, then said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification."
* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud informed me, from Abu al-Hamra', who said: I guarded Madinah for seven months during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ), when dawn broke, come to the door of 'Ali and Fatimah and say: "The prayer, the prayer," [and recited]: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾.
* 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, with his chain, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.
* 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Kulthum al-Muharibi, from Abu 'Ammar, who said: I was sitting with Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' when they mentioned 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and they reviled him. When they stood up, he said: Sit until I tell you about this one whom they reviled. I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn came to him, so he threw his cloak over them, then said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; O Allah, remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification." I said: O Messenger of Allah, and me? He said: "And you." He said: By Allah, it is indeed the most reliable of my deeds with me.
* 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to me, saying: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to me, who said: I heard Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' relate: I asked about 'Ali ibn Abi Talib at his house, and Fatimah said: He has gone to bring the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and I entered. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat on the bedding, seated Fatimah on his right, 'Ali on his left, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn in front of him. He wrapped them with his garment and said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾. "O Allah, these are my family; O Allah, my family have more right." Wathilah said: I said from the side of the house: And I, O Messenger of Allah, am I of your family? He said: "And you are of my family." Wathilah said: Indeed, it is among the most hopeful of what I hope for.
* Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from Umm Salamah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and covered them with a Khaybari cloak, and said: "O Allah, these are the people of my household; O Allah, remove the impurity from them and purify them with [complete] purification." Umm Salamah said: Am I not among them? He said: "You are on the path to good."

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zurbi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umm Salamah, who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a cooking pot in which she had prepared 'asida (a porridge), and she placed it on a tray before him. He said: "Where is your cousin and your two sons?" She said: "In the house." He said: "Call them." So she went to Ali and said: "Answer the Prophet (ﷺ), you and your two sons." Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached out to a cloak that was on the sleeping place (al-minamah), spread it out, and seated them on it. Then he took the four corners of the cloak in his left hand and gathered it over their heads, and with his right hand he pointed toward his Lord, and said: "These are the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt). So remove from them the impurity (al-rijs) and purify them with a thorough purification."

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that this verse was revealed in her house: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. She said: I was sitting at the door of the house, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I not from the People of the House?" He said: "You are on the path of good; you are one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: In the house were the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them.

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Khalid ibn Mikhlad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn Hashim ibn 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas narrated to me, from 'Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, who said: Umm Salamah informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Ali and the two grandsons (al-Hasan and al-Husayn), then drew them under his garment, then cried out to Allah, and then said: "These are the People of my House (Ahl Bayti)." Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me enter with them." He said: "You are indeed of my family (Ahli)."

Narrated to me by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Isfahani narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Ubayd al-Makki, from 'Ata', from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the house of Umm Salamah: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. So he called al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah and seated them before him, and he called Ali and seated him behind him. Then he and they were covered with the cloak, and he said: "These are the People of my House. So remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification." Umm Salamah said: "I am with them in your place, and you are upon good." [[The phrase "I am with them in your place and you are upon good" is entirely the words of Umm Salamah, and it is parallel to the Prophet's (ﷺ) words to her in the narrations before this one: "You are on the path of good; you are one of the wives of the Prophet ..." etc. (See the nineteenth part of the manuscript no. 100 Tafsir at Dar al-Kutub, folio 60.)]]

Narrated to me by Muhammad ibn 'Umarah, who said: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muri narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a man from the people of Syria: "Did you not read in al-Ahzab: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾?" He said: "And are you they?" He said: "Yes."

Narrated to us by Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us, who said: I heard 'Amir ibn Sa'd, who said: Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when the revelation came down to him, and he took Ali, his two sons and Fatimah, and drew them under his garment, then said: "My Lord, these are my family and the People of my House."

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, in the presence of Umm Salamah, and she said: "It was concerning him that this was revealed: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾." Umm Salamah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to my house and said: "Do not permit anyone to enter." Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering upon her father. Then al-Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering upon his grandfather and his mother. Then al-Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered around the Prophet (ﷺ) on a rug, and the Prophet of Allah covered them with a cloak that he had on, then said: "These are the People of my House. So remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification." This verse was revealed when they had gathered on the rug. She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what about me?" She said: By Allah, he did not respond further, and he said: "You are upon good."

Others said: Rather, by this is meant the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh narrated to us, from 'Alqamah, who said: 'Ikrimah used to proclaim in the marketplace: ﴿Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾, and he said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The Exegesis of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted.﴾ (33:34)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the wives of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And remember the favor of Allah upon you, in that He placed you in houses in which the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited. So thank Allah for that, and praise Him for it." By His words ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah﴾ He means: remember what is read in your houses from the verses of the Book of Allah, and the wisdom. By wisdom he means what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the rulings of the religion of Allah that were not sent down as Qur'an; that is the Sunnah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾: "That is, the Sunnah." He said: "He bestows favor upon them through that."

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah is Subtle toward you, in that He placed you in the houses in which His verses and wisdom are recited, and Acquainted with you, in that He chose you as wives for His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 35:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember Him: Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [33:35].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, those who humble themselves before Allah in obedience, both men and women; those who affirm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in what he brought them from Allah; those who are devoutly obedient (qanitin) to Allah, both men and women, obeying Allah and obeying Him in what He commands and forbids them; those who are truthful to Allah in what they pledged to Him, both men and women; those who are patient for Allah in hardship and adversity, steadfast in His religion and in the time of peril, both men and women; those whose hearts are humbly submissive (khashi') to Allah, fearing Him and His punishment, both men and women; those who give charity (mutasaddiqin) and those who give charity, namely those who discharge the rights of Allah from their wealth, both men and women; those who fast the month of Ramadan, which Allah made obligatory for them to fast, both men and women; those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, and the women who guard theirs, except from their spouses if they are free women, or from those who own them if they are slave women; those who remember Allah with their hearts, their tongues and their limbs, both men and women. Thus Allah has prepared for them forgiveness for their sins and a great reward: meaning a great reward in the Hereafter for those deeds of theirs, and that is Paradise.

Those who held the same view as we have stated concerning this are the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Some women came to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Allah has mentioned you in the Qur'an, but we have not been mentioned at all. Is there anything in us that is mentioned?" So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾: that is, the obedient men and obedient women; ﴿and the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women﴾, that is, those who fear and the women who fear; ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness﴾ for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾ in Paradise.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and a great reward﴾: "Paradise." And regarding His words ﴿and the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾: "The obedient men and obedient women."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata, from Amir, who said: "The qanitat are the obedient women."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men are mentioned but we are not mentioned," so there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women﴾.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, that Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib told him that Umm Salamah said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are the men mentioned in everything and we are not mentioned?' So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ the verse."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sayyar ibn Mazahir al-Anazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah Yahya ibn Muhallab narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why does He mention the believing men and not the believing women?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ the verse.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, who said: Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "Why are women not mentioned alongside men in righteousness?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'ammar narrated to me, saying: Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah narrated to us, who said: I heard Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), say: "I said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'O Messenger of Allah, why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as the men are mentioned?'" She said: "Then one day at midday nothing alarmed me except his call from the pulpit while I was combing my hair. So I tied my hair and went out to one of the rooms of theirs, and I placed my ear near the palm-frond (jarid) [of the partition]. He was saying on the pulpit: 'O people, indeed Allah says in His Book: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women...﴾' up to His words ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾."

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ (33:36)

Says the Exalted One: It is not for a believer in Allah and His Messenger, nor for a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a decree concerning them, that they should choose from their affair other than what has been decreed for them, and oppose the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger and their decree, thereby disobeying them. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger in what they have commanded or forbidden, ﴿has certainly strayed into clear error﴾. He says: he has certainly deviated from the straight path and taken a course other than the way of guidance and rectitude.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed her hand for his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah, and she refused to let him marry her.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter...﴾ to the end of the verse. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to propose on behalf of his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah, and entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah and proposed to her. She said: "I am not going to marry him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then marry him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me consider my own affair." While they were talking, Allah revealed this verse to His Messenger: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ to His words ﴿clear error﴾. She said: "Have you then approved him for me as a husband, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then I will not disobey the Messenger of Allah; I have given myself to him in marriage."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿that they should have any choice about their affair﴾: he said: Zaynab bint Jahsh and her aversion to marrying Zayd ibn Harithah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to do so.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter that they should have any choice about their affair﴾: he said: this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was the daughter of the paternal aunt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to her and she agreed, thinking that he was proposing for himself. When she learned that he was proposing her for Zayd ibn Harithah, she refused and objected, so Allah revealed ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter that they should have any choice about their affair﴾. He said: after that she submitted to him and agreed.

Abu 'Ubayd al-Wassafi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr related to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Ibn Abi 'Amrah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed Zaynab bint Jahsh for Zayd ibn Harithah, and she scorned him and said: "I am better than him in lineage." She was a woman with a sharp temper; so Allah revealed ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter...﴾ the whole verse.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, because she had given herself to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah.

Those who said so:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter...﴾ to the end of the verse: it was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, and she was among the first women to emigrate. She gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah. She and her brother were displeased and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he married us to his slave." He said: then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter that they should have any choice about their affair...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: and a more general command came: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾. He said: that one is specific, and this is a consensus (ijma').

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 37:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember, O Muhammad] when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you so that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.﴾ (33:37)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet ﷺ, in reproach from Allah to him: ﴿And﴾ remember, O Muhammad, ﴿when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor﴾ with guidance, ﴿and you bestowed favor upon﴾ with manumission, meaning Zayd ibn Harithah, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿"Keep your wife and fear Allah."﴾ That is because Zaynab bint Jahsh, it is mentioned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw her and she pleased him, and she was under the guardianship of his freedman. Then dislike of her was cast into the heart of Zayd, since Allah knew what had occurred in the heart of His Prophet, what had occurred. So he intended to separate from her, and Zayd mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ﴿"Keep your wife,"﴾ while he ﷺ loved that she would have been separated from him so that he could marry her, ﴿"and fear Allah"﴾ and be mindful of the duty owed to you regarding your wife. ﴿"And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose"﴾ means: you concealed within yourself love for his separating from her so that you might marry her if he parted from her, and Allah is to disclose what you conceal within yourself of that. ﴿"And you feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him."﴾ He, exalted is His remembrance, says: you feared that the people would say, "He commanded a man to divorce his wife and married her after he divorced her," while Allah has more right that you fear Him than the people.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor﴾: he is Zayd, whom Allah favored with Islam, ﴿and you bestowed favor upon﴾: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed him. ﴿"Keep your wife and fear Allah," and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾. He said: He was concealing within himself the wish that he would divorce her. Al-Hasan said: No verse was revealed to him that was harder on him than this: His saying ﴿and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾. Had the Prophet of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this. (﴿And you feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾) He said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ feared the saying of the people.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The Prophet ﷺ had married Zayd ibn Harithah to Zaynab bint Jahsh, the daughter of his paternal aunt. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day seeking him, and at the door there was a curtain of hair. The wind lifted the curtain and it was uncovered, and she was in her chamber with her head uncovered, so her beauty fell into the heart of the Prophet ﷺ. When that occurred, she became hateful to the other. He came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I want to separate from my companion." He said: "What is that? Has something about her made you doubt?" He said: "No, by Allah, nothing about her has made me doubt, O Messenger of Allah, and I have seen nothing but good." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Keep your wife and fear Allah." That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾: you concealed within yourself that if he separated from her you would marry her.

- Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Hamzah, who said: This verse ﴿and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾ was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh.

- Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Ali ibn Husayn, who said: Allah, blessed and exalted, had informed His Prophet ﷺ that Zaynab would be among his wives. When Zayd came to him complaining about her, he said: "Fear Allah and keep your wife." Allah said: ﴿and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾.

- Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, from A'ishah, who said: Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of what was revealed to him of the Book of Allah, he would have concealed ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So when Zayd ibn Harithah had no longer any need from Zaynab, and that is the *watar* (need), and from it is the saying of the poet:

He bade me farewell before I could bid him farewell, when he had fulfilled from our youth its *watar*.

﴿We married her to you﴾ means: We married Zaynab to you after Zayd had divorced her and she was separated from him. ﴿So that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾ meaning: in marrying the women of those whom they adopted, who are not their sons nor their offspring, in correctness, if they divorce them and they are separated from them. ﴿When they have no longer any need for them﴾ means: when they have fulfilled their needs and desires from them, and parted from them, and the women became lawful to others, and that was not a handing over of them to him. ﴿And ever is the command of Allah accomplished﴾ means: and what Allah decreed of decree was accomplished, that is, it was certainly done. He means by this that Allah's decree concerning Zaynab, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would marry her, was past and accomplished.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿so that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them﴾: meaning, when they divorce them, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted Zayd ibn Harithah.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her...﴾ to His saying ﴿And ever is the command of Allah accomplished﴾: if that was from him not descending to you, then that is the saying of Allah: ﴿And the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Irfan, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who said: Aishah and Zaynab boasted, and Zaynab said: "I am the one whose marriage was revealed."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Zaynab, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed I take pride over you in three things, of which none of your wives takes pride: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; Allah married you to me from the heavens; and the emissary was Jibril, peace be upon him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. That is the way of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a destiny decreed.﴾ (33:38)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "There is no blame upon the Prophet" means: there is no sin upon him in what Allah has made lawful for him, namely marrying the wife of the one whom he had adopted after the latter divorced her.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾: meaning, what Allah has made lawful for him.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿That is the way of Allah with those who passed on before﴾:

He says: Allah, exalted is He, would not hold His Prophet to account for what He had made lawful for him, just as He did not hold those messengers who passed away before him to account for what He had made lawful for them. It was not for His Prophet to fear the people concerning what He had commanded him or made lawful for him. The phrase ﴿the way of Allah﴾ is in the accusative on the meaning of "a truth from Allah," as if He had said: "We did that as a practice from Us."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And the command of Allah is a destiny decreed﴾:

He says: the command of Allah is a decree that has been decided.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And the command of Allah is a destiny decreed﴾: Allah's knowledge was with Him before He created all things. He resolved in His knowledge to create a creation, to command them and forbid them, and to make a reward for the people of His obedience and a punishment for the people of disobedience. When that command was resolved upon, He decreed it; when He decreed it, He wrote it and kept it hidden with Him, so He named it the Unseen and the Mother of the Book. He created creatures according to that Book: their provisions, their terms, their deeds, and what would befall them of ease and hardship, as written in the Book that they would be afflicted by it. He recited: ﴿Those will receive their portion from the Book, until when Our messengers come to them to take their souls﴾ [7:37]. When that portion is exhausted, the command of Allah, which He resolved and decreed when He decreed it, becomes a decree; nothing happens except what is in that [Book] and in that decree. He resolved a matter, then decreed it, then created upon it, and so He said: "The command of Allah" that has passed and been completed, and He created creatures upon it, "a destiny decreed." He willed a matter by which His command and decree would take effect, and He willed a matter that He is pleased with from His servants in obedience. As for what He willed of their obedience, He was pleased with it for them; and as for what He willed, He wished to carry out His command, His arrangement and His decree concerning it. He recited: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾ [7:179]. He willed that these would be among the people of the Fire, and He willed that their deeds would be the deeds of the people of the Fire. So He said: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every nation its deeds﴾ [6:108], and He said: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to bring about their destruction and to confuse them regarding their religion﴾ [6:137]. These are the deeds of the people of the Fire. ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have done it﴾ [6:137]. He said: ﴿And thus We made for every prophet an enemy, devils...﴾ [6:112] to His saying ﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it﴾ [6:112]. And he recited: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths...﴾ [6:109] to ﴿...everything in front of them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾ [6:111], that they would believe in that. He said: they removed Him from the name by which He is named, saying: He is the doer of what He wills; so they claimed that He did not will [their guidance].

The commentary on the verse: "Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner." (Q. 33:39)

Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: The way (sunnah) of Allah concerning those who passed away before Muhammad among the messengers is that they convey the messages of Allah to those to whom they were sent, and they fear Allah in not conveying that to them, and they fear none but Allah, for it is Him they dread if they fall short in conveying the message of Allah to those to whom they were sent. He says to His Prophet Muhammad: So be among those messengers who have this description, and do not fear anyone but Allah, for Allah protects you from all of His creation, and none of His creation can protect you from Him if He intends harm for you. The phrase "those who convey" (alladhina yuballighuna risalati Allah) in His words is in the genitive (khufida) as a substitution (radd) for "those" (alladhina) in His words "the way of Allah concerning those who passed away" (sunnata Allah fi alladhina khalaw).

* *

And His words "And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner" (wa kafa billahi hasiban).

Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And sufficient for you, O Muhammad, is Allah as a Guardian over the deeds of His creation and as one who reckons with them for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 40:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Muhammad was not, O people, the father of Zayd ibn Harithah, nor the father of any one of your men [[Perhaps: i.e., he did not beget... etc.]] whom Muhammad did not beget, so that marrying his wife after he had divorced her would be forbidden to him. Rather, he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, who sealed prophethood and stamped it, so that it will not be opened to anyone after him until the Hour arises. And Allah is, of all things, of your deeds, your speech, and other things, Knowing, nothing hidden from Him.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Zayd; he was not his son, though by my life, he did have sons: he is the father of al-Qasim, Ibrahim, al-Tayyib and al-Mutahhar. ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾, meaning: the last of them. ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Qadim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Nusayr ibn Dhu'luq, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, regarding His words ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Harithah. The accusative in "Messenger of Allah ﷺ" is in the sense of repeating "was" (kana): "was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ"; the nominative is in the sense of a new statement: "but he is the Messenger of Allah." The reading in the accusative is the one we hold to be correct.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿and the Seal of the Prophets﴾. The readers of the major cities, apart from al-Hasan and 'Asim, recited it with a kasra on the ta' of "khatam al-nabiyyin" (khatim), meaning: he sealed the prophets (the one who ended the prophets). It is reported that in the reading of 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is ﴿But a Prophet who sealed the prophets﴾, and this is evidence for the soundness of the reading of whoever recites it with a kasra on the ta', meaning: he is the one who sealed the prophets, may blessings and peace be upon him and them. Al-Hasan and 'Asim, as is reported, recited ﴿khatam al-nabiyyin﴾ with a fatha on the ta' (khatam), meaning: he is the last of the prophets, as in His words ﴿its seal is musk﴾, meaning: its last part is musk, for whoever recites it thus.

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance (41) and exalt Him morning and evening (42). It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And ever is He, toward the believers, Merciful (43). Their greeting, the Day they meet Him, will be, 'Peace,' and He has prepared for them a noble reward (44)."

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, remember Allah with your hearts, your tongues, and your limbs, with much remembrance, so that your bodies are never free of His remembrance in any state within your capacity to do so. "And exalt Him morning and evening" means: pray to Him at dawn, the Subh prayer, and in the afternoon, the 'Asr prayer.

* *

As for His saying, "It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Your Lord, whom you remember with much remembrance and glorify morning and evening when you do so, is the One who shows mercy to you, and His angels pray for you. It has also been said that the meaning of His saying "sends blessings upon you, and His angels" is: He spreads a good remembrance of you among the servants of Allah.

* *

As for His saying, "that He may bring you out from darkness into light":

It means: the angels of Allah pray for you, so Allah brings you out from misguidance to guidance, and from disbelief to faith.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have held views similar to what we have stated concerning its interpretation.

Mention of those who said so:

- Ali narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "Remember Allah with much remembrance": He does not prescribe an obligation for His servants without setting for it a known limit, then excusing those bound by it in circumstances of excuse, except for remembrance. For Allah has not set a limit for it at which it ends, nor has He excused anyone from abandoning it except one overcome in his reason. He said, "Remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides," by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in sickness and in health, in secret and in public, and in every state. And He said, "And exalt Him morning and evening." So when you do that, He and His angels will send blessings upon you. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels."

- Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying "And exalt Him morning and evening": the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.

* *

As for His saying, "that He may bring you out from darkness into light":

That is: from misguidances to guidance.

- Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out from darkness into light": "From misguidance to guidance." He said: "Misguidance is the darkness, and light is guidance."

* *

As for His saying, "And ever is He, toward the believers, Merciful":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He is merciful toward the believers in Him and His Messenger, such that He would not punish them while they are obedient to Him and follow His command. "Their greeting, the Day they meet Him, will be, 'Peace.'" He, may His praise be exalted, says: The greeting of these believers on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise is "Peace," meaning that some of them say to others: "Security for us and for you, by our entry into this abode from Allah, that He will never punish us with the Fire."

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying "Their greeting, the Day they meet Him, will be, 'Peace'": "The greeting of the people of Paradise is peace."

* *

As for His saying, "And He has prepared for them a noble reward":

He says: He has prepared for these believers a reward for them for their obedience to Him in the world, a noble one, and that is Paradise.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding "And He has prepared for them a noble reward": that is, Paradise.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 49:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period to count concerning them. So provide for them and release them with a gracious release.﴾ (33:49)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them﴾, meaning: before you have had intercourse with them. ﴿Then there is for you no waiting period to count concerning them﴾, meaning: no reckoning of menstrual periods or months that you could count against them. ﴿So provide for them﴾, meaning: give them something they may enjoy, whether goods or a sum of wealth.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and release them with a gracious release﴾:

It means: let them go their way in a manner that is known and fair, and that is the gracious release.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to us, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period to count concerning them﴾: this concerns a man who marries a woman and then divorces her before he has touched her. If he divorces her once, she is separated from him, and there is no waiting period upon her; she may marry whom she wishes. Then he recited ﴿So provide for them and release them with a gracious release﴾, meaning: if he had named a dowry for her, then she has only half of it; and if he had not named a dowry for her, he provides for her according to his means and his ease, and that is the gracious release.

Some of them said: the provision (mut'ah) in this place is abrogated (mansukhah) by His saying ﴿then half of what you have prescribed﴾.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women...﴾ up to His saying ﴿with a gracious release﴾, he said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: then this phrase, the provision, was abrogated by ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them while you had already appointed for them an obligation, then half of what you have appointed﴾.

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, they both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatadah relate from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, he said: This verse was abrogated, ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period to count concerning them﴾, he said: this verse was abrogated by the one in al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 50:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her — exclusively for you, apart from the believers. We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there will be no discomfort for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (33:50)

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾, meaning: those whom you have married with a stated dowry (ṣadāq).

As related:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾: he said, "Their dowries (ṣadaqat)."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾: "Every woman to whom he gave a dowry, Allah had made lawful to him."

* It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments … ﴾ up to His words ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾: "Whatever of this designation [of wives] he wished, much or little."

* * *

As for His words ﴿their bridal payments and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you﴾:

He says: And We made lawful to you your female slaves (imāʾ) whom you took captive, so that you possessed them by captivity, and who became yours through the conquest that Allah granted you from the fay’. ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾: So Allah made lawful to him ﷺ from the daughters of his paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles and maternal aunts, those who emigrated with him from among them, but not those who did not emigrate with him.

As related:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Umm Hani’, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him with my excuse. Then Allah revealed ﴿Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments … ﴾ up to His words ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. She said: "So I was not made lawful to him, because I did not emigrate with him; I was among the Freed ones (al-Tulaqa’)."

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Masʿud it is ﴿and the daughters of your maternal aunts and those who emigrated with you﴾ with a waw. Although this is so in his reading, it may have the same meaning as our reading without the waw, because the Arabs sometimes insert a waw before the description of someone already mentioned, as the poet said:

*Indeed Rushayd and the son of Marwan would not have done so until the matter came to its outcome.*

[The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra’ (Maʿani al-Quran). He said regarding the verse ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allah, i.e., Ibn Masʿud, ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts and those who emigrated with you﴾. The emigrants may be the daughters of the maternal uncle and aunt even if there is a waw, so he said "wa-allati" (and those who), and the Arabs describe with and without waw, as the poet said: "Indeed Rushayd and the son of Marwan…" etc. You say in speech: "If you visit a brother of yours and your near paternal cousin," and if you say "and the near one to you," it would be correct. The author (al-Tabari) transmitted it from al-Farra’ and clarified it by his words about the verse: Rushayd is the son of Marwan.]

Rushayd is the son of Marwan. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim used to interpret the reading of Ibn Masʿud to mean that they are a category other than the daughters of his maternal aunts, namely every emigrant woman who emigrated with the Prophet (ﷺ).

The report from him concerning this:

* It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding the reading of Ibn Masʿud, ﴿and those who emigrated with you﴾, meaning by this: everything that emigrated with him which is not from the daughters of the paternal uncle and paternal aunt, nor from the daughters of the maternal uncle and maternal aunt.

* * *

As for His words ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾:

He says: And We made lawful to him a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet without a dowry.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾: "Without a dowry. He did not do this [for others], and it was made lawful to him exclusively, apart from the believers."

It has been mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah it is ﴿and a believing woman who gave herself to the Prophet﴾ without "in" (if), and its meaning and the meaning of our reading, which has "in," is one, as when a speaker says: "There is no harm in a man having intercourse with a female slave if he owns her," and "a female slave he owns."

* * *

As for His words ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾:

He says: If the Prophet wishes to marry her, it is lawful for him to marry her, when she has given herself to him without a dowry, ﴿exclusively for you﴾, He says: It is not lawful for anyone from your community to approach a woman who has given herself to him; rather this is for you alone, O Muhammad, exclusively reserved for you, apart from the rest of your community.

As related:
