* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾: "It is not permitted for a woman to give herself to a man without the permission of a guardian and without a dowry, except for the Prophet; it was exclusive to him apart from the people." They claim it was revealed concerning Maymunah bint al-Harith, that she was the one who gave herself to the Prophet.

* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives … ﴾ up to His words ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾: "Every woman to whom he gave a dowry, Allah had made lawful to him, until these women gave themselves to him, and so they were made lawful to him apart from the believers, without a dowry, exclusively for you apart from the believers, except a woman who has a husband."

* Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Salih ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Shaʿbi about a woman who gave herself to a man. He said: "It is not lawful for him; she was only for the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿if she gives herself﴾. The majority of the readers of the cities recited ﴿in wahabat﴾ with a kasra on the alif, in the conditional form, meaning: "if she gives." It is mentioned that al-Hasan al-Basri recited ﴿an wahabat﴾ with a fatha on the alif, meaning: "And We made lawful to him a believing woman that he may marry her, because she gave herself to him."

The recitation that I do not permit opposing is the kasra on the alif, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

As for His words ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾, it is not for the believers. It is mentioned that before this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he was permitted to marry whichever women he wished, and Allah restricted him to these, so he did not exceed them, and restricted the rest of his community to two, three, or four.

Those who said this:

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Miʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, that the women whom Allah made lawful to the Prophet were these whom Allah mentioned: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments … ﴾ up to His words ﴿concerning their wives﴾, and Allah only made lawful to the believers two, three, or four.

* And Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives … ﴾ to the end of the verse: "Allah forbade to him whatever else of women; previously he could marry whichever women he wished, and this was not forbidden to him. His wives were greatly distressed that he could marry whomever he loved. When Allah revealed: 'Indeed I have forbidden you from people other than what I have related to you,' this pleased his wives."

The scholars differed concerning the believing woman who gave herself to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whether there was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) such a woman. Some of them said: No woman was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except by a contract of marriage or by ownership of the right hand; as for by gift, none of them was with him.

Those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah ibn al-Azhar, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "No woman who gave herself was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾: "That she gives."

As for those who said that there was with him such women, some of them said: Maymunah bint al-Harith. Others said: Umm Sharik. Others said: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said regarding ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾: "She is Maymunah bint al-Harith."

Others said: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm al-Masakin, a woman of the Ansar.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik wrote to the people of Madinah asking them, and ʿAli wrote back to him. Shuʿbah said: "I believe it was ʿAli ibn Husayn." He said: Abан ibn Taghlib informed me of it, from al-Hakam, that it was ʿAli ibn al-Husayn who wrote to him: "She is a woman of the Asad called Umm Sharik, who gave herself to the Prophet."

* He said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi al-Safar narrated to me, from al-Shaʿbi, that she was a woman of the Ansar who gave herself to the Prophet, and she was among those who were deferred.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Saʿid narrated to me, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas of the Banu Sulaym, that she was among those who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

He said: Saʿid ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to me, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: "We used to speak of Umm Sharik as having given herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and she was a righteous woman."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives﴾:

He says, may His remembrance be exalted: We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon the believers concerning their wives when they wish to marry them, of what We did not make obligatory upon you, and what We singled them out with regarding the ruling on that apart from you. That is: We made obligatory upon them that it is not lawful for them to contract a marriage with a free Muslim woman except with a guardian from the agnatic line and upright witnesses, and that it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said this:

* ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh narrated to me, saying: Mutahhar narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Mattar, from Qatadah, regarding Allah's words ﴿We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives﴾: "Among what Allah made obligatory upon them is that there is no marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses."

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives﴾: "It refers to the four."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives﴾: "Among what Allah made obligatory upon them is that a woman is not to be married except with a guardian and a dowry in the presence of two upright witnesses, and it is not lawful for them to have from women more than four, and what their right hands possess."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and what their right hands possess﴾:

He says, may His remembrance be exalted: We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon the believers concerning their wives, because it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them, and what their right hands possess, for all of them, if they are believing or People of the Book, are lawful to them through captivity, concubinage, and other causes of ownership.

* * *

As for His words ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾:

He says, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed We have made lawful to you, O Muhammad, your wives mentioned in this verse, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her, so that there will be no sin or constriction upon you in marrying any of those whom We have permitted you to marry from the named categories in this verse. And Allah is Forgiving toward you and toward the people of faith through you, Merciful toward you and toward them, that He would punish them for a past sin of theirs after their repentance from it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 51:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them, and take to you whom you will. And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled and they not grieve, and that they all be pleased with what you have given them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing.﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them, and take to you whom you will﴾. Some of them said: by His saying "turji" (defer) is meant "tu'akhkhir" (delay), and by "tu'wi" (take to you) is meant "tadimm" (gather in).

Those who said this:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾, he said: "means: you delay."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾, he said: "You set aside without divorce whom you will of your wives." ﴿And take to you whom you will﴾, he said: "You bring them back to you."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾, he said: "Allah made it lawful for him to leave whom he wills of them and to come to whom he wills of them without a turn, whereas the Prophet of Allah used to divide (his nights equally)."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, regarding ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾, he said: "When they feared that he would divorce them, they said: 'O Prophet of Allah, give us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish.' Among those he deferred were Sawda bint Zam'a, Juwayriya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba and Maymuna, and among those he took to himself were A'isha, Umm Salama, Hafsa and Zaynab."

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾: "He did with the division among the wives whatever he wished; Allah made that lawful for him."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾: "Among those he took to himself, upon him blessings and peace, were A'isha, Hafsa, Zaynab and Umm Salama; so his division for them was from his own self, apart from his division (by rota). Among those he deferred were Sawda, Juwayriya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba and Maymuna; he would divide for them as he willed. He had intended to part from them, so they said to him: 'Divide for us from yourself whatever you wish, and let us remain in our state.'"

Others said: the meaning of that is: you divorce and release whom you will of your wives, and keep whom you will of them without divorce.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾ — "the Mothers of the Believers" — ﴿and take to you whom you will﴾ — "meaning: the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." And "deferment" means: whomever you wish, you release her from them; and "taking in" means: whomever you love, you keep of them.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: you leave off marrying whom you will, and marry whom you will of the women of your community.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said regarding His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾: "When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to a woman, no man was permitted to propose to her until he married her or left her."

It has also been said: this was granted by Allah to His Prophet only when some of them became jealous of the Prophet (ﷺ) and some of them sought more maintenance than what he gave them. So Allah commanded him to give them the choice between the worldly abode and the Hereafter, and to release whoever chose the life of this world and its adornment, and to keep whoever chose Allah and His Messenger. When they chose Allah and His Messenger, it was said to them: "Be now content with what Allah and His Messenger give you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) may divide for you or not divide, may divide for some of you and not for others, may favour some of you over others in maintenance or not, may treat you equally or not; for the matter in that is up to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you have no part in it." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it is mentioned, despite what Allah had granted him in this regard, used to treat them equally in division, except for a woman among them whom he wished to divorce and who was content to forgo her turn.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to divorce his wives, they said to him: "Impose upon us from yourself and your wealth whatever you wish." So Allah commanded him, and he took four to himself and deferred five.

* Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ubayda ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from A'isha, that she said: "Is a woman not ashamed to give herself to a man, until Allah revealed: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾?" I said: "Indeed your Lord hastens to fulfil your desire."

* Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr, meaning al-Abdi, related to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from A'isha, that she used to reproach the women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she said: "Is a woman not ashamed to offer herself without a dowry?" Then it was revealed, or Allah revealed: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will. And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside﴾. I said: "Indeed I see that your Lord hastens to fulfil your desire."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will...﴾ the verse. He said: "His wives had been jealous of the Prophet (ﷺ), so he forsook them for a month. Then the granting of choice from Allah concerning them was revealed to him, and he recited until He reached ﴿and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former Jahiliyya﴾. He gave them the choice between choosing that he release them and let them go, or that they remain, if they desired Allah and His Messenger, on the condition that they are Mothers of the Believers and never marry; and on the condition that he takes to himself whomever of them he wills — those who had given themselves to him — until he himself raises his head toward her; and that he defers whomever he wills until he himself raises his head toward her; and that whoever he seeks from among those with him, and whoever he sets aside, there is no blame upon him. That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled and they not grieve, and they be pleased when they know that it is from my decree concerning them, the preferring of some of them over others." ﴿That is more suitable that they﴾ be pleased. He said: ﴿And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside﴾: whoever he sought, he reached; and whoever he set aside, he did not reach. So he gave them the choice between being pleased with this or parting from them, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, except for one bedouin woman who left. He, upon him blessings of Allah, was upon this, and Allah had stipulated this condition for him; he continued to act justly among them until he met Allah."

The most correct of these interpretations in my view is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, granted His Prophet the right to defer whom he wills of the women whom He made lawful to him, and to take to himself whom he wills of them. This is because He did not restrict the meaning of deferment and taking in to the married wives who were in his marriage at the time this verse was revealed, to the exclusion of others of them whose taking in or deferment might later arise.

Given that, the meaning of the speech is: you delay whom you will of those who have given themselves to you and whose marriage to you I have made lawful, so you do not accept or marry her; or of those who are in your marriage, so you do not approach her. And you take to you whom you will of those who have given themselves to you, or whom you wish of the women whose marriage I have made lawful to you, so you accept or marry her; and of those who are in your marriage, so you lie with her if you wish, and leave her if you wish, without a turn.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some said: the meaning of that is: whoever of your wives you married and lay with, and of those not yet married you set aside from intercourse, there is no blame upon you.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾, he said: "All of this is regarding his wives; if he wills, he comes to whom he wills of them, and there is no blame upon him."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside﴾: "Whoever he sought, he reached; and whoever he set aside, he did not reach."

Others said: the meaning of that is: whomever you have substituted from those you deferred, releasing them from your wives, or from those who died among them whom I made lawful to you, there is no blame upon you.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And whomever you seek out of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled and they not grieve and they all be pleased with what you have given them﴾: "He means by that: the women whom Allah made lawful to him from the daughters of his paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles and maternal aunts, ﴿who emigrated with you﴾." He says: if one of your wives who are with you dies, or you release her, then I have made lawful to you to substitute from those whom I made lawful to you in place of whoever of your wives with you has died or whom you have released from them, and it is not proper for you to add anything to the number of your wives who are with you.

The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of whoever said: the meaning of that is: whomever you seek to lie with of your wives, from among those who are set aside from that, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, due to the indication of His saying ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled﴾ confirming this. For there is no sense in their eyes being cooled if he, peace be upon him, substituted in place of one who died or was divorced among them, unless it is meant that this is more suitable for the eyes of the married ones among them to be cooled; and that is far from what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates.

* *

As for His saying ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled and they not grieve﴾

It means: this which I have granted you, O Muhammad, of my permission for you to defer whom you will of the women whose deferment I granted you, and to take to you whom you will of them, and my lifting from you the burden in seeking to lie with whomever you seek among your wives, and your setting aside whomever you set aside of them, is closer for your wives that their eyes be cooled by it and that they not grieve, and that they be pleased with what you have given them all, of preference in whom you prefer in division, or of maintenance and favouring whom you favour of them over others of your wives, when they know that it is from my good pleasure for you in that, and my permission for you in it, and a release from me, not from you.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be cooled and they not grieve and they all be pleased with what you have given them﴾: "When they know that this came from Allah as a concession, it was better for their souls and less grieving for them."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying "that," the like of it.

As for the correct reading of His saying ﴿with what you have given them, all of them﴾ with the nominative (raf'), the reading with the accusative (nasb) is not permissible in our view, because "kulluhunna" is not an adjective (na't) of the pronoun in His saying ﴿ataytahunna﴾. Rather the meaning of the speech is: "and they all be pleased," so it is an emphasis of the mention of the women within "yardayna." If it were made an emphasis of the pronoun in "ataytahunna," it would have no meaning; and the reading with the accusative is therefore impermissible, as well as because the consensus of the authoritative readers has condemned whoever reads it so.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾

It means: Allah knows what is in the hearts of men of inclination toward some of the women they have over others, through desire and love. It says: therefore, O Muhammad, He lifted from you the burden in what He lifted from you of seeking whomever you sought of them, and setting aside whomever you set aside, as a bounty from Him upon you and an honour. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾: that is, Allah is possessed of knowledge of the deeds of His servants and of all other things. ﴿Forbearing﴾: that is, possessed of forbearance toward His servants, that He does not hasten to punish the people of sins among them; rather He is forbearing and patient with them, so that whoever among them repents may repent, and whoever among them turns back from his sins may turn back.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 52:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever, over all things, an Watcher.﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His words, exalted is He, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: it is not lawful for you to take women after your wives whom you gave the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this] ...﴾ to ﴿Watcher﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was forbidden to marry, after his first wives, anything.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this] ...﴾ to His words ﴿except those whom your right hand possesses﴾, he said: When he gave them the choice and they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, He restricted it to them; so He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives﴾, and they were the nine who chose Allah and His Messenger.

Others said: the meaning of that is only: it is not lawful for you to take women beyond those whom We made lawful for you by Our saying, ﴿O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their due compensation ...﴾ to His words ﴿and the women of the believers, if a woman gives herself to the Prophet﴾. The proponents of this view appear to direct the speech to the meaning: it is not lawful for you of women except those whom We have made lawful for you.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ziyad, who said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Was it permitted for the Prophet (ﷺ), if his wives died, to marry?" He said: "It was not forbidden to him." So I recited to him this verse, ﴿O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives﴾. He said: He made lawful for him a kind of women, and forbade him what was other than them: He made lawful for him every woman whose due compensation he gives, and what his right hand possesses of what Allah granted him as spoils, and his paternal uncle's daughters, and his paternal aunts' daughters, and his maternal uncle's daughters, and his maternal aunts' daughters, and every woman who gives herself to him, if he wishes to marry her, sincerely for him apart from the believers.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ziyad al-Ansari, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Do you see, if the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) died, would it have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "And what would forbid that to him?" I said: "His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾." He said: "Allah only made lawful for him a kind of women."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa narrated to me, from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Do you see, if the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) had died, would it not have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "What would prevent him from that?" And perhaps Dawud said: "What would forbid that to him?" I said: "His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾." He said: "Allah only made lawful for him a kind of women," and then He said, ﴿O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ to His words ﴿if a woman gives herself to the Prophet﴾, and then it was said to him, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from one he named, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾, he said: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman nor a foreign woman, and he would marry afterwards from the women of Tihamah, and whomever he wished from the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and maternal uncles and aunts, if he wished, three hundred.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾: these are the ones whom Allah named, except ﴿your paternal uncles' daughters ...﴾, the verse.

It has been reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾, meaning after the naming, he says: It is not lawful for you any woman except a paternal uncle's daughter, or a paternal aunt's daughter, or a maternal uncle's daughter, or a maternal aunt's daughter, or a woman who gave herself to you, of those who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and the women who emigrated with you﴾, meaning by that: everything that emigrated with him, which is not from the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts, nor from the daughters of maternal uncles and aunts.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: it is not lawful for you [to take] women other than the Muslim women; as for Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾: not a Jewess, nor a Christian, nor an unbeliever.

The view most worthy of being correct in my opinion is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: it is not lawful for you [to take] women after those whom I have made lawful for you by My saying, ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their due compensation ...﴾ to His words ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾.

I only said that this is more worthy as the interpretation of the verse, because His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women﴾ come after His words ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾, and it is not permissible to say: "We have made these lawful for you," and yet they are not lawful for you except by one of the two verses abrogating the other, or by the time of revealing one of the two verses being after the other. Since that is so, and there is no indication or proof that the ruling of one of the two verses abrogates the ruling of the other, nor that the revelation of one of them preceded the other, and their meanings were possible to be sound, it is not permissible to say that one of them abrogates the other. And since that is so, and the statement of the one who said, "the meaning is: it is not lawful after the Muslim women, a Jewess, nor a Christian, nor an unbeliever," has no intelligible meaning, since His words ﴿after [this]﴾ mean only: after those named and mentioned earlier in the verse before this verse; and in the verse in which mention was made of those named as made lawful to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), there was no mention of the permission of all Muslim women, rather there was mention of his wives, and what his right hand possesses of what Allah granted him, and his paternal uncles' daughters and paternal aunts' daughters, and his maternal uncles' daughters and maternal aunts' daughters who emigrated with him, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, so the unbelieving women are particularly singled out for prohibition. What we have said on this is correct, rather than the view of one who opposes our view.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited ﴿yahillu﴾ with the ya', meaning: no woman is lawful for you after this. Some reciters of Basra recited ﴿la tahillu lakan-nisa'﴾ with the ta', directing it to the fact that it is the act of the women, and "the women" is a plural for the many among them.

The more correct of the two readings in the matter is the reading of the one who recited it with the ya', for the reason mentioned to them, and for the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and the aberration of those who opposed them in that.

* *

His words ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: it is not lawful for you [to take] women after the Muslim women, neither a Jewess, nor a Christian, nor an unbeliever, nor to exchange the Muslim women for other unbelieving women.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾: nor to exchange the Muslim women for others among the Christians, Jews and polytheists, ﴿even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses﴾, he said: It is not lawful for you to marry from the polytheist women except those who were captured and whom your right hand possesses from among them.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: nor to exchange your wives who are under your care for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others.

Mention of those who said that:

It has been reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾: it is not proper for you to divorce any of your wives who does not please you, and that was not proper for him.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: nor to exchange your wives for others, by giving your wife to someone and taking his wife.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾: The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah used to exchange their wives; one would give his wife to this one and take his wife; so He said, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses﴾. There is no harm in exchanging your slave-girl for whatever you wish to exchange, but as for free women, no. He said: That was among their practices in the Jahiliyyah.

The view most correct in the matter is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: nor to divorce your wives and then substitute others for them as wives.

We only said that this is more correct because of what we have already explained earlier, that the saying of the one who said that the meaning of His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾ is: it is not lawful for you a Jewess or a Christian or an unbeliever, is a view with no basis.

Since that is so, then likewise His words ﴿nor to exchange them﴾ meaning "an unbeliever" has no meaning, since among the Muslim women there are those who have been forbidden to him by His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾ which we have shown earlier. As for what Ibn Zayd said on this too, it is a view with no meaning, because if it meant exchange, the recitation and the revelation would be: "nor to barter them for women" (wa la an tubadila bihinna min azwaj), or "wa la an tubaddala bihinna" with a damma on the ta'; but the consensually agreed recitation is: "wa la an tabaddala bihinna" with a fatha on the ta', meaning: nor to substitute them. Moreover, the practice Ibn Zayd mentioned from the Jahiliyyah is not known among any nation that we know of: that a man exchanges his free wife with another, so that it is said: that was among their practices, and so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the doing of its like.

If someone says: Was it not lawful for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to marry a woman in addition to his wives who were with him, so that the interpretation of His words ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ would be directed to what I have interpreted; or he says: where is the mention of his wives who were with him in this place, so that the pronoun in His words ﴿nor to exchange them﴾ refers to them, and he supposes that the pronoun in that refers to the women in His words ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾? It is said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was indeed permitted to marry whichever of the women Allah had made lawful for him, beyond his wives who were with him on the day this verse was revealed. He (ﷺ) was forbidden by this verse only to part from whoever was with him by divorce intended to substitute another in her place, due to the admiration of the beauty of the one substituted; for Allah had made them the mothers of the believers and gave them the choice between the life of this world and the Last Abode, and contentment with Allah and His Messenger, and they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode; so they were made forbidden to others by that, and he was prevented from parting from them by divorce. As for marrying others, it was not prohibited to him; rather Allah made that lawful for him, as is explained in His Book. And it has been narrated from 'A'ishah that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not pass away until Allah made lawful for him the women of the earth.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him, meaning: the women of the earth.

'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Hubari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him.

al-'Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Mu'alla narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until it was made lawful for him to marry from the women whatever he wished.

Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: I think 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr narrated to me, Abu Zayd said, and Abu 'Asim said once, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until Allah made women lawful for him. He said: Abu al-Zubayr said: I saw a man narrating to him from 'Ata'.

Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him.

If someone says: If the matter is as you have described, that Allah forbade His Prophet by this verse to divorce his wives whom He gave the choice and they chose him, then what is the meaning of the report narrated from him that he divorced Hafsah and then took her back, and that he intended to divorce Sawdah until she reconciled with him by leaving her turn to 'A'ishah? It is said: That was before the revelation of this verse.

The evidence for the correctness of what we have said, that this was before Allah forbade His Prophet to divorce them, is the report that 'Umar entered upon Hafsah, who was grieved when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withdrew from his wives; among what he said to her: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had divorced you, so I spoke to him and he took you back. By Allah, if he divorces you, or if he had divorced you, I would not speak to him about you." That was without doubt before the revelation of the verse of choice, because the verse of choice was revealed only after the period of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) oath of withdrawal from them had ended.

As for the proof that the matter of Sawdah was before the revelation of this verse, it is that Allah only commanded His Prophet to give his wives the choice between parting from him and remaining with him, contented with there being no division of turns for them, and that he would defer whom he wished of them, and shelter whom he wished of them, and prefer whom he wished of them over whom he wished; and for this reason He, mentioned and exalted, said to him: ﴿And whomever you seek from those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and they be pleased with what you have given them, all of them﴾. And it is impossible that the reconciliation between her and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took place on her leaving her turn to 'A'ishah in a situation where she had no day from him.

It is not permissible that this occurred from her except in a situation where she had a day from him which was a right owed to her that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had to fulfil, and that did not belong to them after the choice, as I have described before in this book of ours.

So the sense of the speech is: It is not lawful for you, O Muhammad, women after those whom I made lawful for you in the verse before, nor to divorce your wives whom Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode they chose, and substitute for them other wives, even if the beauty of whomever you wished to substitute for them pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. The "an" in His words ﴿an tabaddala bihinna﴾ is in the nominative case, because its meaning is: "It is not lawful for you women after, nor the substitution of your wives"; and "illa" in His words ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ is an exception from the women. The meaning of that is: It is not lawful for you women after those whom I made lawful for you, except what your right hand possesses of the maidservants; for you may possess maidservants of whatever kind of people you wish.

* *

His words ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, a Watcher﴾.

He says: And Allah is over everything, of what He made lawful for you and forbade you, and all other things, a Guardian, nothing of its knowledge escapes Him, and the preservation of all of that does not burden Him.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: (And Allah is over all things a Watcher): that is, a Guardian, according to al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 33, verse 53 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that would be an offense to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not [permissible] for you to offend the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.﴾ (33:53)

He, the Exalted, says to the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger, do not enter the houses of the Prophet of Allah unless you are invited to a meal that you are served, ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾, meaning: not awaiting its ripening and readiness. It is a verbal noun from their saying: qad anā hādhā al-shay' yaʾnī inan wa aniyan wa inā' (this thing has ripened), as al-Ḥuṭayʾah said:

*"I delayed the evening meal until Suhayl or al-Shiʿrā, and so my waiting lengthened."* [[The verse is by al-Ḥuṭayʾah (Lisan: anā). Āntu al-shay' means I postponed it, and its noun is al-anāʾ on the pattern fiʿāl with a fatḥa. He means he postponed his evening meal until the rising of Suhayl or the rising of al-Shiʿrā, so his waiting lengthened. He said: Abū Saʿīd (al-Aṣmaʿī) transmitted it as "wa-anaytu" with a doubled nūn. It is said: anaytu al-ṭaʿām fī al-nār, when I prolonged its stay over the fire. And anā al-shay' yaʾnī anyan wa ini wa anī: it became due and reached maturity. Abū ʿUbayda said in Majāz al-Qurʾān (ed. Jāmiʿa, p. 1197), "to a meal, without waiting for its preparation," meaning its ripening and readiness. It is said: anā laka yaʾnī anyan, meaning it has become due and reached you. *"Death has pressed its grip upon him by a day that has come due, and every pregnant one has her term."*]]

There is another dialect in which it is said: qad āna laka, meaning it has become clear to you, its time has come; and nāla laka, and anāla laka. From this is the saying of Ruʾbah ibn al-ʿAjjāj:

*"She stirred, and it befits me that I should be still: a dove that cooed a warbling coo."* [[The two verses are from rajaz, by the well-known rajaz poet Ruʾbah (his Dīwān, Leipzig ed., 1903, p. 87). In Lisan (nawl): as for nawl, you say nawluka an taf'al kadhā, meaning it is incumbent upon you to do such a thing. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: meaning your right is to do such a thing. Its origin is from taʾannul, as if he were saying: your reaching for such and such. Al-ʿAjjāj said: (hājat... etc.), meaning his right is to refrain. It is also said the rajaz is by Ruʾbah. The origin of nawl is the verbal noun of nālahu bi-khayr, yanwaluhu nawlan, nawlan, and nīlan. It is said anālahu bi-khayrin, inālatan.]]

Ahl al-ta'wīl (the scholars of interpretation) said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, he said: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan related to us, he said: Warqāʾ related to us, all together, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the words of God ﴿to a meal, without waiting for its preparation﴾, he said: watching for its cooking.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾, he means: not waiting for the food to be made.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazīd related to us, he said: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾, he said: not watching for its readiness.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, the like of it.

The accusative of ﴿ghayra﴾ in His saying ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾ is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the kāf and mīm in His saying ﴿unless permission is given to you﴾, because the kāf and mīm are definite while ghayr is indefinite, and it is an attribute of the kāf and mīm. Some grammarians of Basra used to say: it is not permissible to put ﴿ghayr﴾ in the genitive as modifying the food, unless you say "antum" (you). He said: Do you not see that if you said: "Abdullah showed me a woman hating her," there would only be the accusative, unless you say "mubghiḍan lahā huwa" (hating her, he). For if you apply its attribute to her without making explicit the pronoun that shows the attribute belongs to him, it would not be grammatical. If you said "this is a man with a woman, clinging to her" (mulāzimihā), it would be ungrammatical until you put it in the nominative, saying mulāzimuhā, or say mulāzimahā huwa and then put it in the genitive.

Some grammarians of Kufa used to say: if you made ﴿ghayr﴾ in His saying ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾ genitive, it would be correct, because before it is "al-ṭaʿām" (the food), which is indefinite, so their action is made to follow the food, since the mention of the food is returned to in "its preparation," as the Arabs say: "I saw Zayd with a woman, doing good to her" (muḥsinan ilayhā) and "muḥsinin ilayhā". Whoever says muḥsinan makes it an attribute of Zayd, and whoever puts it in the genitive is as if he said: "I saw him with the one to whom he does good." When the relative clause belongs to an indefinite, you follow it, even if it is a verb not belonging to the indefinite, as al-Aʿshā said:

*"So I said to him: this, bring it to us with a white she-camel led by its halter."* [[The verse is by al-Aʿshā of Banū Qays ibn Thaʿlabah (his Dīwān, Cairo ed., p. 69). The version in it is: "fa-qulnā lahu hādhihi hātihā, bi-admāʾa fī ḥabli muqtādihā." It differs from the author's version which he cited. The Dīwān version contains no evidence for the author. The poet praises, in the poem, Salāma Dhā Fānish of the kings of Yemen. In the introduction of the poem are verses on love and wine, and this verse is among them. His saying "this" refers to the wine which the cupbearer brought, and the poet bargains with him over its price, and the poet agreed to buy the wine he described, on condition that its price be his she-camel, the white one his servant leads by its halter. The adma in camels is whiteness with blackness of the eyes (Lisan). This is the explanation of the verse according to the Dīwān version. As for the author's version, he took the i'rab of (muqtādihā) in the genitive following admāʾ, because it is indefinite, though the leading is for his servant understood from context; it is an attribute running on something other than its owner, and he did not make explicit the pronoun of the adjective, so it must be said: muqtādihā anta, i.e. the owner of the wine, or say muqtādihā huwa: i.e. the servant leads it. But when the described noun is definite, as in His saying ﴿unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its preparation﴾, then the accusative of ghayr is permissible as a state from the pronoun in lakum, and the genitive is permissible according to the Kufans by following as an adjective, even if the pronoun is not made explicit with it. The author has explained the context fully, so no further discussion is needed.]]

So he made *al-muqtād* follow the i'rab of *bi-admāʾ*, because it is like your saying "bi-admāʾ tuqtaduhā" (with a white she-camel you lead), so he put it in the genitive because it is its relative clause. He said: it is recited "bi-admāʾi muqtādihā" with the genitive of admāʾ because it is annexed to al-muqtād, and he said: its meaning is: bring it through the hand of the one who leads it. He also recited:

*"And if a man sent gifts to you, though between him and you lie a desert of mirage and a wasteland of bayḍā, it is a right that you should respond to his call, and that you know the one who is helped is successful."* [[The two verses are by al-Aʿshā. Their citation was given earlier in the author's words for the same purpose as here (see 17:197). The point is in his saying "maḥqūqatun," for it is a predicate about "wa-in imraʾan." The predicate here is other than the subject, since the subject here is masculine and the predicate feminine. The grammarians differed on this. The Basrans said it should have said "maḥqūqatun anta" with the pronoun made explicit, because omitting it causes ambiguity in speech and it is not known whom the maḥqūqa refers to. As for the Kufans, they permitted in this case and similar ones, in predicate and attribute not agreeing with their subject, that the pronoun be expressed or not, contrary to what the Basrans said, and they cited the two verses of al-Aʿshā as evidence for a predicate not agreeing with what it refers to without an expressed pronoun. The Basrans explained that in the verse as expansion (ittisāʿ) and ellipsis. (See the question explained in full in al-Inṣāf fī Masāʾil al-Khilāf by Abū al-Barakāt ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Anbārī, Cairo ed., pp. 45–48, question no. 8.)]]

It is related from some Arabs by report that they recited:

*"Do you see, when I gave you all my affection, and it was not with me, if you refused, a refusal?
Are you, having submitted to death, dead? And is there any survival for submitting souls?"* [[These two verses I did not find in al-Farrāʾ's Maʿānī al-Qurʾān nor in Abū ʿUbayda's Majāz al-Qurʾān. The evidence in them is that his saying "fa-mayyit" is conjoined to his saying "a-muslimatī," and the conjoined here is other than the conjoined to in meaning. So the requirement would be that he say "fa-mayyitun anā," with the pronoun made explicit, according to the Basran school. But he did not make the pronoun explicit, and this agrees with the Kufan school, which says that making the pronoun explicit and not making it explicit are both permissible, and this is common in the speech of the Arabs.]]

He did not say "fa-mayyitun anā." Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say "yadaka bāsiṭuhā" (your hand is its extender), meaning "anta", and it is common in speech. He said: on this basis the genitive of *ghayr* is permissible.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to permit the genitive of *ghayr* in *ghayra nāẓirīna* in ordinary speech, but not in recitation, due to the verses we have cited. As for recitation, the genitive of *ghayr* is not permissible, but only the accusative, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is on its accusative.

* *

As for His saying ﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾:

It means: but when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invites you, then enter the house into which he has permitted you to enter. ﴿And when you have eaten, then disperse﴾: meaning, when you have eaten the food to which you were invited, then disperse, i.e., scatter and leave his house. ﴿Nor those who linger for conversation﴾: His saying ﴿nor those who linger for conversation﴾ is in the genitive position, conjoined to *nāẓirīna* (watching), as one says in speech: "You are neither silent nor speaking." It is also possible to say that *mustaʾnisīna* is in the accusative position, conjoined to the meaning of *nāẓirīna*, because its meaning is: unless permission is given to you for a meal, not watching for its preparation, so His saying ﴿nor those who linger﴾ would then be in the accusative. The Arabs do so when they separate the first and second: they sometimes return to the wording of the first and sometimes to its meaning. Al-Farrāʾ mentioned that Abū al-Qamqām recited to him:

*"Do you truly, in all time, not be the one who sees Rāmah, nor an intelligent person, except that you are led as a camel in a caravan? Nor one who ascends among the ascenders to Munʿaj, nor one who descends, as long as I live, to the hill of Shaṭīb."* [[The two verses are among al-Farrāʾ's citations in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān (Jāmiʿa microfilm, p. 258), and his version is more sound than the author's version. Rāmah, ʿĀqil and Munʿaj (in the author's version) and Manbij (in al-Farrāʾ's version) are place names in the Arabian Peninsula, except Manbij, which is in Syria, near Aleppo. The two verses are among those that Abū al-Qamqām recited to al-Farrāʾ. The evidence is in his saying "wa-lā muṣʿidin" in the genitive; it is conjoined to "rāʾī," and the conjoined-to is in the accusative, while the conjoined is in the genitive by the presumption of the extra bāʾ in the predicate of *laysa*, which is the first conjoined-to. As if he said: "You are not a seer, nor an ascender." Al-Farrāʾ cited the two verses in explaining the i'rab of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿nor those who linger﴾, for he considered it conjoined to *nāẓirīna ināhu* in the genitive, or in the accusative following *ghayr*. He said: if you made *al-mustaʾnisīna* in the accusative position, you would suppose it follows *ghayr*, since you have put speech between them. Thus. And so every meaning that admits two aspects, then if you separate the two with speech, the latter may be inflected differently from the first. Of that is your saying: "You are not one who does good to those who harmed him, nor one who is gracious."]]

So *muṣʿid* is conjoined, given that *rāʾī* has the governing preposition bāʾ, since speech intervened between it and *muṣʿid* just as speech intervened between them.

The meaning of His saying ﴿nor those who linger for conversation﴾ is: nor those who converse after you have finished eating the food, seeking companionship from one another through it.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, he said: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan related to us, he said: Warqāʾ related to us, all together, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿nor those who linger for conversation﴾, after you have eaten.

The people of knowledge differed about the occasion on which this verse was revealed. Some of them said: it was revealed on account of a people who ate at the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) feast on the wedding of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, then sat conversing in the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a need concerning his family, but shyness prevented him from ordering them to leave his house.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿImrān ibn Mūsā al-Qazzāz related to me, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb related to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and she sent a summoner to the food, so I summoned. The people came, ate and went out, then another group came, ate and went out. I said: O Prophet of Allah, I have invited until I do not find anyone to invite. He said: "Lift up your food." Zaynab was sitting in a corner of the house, and she had been given a camel, and three men remained conversing in the house. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out heading toward ʿĀʾishah's chamber, and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house." They said: "And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah, how did you find your family?" He went around the chambers of his wives, and they said the same as ʿĀʾishah said. The Prophet (ﷺ) returned, and behold, the three were still conversing in the house. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely shy, so he went out heading toward ʿĀʾishah's chamber. I do not know whether I informed him, or someone informed him, that the group had gone out. He returned until he placed his foot on the threshold inside the house, with the other outside it, when the curtain was lowered between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed.

⁕ Abū Muʿāwiyah Bishr ibn Duḥayah related to me, he said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked me about the veil, and I said: I am the most knowledgeable of people about it; it was revealed concerning Zaynab. The Prophet (ﷺ) held a wedding feast for her with dates and sawiq (a barley porridge), and then the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you...﴾ until His saying ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾.

⁕ Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Wahb related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: Yūnus informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Anas ibn Mālik informed me that he was ten years old when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, and I was the most knowledgeable of people about the matter of the veil when it was revealed concerning the building of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) marriage to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke with her as a bride, and he summoned the people, and they partook of the food until they went out, but a group remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prolonged their stay. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood and went out, and I went out with him so that they would leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked and I walked with him, until he reached the threshold of ʿĀʾishah's chamber, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) thought they had gone out, so he returned and I returned with him, until he entered upon Zaynab, and behold, they were sitting and had not stood up. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned and I returned with him, and behold, they had gone out. He struck a curtain between me and him, and the veil was revealed.

⁕ Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdiyy related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, who said: I invited the Muslims to the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) wedding feast on the morning he consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. He fed them bread and meat generously, then he returned as he used to do, and came to the chambers of his wives and greeted them, and they prayed for him. He returned to his house and I was with him. When we reached the door, behold, two men were conversing in a corner of the house. When he saw them he turned back. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) they turned away from his house, and they left hastily. I do not know whether I informed him or someone else did, but he returned to his house, and the curtain was lowered between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed.

⁕ Ibn Bashshār related to me, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdiyy related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If only you were screened from the Mothers of the Believers, for the righteous and the wicked enter upon you." So the verse of the veil was revealed.

⁕ al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Maʿrūf related to me, he said: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: I am the most knowledgeable of people about this verse, the verse of the veil: when Zaynab was presented to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he prepared food and invited the people. They came, entered, and Zaynab was in the house with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they began conversing, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept going out and coming back in while they remained seated. He said: So this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ until ﴿ask them from behind a screen﴾. He said: So the people stood up and the screen was set up.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 53 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Umar ibn Isma'il ibn Mujalid narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from Bayan, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummated his marriage with one of his wives. He sent me, and I invited the people to the food. When they had eaten and gone out, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, heading towards the house of Aisha, but he saw two men sitting, so he turned back. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission﴾.

⁕ Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Al-Mas'udi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Nahshal narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: Umar ordered the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to observe the hijab. Zaynab said: "O son of al-Khattab, you are indeed jealous of us, while revelation descends in our houses." So Allah revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to me, saying: Ashhal ibn Hatim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Amr ibn Sa'd, from Anas, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ, and he would pass by his wives. He was brought a newly-wed woman, then he came while there were people with her. He went off and attended to his need, and he delayed, and returned when they had left. He entered, and a curtain was lowered between me and him. I related this to Abu Talha, and he said: "If it is as you say, something will surely be revealed concerning this." And the verse of the hijab was revealed.

Others said: That occurred in the house of Umm Salama.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not remain seeking familiar conversation﴾. He said: This was in the house of Umm Salama. They ate, then they prolonged the conversation, and the Prophet ﷺ would enter and leave, being shy of them, while Allah is not shy of the truth.

⁕ He said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾: It has reached us that they were commanded to observe the hijab at that time.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, that was causing harm to the Prophet﴾:

He says: Your entering the houses of the Prophet without being given permission, and your sitting in them for familiar conversation after finishing the food to which you were invited, was causing harm to the Prophet, so that he was shy of you to expel you from them when you sat in them for conversation after finishing the food, or to prevent you from entering when you entered without permission, while disliking that from you. ﴿But Allah does not hesitate from the truth﴾ to make it clear to you; and even if your Prophet was shy and did not make clear to you his dislike of that, out of shyness towards you. ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾: He says: When you ask the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the women of the believers, who are not wives of yours, for something, ﴿then ask them from behind a screen﴾, meaning: from behind a partition between you and them, and do not enter upon their houses. ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Your asking them for something, when you ask them that from behind a screen, is purer for your hearts and their hearts from the afflictions of the eye that arise in them, which occur in the breasts of men concerning women, and in the breasts of women concerning men, and more fitting that Satan has no path over you and them.

It has been said: The reason Allah commanded the women to observe the hijab was only that a man was eating with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with Aisha also present, and her hand touched the man's hand, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eating and with him was some of his companions. The hand of one of them touched the hand of Aisha, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that; so the verse of the hijab was revealed.

It has been said: It was revealed on account of Umar's question to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives; so would you command them to veil?" He said: Then the verse of the hijab was revealed.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, with a similar report.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Aisha, who said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to go out at night when they relieved themselves, to al-Manasi', which is a wide open ground. Umar would say: "O Messenger of Allah, veil your wives," but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do so. Then Sawda bint Zam'a, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, went out, and she was a tall woman. Umar called out to her in his loudest voice: "We have recognised you, O Sawda," out of eagerness that the hijab be revealed. She said: So Allah revealed the hijab.

⁕ Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, who said: Sawda went out for her need after the hijab had been imposed upon us, and she was a woman who towered over women in height. Umar saw her and called out to her: "O Sawda, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look how you go out, or how you act!" She turned back and returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was having his supper. She informed him of what had happened and what he had said to her. In his hand was a bone [[al-'Irq, with a fatha and then a sukun: the bone from which most of the meat has been taken. One says: "araqtu al-'azm" and "i'taraqtahu" and "ta'arraqtahu": when you take the meat off the bone with your teeth (al-Nihaya of Ibn al-Athir).]], and revelation came to him, then it lifted from him, and the bone was still in his hand. He said: "Indeed Allah has permitted you to go out for your needs."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Umar ordered the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to observe the hijab. Zaynab said: "O son of al-Khattab, you are indeed jealous of us, while revelation descends in our houses?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾.

⁕ Abu Ayyub al-Nahrani Sulayman ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, saying: Ibn Harb narrated to me, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Aisha, that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to go out at night when they relieved themselves, to al-Manasi', which is a wide open ground. Umar ibn al-Khattab would say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Veil your wives," but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do so. Then Sawda bint Zam'a, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, went out one night after the evening meal, and she was a tall woman. Umar called out to her in his loudest voice: "We have recognised you, O Sawda," out of eagerness that the hijab be revealed. Aisha said: So Allah revealed the hijab. Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses...﴾ the verse.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It is not fitting for you, and it is not proper for you, to harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾. He says: It is not fitting for you to marry his wives after him, ever, because they are your mothers, and it is not lawful for a man to marry his mother.

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a man who used to enter before the hijab, and who said: "If Muhammad dies, I will surely marry one of his wives," naming her. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning that: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾: "It would often reach the Prophet ﷺ that a man would say: 'If the Prophet ﷺ dies, I will marry so-and-so after him.' So that was causing harm to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah...﴾ the verse."

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that the Prophet ﷺ died while he had taken Qaylah bint al-Ash'ath, and then Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her after that. This was very grievous to Abu Bakr, so Umar said to him: "O Khalifah of the Messenger of Allah, she is not one of his wives; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give her the choice nor veil her, and he had cleared her of himself by the apostasy she committed along with her people." Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while he had taken the daughter of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and had not consummated with her; he mentioned a similar report.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾:

He says: Your harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and your marrying his wives after him is, in the sight of Allah, a great sin.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 54:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Whether you reveal anything or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ (33:54).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: If you make apparent with your tongues anything, O people, concerning the restriction upon women [i.e., their being watched or approached], or other than that of what He has forbidden you, or harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by saying, "I will marry his wife after his death," ﴿or conceal it﴾ means: or conceal that in your souls. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ means: indeed Allah, with regard to all of that and other than it, of your affairs and the affairs of others, is Knowing, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of that.

The commentary on the words of God, exalted is He: "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness" (33:55).

God, exalted is He, says: There is no hardship or sin upon the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning their fathers.

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning by which the blame was lifted from them concerning these persons. Some of them said: the blame was lifted from them concerning removing their outer garments (jalabib) in their presence.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers..." the whole verse, he said: that they remove the jilbab.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers," and whoever is mentioned with them, that they may be seen by them.

Others said: the blame was lifted from them concerning these persons in abandoning concealment (al-ihtijab).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "There is no blame upon them..." up to "Witness": He granted these persons a concession that they need not veil from them.

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: this is the lifting of the blame from them concerning these Muslim men, that they need not veil from them. This is because this verse follows the verse of the veil, and comes after the words of Allah: "And when you ask them for any article, ask them from behind a screen (hijab)." So His words "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers" are not an exception from the category of those who were commanded to ask them for goods from behind a screen, if they asked them for that; this is more fitting and more appropriate than that it be a predicate of a subject with a different meaning.

So the meaning of the speech is then: there is no sin upon the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Mothers of the Believers in permitting their fathers and abandoning the veil before them, nor in regard to their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers. By "their brothers and the sons of their brothers" is meant their brothers and the sons of their brothers. The plural form of "brothers" (ikhwan) came out in the manner of the plural of "fata" (youth) when it is pluralized as "fityan," so likewise the plural of "akh" (brother) when pluralized as "ikhwan." As for when it is pluralized as "ikhwa," that is analogous to the plural of "fata" when pluralized as "fitya." And nor the sons of their brothers. The paternal uncle (al-'amm) was not mentioned in this, according to what al-Sha'bi said, out of caution lest they describe them to his sons.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi and 'Ikrima, regarding His words: "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess." I said: What is the matter with the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle, that they were not mentioned? He said: Because they would describe them to their sons, and they disliked that she should remove her head-covering in front of her maternal uncle or paternal uncle.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrima and al-Sha'bi, similarly, except that he did not mention "would describe them."

* *

As for His words, "nor their women"

That is: there is no blame upon them either in not veiling before the women of the believers.

As follows:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, "nor their women," he said: the women of the believing free women; there is no blame upon them that they display that adornment. He said: This all concerns adornment only. He said: It is not permissible for a woman to look at any part of the nakedness (awrah) of a woman. He said: If a man looked at the thigh of a man, I would not see any harm in it. He said: "nor what their right hands possess": so it is not proper for her to uncover her earring before a man. He said: As for kohl, the ring, and dye, there is no harm in them. He said: The husband has a special status, and the fathers have status over the man. He said: And the others vary in rank. He said: All of this is encompassed by "what appears of adornment." He said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) would not veil before the slaves.

* *

As for His words, "nor what their right hands possess"

From among men and women. Others said: from among women.

* *

As for His words, "And fear Allah"

That is: fear Allah, O women, lest you transgress what Allah has set as limits for you, so that you display of your adornment what it is not permitted for you to display, or abandon the veil which Allah has commanded you to observe, except in what He has permitted you to leave; and adhere to His obedience. "Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness": God, exalted is He, says: Indeed Allah is a witness over what you do of your veiling and your abandoning the veil before those for whom He has permitted you to abandon it, and over your other affairs.
