That is: so fear Allah concerning yourselves, lest you meet Allah while He is a witness against you in disobedience to Him and opposition to His command and prohibition, and so you perish; for He is a witness over everything.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 56:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace.﴾ (56)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed Allah and His angels bless the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

As follows:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾: he said, "They bless the Prophet."

It is possible that it may be said that the meaning of this is: Allah has mercy upon the Prophet, and His angels invoke for him and seek forgiveness for him, because the word salah (ṣalāh, prayer/blessing) in the speech of the Arabs when it comes from other than Allah means only supplication (du'a'). We have explained this earlier in this book with its evidence, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it.

﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: O you who have believed, invoke blessings for the Prophet of Allah Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿And greet him with the greeting of peace﴾: he says, greet him with the greeting of Islam.

Reports have come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in accordance with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun related to us, from Anbasah, from Uthman ibn Mawhab, from Musa ibn Talhah, from his father, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I heard Allah say ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...﴾ the verse. So how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

* Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi related to me, saying: Ya'la ibn al-Ajlah related to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn Ujrah, who said: When ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace﴾ was revealed, I came to him and said: "The greeting of peace upon you we know, so how is the blessing upon you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: Abu Isra'il related to us, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, who said: He addressed us at Fars and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels...﴾ the verse. Someone informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: "It was revealed thus." We said, or they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we already know the greeting of peace upon you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ziyad, from Ibrahim regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels...﴾ the verse. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this greeting of peace we know, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your messenger, and his household, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

* Ya'qub al-Dawraqi related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ayyub related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: When ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace﴾ was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, the greeting of peace we know, so how is the blessing, since Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sins and what followed?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim. O Allah, bless Muhammad as You blessed the family of Ibrahim."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words (﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace﴾). He said: When this verse was revealed they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we already know the greeting of peace upon you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad as You blessed Ibrahim." And al-Hasan said: "O Allah, make Your blessings and Your mercy upon the family of Muhammad, as You made them upon Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment (57). And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin (58).﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾ means: indeed, those who harm their Lord by disobeying Him and committing what He has forbidden them. It has also been said that by this He meant the makers of images (ashab al-tasawir), because they aim to create the likeness of Allah's creation.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Qurashi related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Salama ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ikrimah, who said: "Those who harm Allah and His Messenger are the makers of images."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, he said: "Glory be to Allah! Some of the ignorant among the children of Adam have never ceased until they engaged in harming their Lord. As for their harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it was their criticism of him regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy, as it is mentioned."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, he said: "It was revealed concerning those who criticized the Prophet (ﷺ) when he took Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab."

* *

As for His words ﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾:

He, may He be exalted, says: Allah has removed them from His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them in the Hereafter a punishment that will humiliate them through their abiding in it forever.

As for His words ﴿And those who harm believing men﴾:

Mujahid used to interpret the meaning of ﴿yu'dhun (harm)﴾ as "they stand (yaqifun)" [i.e., they stop and confront them].

Mention of the transmission from him:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And those who harm﴾, he said: "They stand."

So the meaning of the statement, according to what Mujahid said, is: "And those who confront the believing men and believing women and disparage them, seeking to defame them."

﴿Without their having earned it﴾ means: without what they have done.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿without their having earned it﴾, he said: "They did."

He says: They have certainly borne falsehood, lies and a grave calumny. "Buhtan" means the most vile lie. ﴿And a manifest sin﴾ means: and a sin that makes clear to its hearer that it is a sin and a falsehood.

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment (57). And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin (58).﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾ means: indeed, those who harm their Lord by disobeying Him and committing what He has forbidden them. It has also been said that by this He meant the makers of images (ashab al-tasawir), because they aim to create the likeness of Allah's creation.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Qurashi related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Salama ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ikrimah, who said: "Those who harm Allah and His Messenger are the makers of images."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, he said: "Glory be to Allah! Some of the ignorant among the children of Adam have never ceased until they engaged in harming their Lord. As for their harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it was their criticism of him regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy, as it is mentioned."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, he said: "It was revealed concerning those who criticized the Prophet (ﷺ) when he took Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab."

The Exegesis of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (33:59)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: Do not imitate slave women in their clothing when they go out of their houses for their needs, uncovering their hair and their faces. Rather, let them draw their cloaks close around them, lest a wicked man who sees that they are free women approach them with harm in speech.

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the manner of the drawing close (al-idnaa') that God commanded them. Some of them said: It is that they cover their faces and their heads, so that nothing of them shows except one eye.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them﴾: God commanded the women of the believers, when they go out of their houses for a need, to cover their faces from above their heads with the cloaks, and to show one eye.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad, from Ubaydah regarding His saying (O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them). Ibn Awn said: He wore it (the cloak) among us. Muhammad said: And Ubaydah wore it among me. Ibn Awn said: He wrapped himself with his garment, covering his nose and his left eye, and exposing his right eye, and he drew his garment down from above until it was close to his eyebrow or upon the eyebrow.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubaydah about His saying ﴿tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them﴾. He said: So he gathered his garment, covering his head and his face, and he uncovered one of his eyes with his garment.

Others said: Rather, they were commanded to tighten their cloaks over their foreheads.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them ...﴾ up to His saying ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He said: The free woman used to wear the dress of the slave woman, so God commanded the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them. And the drawing close of the cloak: that she veil herself and tighten it upon her forehead.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id related to us from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers﴾: God obligated them, when they went out, to veil on the eyebrows (yuqnan 'ala al-hawajib). ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused﴾. The enslaved woman, when she passed by, they would harass her, so God forbade free women from imitating slave women.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿draw their cloaks close around them﴾: they wrap themselves so that it is known that they are free women, so that no wicked man approaches them with harm in speech or with suspicion.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Anbasah, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Salih, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah without a settled dwelling, and the women of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others, when night came, would go out to attend to their needs. And men would sit on the road for dalliance. So God revealed ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close around them﴾: they should veil themselves with the cloak until the slave woman is distinguished from the free woman.

* *

As for His saying ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused﴾:

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Their drawing their cloaks close upon themselves, when they draw them around them, is nearer and more apt that they be known by those who pass them, and that they be recognized as not being slave women, so that they are spared harm in speech that is disliked, or an approach with suspicion. ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving﴾ regarding what has passed from them of leaving off drawing their cloaks around them, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, that He would not punish them after their repentance for drawing the cloaks close around them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 60–61:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in al-Madinah do not desist, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except for a little. Cursed, wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a (thorough) killing﴾.

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: If the people of hypocrisy, who conceal disbelief and display faith, do not desist, ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning: doubt, from the desire for fornication and love of immorality.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Dinar narrated to us from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease do not desist﴾, he said: They are the fornicators.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, he said: the desire for fornication.

He narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih al-Tammar narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾, he said: the desire for fornication.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us from 'Anbasah, from one who narrated to him from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, he said: the fornicators.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease do not desist ...﴾ the verse, he said: These are a category of the hypocrites. ﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ are the people of fornication. He said: The people of fornication from among the people of hypocrisy are those who seek women and pursue fornication. And he recited: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾. He said: And the hypocrites are of ten categories in Bara'ah. He said: So those in whose hearts is a disease are a category of them, a disease concerning the matter of women.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the agitators in al-Madinah﴾:

He says: and the people of agitation in al-Madinah, with falsehood and lies.

Their agitation, as it has been mentioned, was like that which:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in al-Madinah do not desist ...﴾ the verse. Al-irjaf (agitation) is the lie which the people of hypocrisy spread, and they would say: "A host and a multitude have come to you." It has been related to us that the hypocrites wished to display what was in their hearts of hypocrisy, so God threatened them with this verse: ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease do not desist ...﴾ the verse. When God threatened them with this verse, they concealed that and kept it secret.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the agitators in al-Madinah﴾: they are also the people of hypocrisy who agitate against the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and against the believers.

* *

As for His saying ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾:

He says: We will surely empower you over them and urge you against them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me from 'Ali from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾, he said: We will surely empower you over them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾: that is, We will surely drive you against them and urge you against them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except for a little﴾:

He says: then We will surely banish them from your city, so they will not dwell with you therein except for a little while, a period and a term, until you expel them from it and We remove them from it.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except for a little﴾, that is, in al-Madinah.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Cursed, wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a (thorough) killing﴾:

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: expelled and banished, ﴿wherever they are found﴾, meaning: wherever they are met on earth, they will be seized and killed, for their disbelief in God, with a (thorough) killing.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Cursed﴾, in every state, ﴿wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a (thorough) killing﴾, if they display hypocrisy. The accusative of His saying ﴿Cursed﴾ is by way of reviling. It is also permissible that "a little" be an attribute of the cursed, so that His saying ﴿cursed﴾ is taken as referring back to "a little", and its meaning would be: then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except as few cursed ones who will be killed wherever they are reached.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 62:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will never find any change in the way of Allah﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before﴾ — these hypocrites who are in the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and those among the companions of these hypocrites, that if they openly show their hypocrisy, He will have them killed with killing and curse them with a great curse.

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before...﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: Thus is the way of Allah regarding them when they openly show hypocrisy.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿and you will never find any change in the way of Allah﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And you will never find, O Muhammad, any change (taghyir) in the way of Allah which He has established among His creation, so be certain that He will not change His way regarding these hypocrites.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah. And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near."﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:63]

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿They ask you,﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿about the Hour﴾ — when will it be established? Say to them: "Its knowledge is only ﴿with Allah﴾; none other than Him knows the time of its establishment." (﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾) That is, He says: And what would make you aware, O Muhammad, that the establishment of the Hour may be near at hand? Its time has drawn close, and the moment of its coming has approached.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 64–68:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire. They will abide therein forever, not finding any protector or helper.﴾

His Exalted Remembrance says: Indeed Allah has removed the disbelievers in Him far from every good and kept them distant from Him. ﴿And He has prepared for them a blazing Fire﴾ means: He has prepared for them in the Hereafter a fire that blazes and flares up, to burn them in it. ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾ means: they will remain in the blazing Fire forever, without end. ﴿They will not find any protector﴾ who will take charge of them and rescue them from the Fire into which Allah has cast them. ﴿Nor any helper﴾ who will aid them and deliver them from the punishment of Allah inflicted upon them.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿On the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger."﴾

His Exalted Remembrance says: These disbelievers will not find any protector or helper on the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, from state to state. ﴿They will say﴾ — and this is their condition in the Fire — ﴿"Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah"﴾ in the world, ﴿and obeyed the Messenger in what he brought us from Him of His commands and prohibitions, so that we would have been with the people of Paradise in Paradise." Oh what a regret and remorse! How great and how immense it is.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ ﴿"Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse."﴾

His Exalted Remembrance says: The disbelievers will say on the Day of Resurrection in Hell: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders in error and our elders in polytheism." ﴿And they led us astray from the way﴾ means: they diverted us from the path of truth and the road of guidance and faith in You, and from acknowledging Your oneness and sincerely obeying You in the world. ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment﴾ means: punish them with a punishment twice ours, the punishment with which You are punishing us. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾ means: disgrace them with a great disgrace.

And the people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah﴾ (69).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the companions of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger, do not harm the Messenger of Allah with a saying he dislikes from you, nor with a deed he does not love from you, and do not be like those who harmed Moses, the Prophet of Allah, by slandering him with a defect, falsely and baselessly. ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said﴾, of the lies and falsehood in it, by the proof He manifested of their lying. ﴿And he was honorable in the sight of Allah﴾ means: Moses was, in the sight of Allah, one whose intercession was accepted in what he asked, a person of standing and rank with Him because of his obedience to Him.

Then the interpreters differed about the harm with which Moses was harmed, which Allah mentions in this place. Some of them said: they accused him of being a *adar* (one with a swollen scrotum, hernia), and a report to this effect has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the report related from him and of those who said this:

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya told us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾, he said: His people said to him: "You are an adar." He went out one day to bathe, and he placed his garments on a rock, and the rock ran off with his garments, and he went after it naked until it reached the assemblies of the Children of Israel. They saw him, and he was not an adar. That is the meaning of His words ﴿So Allah cleared him of what they said﴾.

Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ikrima, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ): concerning ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾, he said: They said, "He is an adar." He said: Moses went to bathe, and he placed his garments on a stone, and the stone passed by with his garments, and Moses followed it from behind, and said: "My garments, O stone! My garments, O stone!" Then it passed by an assembly of the Children of Israel, and they saw him; so Allah cleared him of what they said, ﴿and he was honorable in the sight of Allah﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses ...﴾ up to ﴿honorable﴾: he said: Their harm to Moses was that they said, "By Allah, what prevents Moses from putting his garments down with us except that he is an adar." This harmed Moses. Then one day, while he was bathing with his garment upon a rock, when Moses finished washing and went to his garment to take it, the rock set off running with his garment, and he set off running after it until it passed by an assembly of the Children of Israel while he was seeking it. When they saw Moses, peace be upon him, stripped with no garment on him, they said: "By Allah, we see no fault in Moses, and he is indeed innocent of what we used to say about him." So Allah said, ﴿So Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah﴾.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses ...﴾ the verse: Moses was a man who was extremely protective of his private parts and his garments. They used to say: "Nothing makes him do that except a defect in his private parts which he dislikes to be seen." One day he stood to bathe in the open desert and placed his garments on a rock, and the rock ran off with his garments. He came seeking it naked until he was seen by them, naked, and they saw him innocent of what they said, and he was honorable with Allah. He said: "The *wajih* (honorable) in the speech of the Arabs is the beloved, the accepted."

Others said: rather, they described him as being *abras* (leprous).

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ya'qub told us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: The Children of Israel said that Moses was an adar, and a group said: he is abras, from the intensity of his concealment. He used to come every day to a spring, bathe, and place his garments on a rock beside it. The rock ran off with his garments until it reached an assembly of the Children of Israel. Moses came seeking it, and when they saw him naked, with nothing of what they had said on him, he put on his garments, then turned to the rock and struck it with his staff, and the staff left a mark on the rock.

Bahr ibn Habib ibn Arabi told us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubada told us, saying: Awf told us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayra, concerning this verse (﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said ...﴾), the verse: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a man who was bashful and very concealing; hardly any of his skin could be seen out of modesty. The Children of Israel harmed him and said: 'He conceals himself this much only because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a hernia, or some affliction.' Allah wished to clear him of what they said. One day Moses was alone, so he placed his garments on a stone and bathed. When he finished washing, he went to his garment to take it, but the stone ran off with his garment. Moses took a staff and pursued the stone, saying: 'My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone!' until he reached a company of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, like the best of people in form, and Allah cleared him of what they said. The stone stopped, took his garment and he put it on, and he began striking the stone with it. By Allah, there are indeed marks on the stone from the traces of his striking it, three or four or five times."

Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a bashful, concealing man," and then he mentioned something similar.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan related from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, but the Prophet of Allah Moses was bashful, so he would cover himself when he bathed. They slandered him concerning his nakedness. One day, while the Prophet of Allah was bathing, he placed his garments on a rock, and the rock ran off, and the Prophet of Allah followed it, striking it with his staff: 'My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone!' until it reached, or stood in the middle of, a company of the Children of Israel. The rock stopped, the Prophet of Allah took his garments, and they looked at the best of people in form and most upright in manliness. The chiefs said: 'May Allah destroy the liars of the Children of Israel.' That was the innocence with which Allah cleared him."

Others said: rather, their harm to him was their claim against him that he had killed his brother Aaron.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me, saying: Abbad told us, saying: Sufyan ibn Habib told us, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning the words of Allah ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses ...﴾ the verse, he said: Moses and Aaron ascended the mountain, and Aaron died. The Children of Israel said: "You killed him, and he was more beloved to us than you and gentler to us than you." So they harmed him with this. Allah commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by him over the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. So Allah cleared him of that. They took him and buried him, and no one from Allah's creation looked upon his grave except the vulture; so Allah made it deaf and mute.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that one should say: the Children of Israel harmed the Prophet of Allah with some of what he disliked to be harmed with, and Allah cleared him of what they harmed him with. It is permissible that their saying was that he was abras, and it is permissible that their claim against him was that he had killed his brother Aaron, and it is permissible that all of that was the case, since all of it has been mentioned as things with which they harmed him. No saying on this is more accurate than what Allah said: that they harmed Moses, and Allah cleared him of what they said.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan). He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.﴾

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: "O you who have believed" means: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, "fear Allah," meaning: beware of disobeying Him, so that you thereby deserve His punishment.

* *

And His saying ﴿and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan)﴾

He means: say concerning the Messenger of Allah and the believers a word that is correct and not deviating, a truth that is not false.

As related:

* Al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Waraqa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan)﴾: he said, "sadadan" (rightness).

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: 'Anbasa narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, regarding ﴿and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan)﴾: he said, "sidqan" (truthfulness).

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan)﴾, meaning: "'adlan" (justly). Qatada said: "It refers to his speech and to all his actions, and al-sadid is truthfulness."

* Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrima, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadidan)﴾: "Say: There is no god but Allah."

* *

And His saying ﴿He will amend for you your deeds﴾

He, Exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers: fear Allah and speak the rightful speech, and He will guide you to righteous deeds, so He will amend your deeds ﴿and forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: and He will pardon you for your sins, so He will not punish you for them. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, by acting on what He has commanded him and refraining from what He has forbidden him, and speaking the rightful speech, ﴿has certainly attained a great attainment﴾, meaning: he has gained the great honour from Allah.

And His saying ﴿He will amend for you your deeds﴾

He, Exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers: fear Allah and speak the rightful speech, and He will guide you to righteous deeds, so He will amend your deeds ﴿and forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: and He will pardon you for your sins, so He will not punish you for them. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, by acting on what He has commanded him and refraining from what He has forbidden him, and speaking the rightful speech, ﴿has certainly attained a great attainment﴾, meaning: he has gained the great honour from Allah.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 33, Verse 72:**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of the meaning) of His words, ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.﴾

The people of *ta'wil* (interpreters of the Qur'an, that is, exegesis or *tafsir*) differed concerning the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is that God offered His obedience and His obligations to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, on the condition that if they did well they would be rewarded and recompensed, and if they neglected them they would be punished. So they refused to bear it, out of fear that they would not fulfil what was incumbent upon them. Adam bore it, ﴿indeed, he was a wrongdoer﴾ to himself, ﴿ignorant﴾ of that which was in his own interest.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾. He said: "The trust" is the obligations which God imposed upon the servants.

• He said: Hushaym related to us from al-Awwam, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it﴾. He said: "The trust" is the obligations which God imposed upon His servants.

• He said: Hushaym related to us, saying: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab and Juwaybir [[In the original: Jubayr. It will come in the same hadith that it is Juwaybir.]] both informed us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust...﴾ up to His words ﴿ignorant﴾. He said: "The trust" is the obligations. Juwaybir said in his narration: When it was offered to Adam, he said: "O Lord, and what is the trust?" It was said: "If you fulfil it you will be recompensed, and if you neglect it you will be punished." He said: "O Lord, I have borne it with what it contains." He said: So he did not remain in the Garden except for the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset, until he committed disobedience and was expelled from it.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas that he said concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust﴾: "It was offered to Adam, and he was told: 'Take it with what it contains. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you.' He said: 'I have accepted.' So there was only the time between the afternoon and the night of that day until he committed the sin."

• Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾: "If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them. So they disliked that and were apprehensive, not out of disobedience, but out of glorifying the religion of God, that they should not bear it. Then it was offered to Adam, and he accepted it with what it contains," and this is His words ﴿and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, deceived by the command of God.

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust﴾: "The obedience was offered to them before it was offered to Adam, but they could not bear it. So He said to Adam: 'O Adam, I offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, but they could not bear it. Will you take it with what it contains?' He said: 'O Lord, and what is in it?' He said: 'If you do well you will be rewarded, and if you do evil you will be punished.' So Adam took it and bore it, and that is His words ﴿and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from a man, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾. He said: "Adam. It was said to him: 'Take it with its due.' He said: 'And what is its due?' It was said: 'If you do well you will be rewarded, and if you do evil you will be punished.' So he did not remain between noon and the afternoon before he was expelled from it."

• It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾: "They could not bear it. So He said: 'O Adam, will you take it with what it contains?' Adam said: 'And what is in it, O Lord?' He said: 'If you do well you will be rewarded, and if you do evil you will be punished.' He said: 'I have borne it.' Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: 'I have entrusted it to you.' So Adam did not remain except for the time between the first prayer and the afternoon prayer, until Iblis, may Allah curse him, expelled him from the Garden." And "the trust" is the obedience.

• Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Isa ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Musa ibn Abi Habib, from al-Hakam ibn Amr, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the trust and fidelity descended upon the son of Adam along with the prophets, and they were sent with it. Among them were the Messenger of Allah, and among them a prophet, and among them a prophet and messenger. The Qur'an descended, and it is the speech of Allah, and the Arabic and the non-Arabic descended, so they knew the matter of the Qur'an and knew the matter of the Sunnah with their tongues. Allah did not leave anything of His command, of what they do and what they avoid, which constitutes proofs against them, except that He made it clear to them. There is no people of a language but that they recognise good from evil. Then the trust is the first thing to be lifted, and its trace remains in the roots of people's hearts. Then fidelity, covenant and obligations are lifted, and the books remain. So there is a scholar who acts, and an ignorant one who knows it and denies it, until it reaches me and my community. None perishes before Allah except the one who perishes, and none is heedless of it except the one who abandons it. Beware, O people, and beware of the whisperer who withdraws. Indeed He will test you, which of you is best in deed."

• Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi related to us, saying: al-Awwam al-Attar related to us, saying: Qatadah and Aban ibn Abi Ayyash related to us, from Khulayd al-Asri, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with five things, with faith, will enter the Garden: whoever preserves the five prayers, with their ablutions, bowings, prostrations and their appointed times, and gives the zakat from his wealth willingly." And he used to say: "By Allah, none does that except a believer." "And fasts Ramadan, and performs the pilgrimage to the House if he is able to do so, and fulfils the trust." They said: "O Abu al-Darda', and what is the trust?" He said: "The ritual washing from major impurity, for Allah did not entrust the son of Adam with anything of his religion other than that."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "Among the trust is that a woman was entrusted with her private part."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾: "Indeed Allah offered it to them, that the religion be made obligatory upon them, and that He make for them reward and punishment, and entrust them with the religion. They said: 'No, we are subjected to Your command. We do not desire reward or punishment.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And Allah offered it to Adam, and he said: 'Between my ear and my shoulder.'" Ibn Zayd said: Allah said to him: "Since you have borne this, I will help you. I will make a screen for your sight, so that if you fear you may look at what is not lawful for you, then lower its screen. I will make a gate and a lock for your tongue, so that when you fear, you close it. And I will make a garment for your private part, so you do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾: "He means by it: the religion, the obligations and the limits. ﴿But they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾. It was said to them: 'Will you bear it and fulfil its due?' They said: 'We cannot bear that.' ﴿And man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾. It was said to him: 'Will you bear it?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Will you fulfil its due?' He said: 'Yes.' Allah said: 'Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant of its due.'"

Others said: Rather, by "the trust" in this place is meant the trusts of people.

Mention of those who said this:

• Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, from Shurayk, from al-A'mash, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Martyrdom in the way of Allah expiates all sins, or he said: expiates everything except the trust. The owner of the trust will be brought and it will be said to him: 'Return your trust.' He will say: 'O Lord, the world has gone!' three times. Then it will be said: 'Take him to the abyss.' He will be taken to it, and he will plunge into it until he reaches its bottom, where he will find it in its former state. He will carry it and place it on his shoulder, and ascend with it to the edge of Hell, until when he sees that he has come out, it slips from him, and he falls after it for ever and ever." They said: "The trust is in prayer, the trust is in fasting, and the trust is in speech, and the greatest of that is deposits." I met al-Bara' and said: "Do you not hear what your brother Abd Allah says?" He said: "He has spoken the truth."

Shurayk said: Ayyash al-Amiri narrated to me, from Zadhan, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a similar manner, but he did not mention "the trust in prayer and in everything."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, who said: "Indeed Allah offered the trust to the lowest heaven, and it refused, then to the one next to it, until He finished with them, then the earths, then the mountains. Then He offered it to Adam, and he said: 'Yes, between my ear and my shoulder.' Three things I command you with, for they are a help to you: I have made for you a tongue between two jaws, so restrain it from everything I have forbidden you. I have made for you a private part and covered it, so do not uncover it for what I have forbidden you. [[The third is omitted; and in al-Durr: "I have made for you a sight, and made for you two eyelids, so shut them against everything I have forbidden you, and made for you your tongue..." etc.]]"

Others said: Rather, that refers to Adam's entrusting his son Qabil with his family and offspring, and Qabil's betrayal of his father in killing his brother.

Mention of those who said this:

• Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him. He would marry the boy of one birth to the girl of the other birth, and the girl of one birth to the boy of the other birth, until two were born to him, called Qabil and Habil. Qabil was a farmer, and Habil was a herder. Qabil was the elder, and he had a sister more beautiful than Habil's sister. Habil asked to marry Qabil's sister, but he refused and said: 'She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I am more entitled to marry her.' His father ordered him to marry her to Habil, but he refused. They both offered a sacrifice to Allah, to see which of them was more entitled to the girl. Adam was at that time absent from them, in Mecca, looking at it. Allah said to Adam: 'O Adam, do you know that I have a House on earth?' He said: 'No, O Allah.' He said: 'I have a House in Mecca, so go to it.' Adam said to the heaven: 'Guard my son with the trust,' and it refused. He said to the earth, and it refused. He said to the mountains, and they refused. He said to Qabil, and he said: 'Yes. Go and return, and you will find your family as will please you.' When Adam set out, they offered their sacrifice. Qabil would boast over him, saying: 'I am more entitled to her than you: she is my sister, I am older than you, and I am the guardian of my father.' When they offered, Habil offered a fat young camel, and Qabil offered a bundle of ears of grain. He found in it a great ear, rubbed it and ate it. Fire descended and consumed Habil's offering and left Qabil's. He was angry and said: 'I will surely kill you, so that you will not marry my sister.' Habil said: ﴿Indeed Allah accepts only from the righteous. If you extend your hand against me to kill me, I shall not extend my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds...﴾ up to His words ﴿so his soul permitted him the killing of his brother﴾. He sought him to kill him, and the boy escaped from him into the mountain tops. One day he came to him while he was grazing his sheep on a mountain, and he was asleep. He raised a rock and crushed his head with it, and he died. He left him in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God sent two brother ravens, which fought, and one killed the other. He dug for it, then covered it with earth. When he saw that, he said: ﴿Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and bury my brother's corpse?﴾. That is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Then Allah sent a raven scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse﴾. Adam returned and found that his son had killed his brother. That is when He says ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains...﴾ to the end of the verse."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is what was said by those who said that by "the trust" in this place is meant all the meanings of trusts in the religion and the trusts of people. This is because God did not restrict His words ﴿We offered the trust﴾ to some of the meanings of trusts, as we have described.

The people of *ta'wil* gave the same interpretation to the meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ as we have stated.

Mention of those who said this:

• Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾. He means Qabil, when he bore Adam's trust and did not guard his family for him.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from a man, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words ﴿And man bore it﴾: "Adam. ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾": "A wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of what he took on, between himself and his Lord."

• Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾: "He was deceived by the command of Allah."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾: "A wrongdoer to her, meaning the trust, ignorant of its due."

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and the believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful" (33:73).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And man bore the trust, so that Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women, among them, those who show that they perform the obligations of Allah, believing in them, while they conceal disbelief in them; and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who associate others with Allah in their worship, taking gods and idols. "And Allah turns in forgiveness to the believing men and the believing women" means He brings them back to His obedience and to the performance of the trusts He has obligated upon them, until they fulfill them. "And Allah is ever Forgiving" toward the sins of the believing men and women, by covering them and by abandoning punishment for them. "Merciful" means that He will not punish them for them after they have repented of them.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Anbari narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from al-Hasan, that he used to recite this verse: "Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains..." until he reached "so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women," and he would say: "The two who betrayed it are the two who wronged it: the hypocrite and the polytheist."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women": "These are the two who betrayed it." "And that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and the believing women": "These are the two who discharged it." "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

The end of Surat al-Ahzab, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
